items.title: Harshal Patel set to join Gujarat Titans
items.summary: New Delhi: Sunrisers Hyderabad are set to trade seam bowler Harshal Patel to Gujarat Titans for Rs 4 crore ahead of the 2027 season.The deal will see Harshal, a two-time IPL Purple Cap winner, move for half the amount SRH paid to acquire him at the 2025 mega auction.According to Cricinfo, "SRH have agreed to an all-cash trade, with GT procuring Harshal for INR 4 crore ($US 424,000 approx.), which is half the price he was bought for at the 2025 mega auction. Accordingly, GT's auction purse will be deducted by INR 4 crore."Also read: Aaryavir Sehwag, Lakshya Raichandani star as India beat Pakistan to win U19 Asia CupThe right-arm pacer enjoyed his most successful IPL campaigns in 2021 and 2024, finishing as the leading wicket-taker in both seasons. He claimed 32 wickets for Royal Challengers Bengaluru in 2021 and 24 for Punjab Kings in 2024.The 35-year-old, who was bought for Rs 8 crore in the mega auction, had a productive first season with SRH, taking 16 wickets in 13 matches at an economy rate of 9.80 in IPL 2025.However, his opportunities dried up in the following season as the franchise preferred uncapped Indian pacers Praful Hinge and Sakib Hussain.Harshal featured in just five matches in IPL 2026 and went wicket-less, conceding 10.82 runs per over.The move to GT will also take Harshal, who turns 36 later this month, to his home state. Born in Ahmedabad, he shifted to Gujarat a few years ago to pursue domestic cricket.At GT, he is expected to add experience to a pace attack that includes Kagiso Rabada, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna and Jason Holder.Gujarat Titans had shown interest in signing Harshal at previous auctions. They pulled out at Rs 10.5 crore during the 2024 auction before Punjab Kings secured him for Rs 11.75 crore. GT also bid for him at the 2025 mega auction, withdrawing at Rs 6.5 crore.The trade is part of an active pre-auction window ahead of the November 17 retention deadline, with SRH emerging as one of the busiest franchises.SRH have already acquired left-arm pacer T Natarajan from Delhi Capitals and brought in fast bowlers Khaleel Ahmed and Nathan Ellis from Chennai Super Kings in a four-player trade.

items.title: Telangana implements gig worker rules
items.summary: Hyderabad: The Telangana government on Saturday launched the Telangana Platform-Based Gig Workers (Registration, Social Security and Welfare) Rules, 2026, setting out 12 fundamental rights for gig and platform workers, including minimum remuneration, social security benefits, transparency in payments and protection against arbitrary account deactivation.Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, who launched the Telangana Gig Workers Special Security Scheme along with Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in Hyderabad, said the government would enforce the legislation to protect workers in the sector. The move fulfils a promise made by Gandhi during his Bharat Jodo Yatra in Hyderabad, when gig workers had raised concerns over working conditions and lack of social security.The bill was first passed by the Telangana Assembly in March 2026.As part of this scheme, the state will extend accident insurance coverage to gig workers and uncreases the coverage limit under the Aarogyasri health scheme to Rs 10 lakh.The rules provide for registration of workers and issuance of unique identification numbers, representation in decision-making, social security benefits including insurance, healthcare and pensions, and a welfare fund to be financed through contributions from aggregators.They also provide for greater transparency in earnings, payments and ratings, protection against discrimination, minimum remuneration, health and safety safeguards, fair contracts and advance notice of changes in working conditions.Other provisions also include the right to refuse work without penalties, safeguards against arbitrary blocking or deactivation of worker accounts, and time-bound grievance redressal mechanisms.Shaik Salauddin, founder-president of the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers Union (TGPWU), called the launch a significant milestone in the decade-long struggle of gig and platform workers in the state.He said the focus would now shift to ensuring that the provisions translated into enforceable benefits on the ground. The union has called on the state government to ensure time-bound implementation of the rules, operationalise the Welfare Board and Welfare Fund, and hold aggregators accountable for their contributions and obligations.Salauddin also said the union would continue to push for comprehensive national legislation guaranteeing rights to gig workers, arguing that the Centre's National Social Security Board, notified on October 30, was not a substitute for enforceable workplace protections."We will continue to organise, defend these rights and hold platforms and governments accountable for their implementation.We fought for a decade to secure these rights. We will continue to fight until every gig worker can exercise them," Salauddin added.

items.title: Voyager 1 nears one light-day from Earth
items.summary: Imagine sending a message to a spacecraft and having to wait an entire day just for it to arrive. Then imagine waiting another day for its reply. That is the extraordinary distance NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching, nearly half a century after it left Earth. The spacecraft is expected to cross the 16-billion-mile (26-billion-km) mark on Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. ET (10:16 GMT), according to NASA.Launched in September 1977, Voyager 1 is now on the verge of reaching a distance of one light-day from Earth, a milestone that puts into perspective just how far humanity's most distant spacecraft has travelled.To understand the scale, 26 billion kilometres is roughly equivalent to travelling around Earth's equator more than 650,000 times. It is also enough distance to circle the Earth nearly 650,000 times, compared with the roughly 40,000 km needed for a single trip around the planet.At its current speed of approximately 38,000 miles per hour (61,000 km per hour), Voyager 1 continues to move through interstellar space, far beyond the region dominated by the Sun's solar wind.The milestone is particularly striking because a light-day is not simply a measure of how long Voyager has been travelling. It describes how far light itself can travel in 24 hours. Since light moves at nearly 300,000 km per second, it covers approximately 26 billion km in a day.In other words, if NASA sends a radio command to Voyager 1 once it reaches this distance, even a signal travelling at the speed of light will need around 24 hours to get there.Why Voyager 1 reaching one light-day is such a stunning achievementThe distance is difficult to comprehend because everyday measurements become almost meaningless at this scale. A journey that would take a commercial aircraft travelling at 900 km per hour more than 3,000 years to cover is being completed by Voyager 1 over several decades.Even at its extraordinary speed, the spacecraft has taken nearly 49 years to approach the one-light-day mark. And unlike a car or aircraft, Voyager 1 cannot stop for maintenance, refuel at a station or return to Earth for repairs.Its continued operation is therefore as remarkable as the distance it has covered.Astrophysicist Alan Cummings, a senior research scientist at Caltech's Space Radiation Laboratory and a Voyager programme scientist since 1973, described the milestone as an engineering achievement."I view it as an engineering milestone, marking the amazing longevity of Voyager 1 — and also an engineering achievement to be able to communicate with Voyager 1 at its distance," Cummings said.The communication challenge is particularly significant. Radio signals travel at the speed of light, meaning the time taken to exchange information increases as Voyager 1 moves farther away. At one light-day, a message from Earth will take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft, while its response will take another 24 hours to return.That means NASA would need to wait roughly two days to send a command and receive a response, even if the spacecraft responded immediately.Voyager 1 has already left the Sun's protective bubbleVoyager 1's journey is not just about setting distance records. The spacecraft has travelled into a region of space that no human-made probe had directly explored before.In 2012, it crossed the outer boundary of the heliosphere, a vast protective bubble created by the Sun's charged particles and magnetic field, and entered interstellar space.This transition allowed scientists to study conditions beyond the Sun's immediate influence, including galactic cosmic rays — high-energy particles that originate outside our solar system.Cummings said Voyager 1 provided the first measurements of the energy spectra of low-energy galactic cosmic rays in interstellar space. These particles are largely prevented from entering the heliosphere by the outward pressure of the solar wind, making measurements beyond that boundary particularly valuable.The spacecraft also made important discoveries during its earlier planetary encounters. It identified a thin ring around Jupiter and two previously unknown moons, Thebe and Metis. During its encounter with Saturn, it discovered five new moons and identified a ring known as the G-ring.These findings helped reshape scientists' understanding of the giant planets and their surrounding environments.

NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule on Saturday said the merger discussions between the two factions of the Nationalist Congress Party ended for her after her cousin Ajit Pawar's death, and she had not received any communication from the other side on the issue.
She also rejected speculation about her party joining the BJP-led NDA.
Sule's categorical denials came amid renewed buzz about the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) and the NCP headed by Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar reuniting.
"When my brother (then NCP chief Ajit Pawar) was alive, there were discussions about a merger. A date had also been decided. But the day my brother passed away, the merger issue came to a full stop for me and within our party," Sule told reporters.

items.title: Jefferies' Chris Wood sees fresh US-Iran tensions as biggest risk to India, sees this sector as the best hedge

But in emerging markets, the obvious market to benefit from the reverse AI trade has been India, most particularly with the recent disappointing election result in Brazil, he said.Chris Wood on FII returnThis is why it is no surprise to Wood that foreign investors have turned net buyers of Indian equities in the past three weeks, after a massive selloff at the beginning of 2025. The other point that the ace investor pointed out is India’s attractive valuations, relative to history, which remains comparatively modest while the cyclical recovery in the economy this year has been better than expected.The Nifty index and the Nifty MidCap 100 index are now trading at 18x and 23x one-year forward earnings respectively. Most importantly, there is accumulating evidence that a long anticipated private-sector capex cycle is finally happening, with the best chart supporting this view of the rising trend in the imports of machinery goods. They have more than doubled from $29 billion in FY21 to $62 billion in FY26.Chris Wood on India's strong domestic flowsWood pointed out that the Indian stock market remains supported by extraordinarily resilient domestic equity mutual fund inflows. These inflows totaled Rs 350 billion in October this year and Rs 3.9 trillion in the first ten months of 2026, or an average of $4.1 billion per month.In this respect, India remains the most dynamic capital market in the world after the US, though directional terms for the benchmark indices have been capped by rising equity insuance to absorb these inflows.Iran war escalations biggest risk to Indian marketChris Wood said the international brokerage heard from a usually reliable source at the start of this week that Iran has agreed to re-open the Strait of Hormuz if it receives $8 billion of its frozen assets in an initial downpayment and if the US ends its blockade which has been in place since mid-April.Meanwhile, Donald Trump said this week that “Iran militarily is effectively over" and that renewed US strikes are "highly unlikely”. However, the hopes of any peace deal still remain elusive. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s comments in France at the G7 foreign ministers meeting suggests he favours a policy of intensifying economic pressure on Iran via the blockade. As for Iran the question is whether it decides to turn pre-emptive.Which sector does Chris Wood see as the best hedge to renewed geopolitical tensions?In this background, Jefferies will maintain energy stocks in the portfolios since they are the only way to hedge renewed geopolitical tensions. This is another way of advising investors who do not own energy stocks to take advantage of the recent sharp decline to buy them.“For such reasons GREED & fear will maintain energy stocks in the various GREED & fear portfolios as the only practical hedge available,” Wood wrote in his report.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: When should you sell a stock? Donald Cassidy's 5 lessons on making profitable sell decisions
items.summary: Investors often spend considerable time identifying the right stocks and deciding when to enter the market. However, knowing when to exit an investment is equally important. According to veteran investment researcher Donald Cassidy, the ability to make timely selling decisions can play a crucial role in determining long-term investment returns.Cassidy argues that investors often underestimate the importance of selling, even though profits are ultimately realised only when shares are offloaded. In his book It's When You Sell That Counts, he explains how emotional biases, market sentiment and the reluctance to accept losses can prevent investors from making rational exit decisions.Read more: How to win the investing game? Charles Ellis says make fewer mistakes, focus on long-term goalsCassidy was a senior research analyst at Lipper Inc. from 1990 to 2006, specialising in mutual funds, closed-end funds, investor psychology and behavioural finance. He has also addressed CFA societies internationally and served on the faculty of Harvard University's annual congress on the psychology of investing.According to Cassidy, fear, greed and confusion frequently lead investors to postpone selling decisions. By the time they eventually decide to exit, the opportunity to lock in profits or limit losses may have already passed.Here are five lessons from Cassidy on how investors can make better selling decisions.1. Overcome emotional barriers and challenge conventional thinkingOne of the biggest obstacles to profitable selling is investors' emotional attachment to their holdings. Many investors find it difficult to sell a stock because they fear missing out on further gains or regret exiting an investment that could potentially deliver higher returns.Cassidy believes investors need to recognise these psychological barriers and develop the discipline to make decisions based on analysis rather than emotions.Following the crowd and adopting a buy-and-hold approach may appear comfortable, but these strategies do not always produce the best outcomes. Investors should evaluate the reasons for holding a stock and prepare arguments both for and against retaining it.He also advocates contrarian thinking, suggesting that investors should be willing to consider selling when market enthusiasm is excessive and avoid panic selling when markets decline sharply.Read more: Nicholas Sleep’s investing lessons: Why patience, conviction and long-term thinking matter2. Do not assume today's corporate winners will remain winners foreverInvestors often develop strong preferences for companies that have delivered consistent growth and generated substantial returns. However, Cassidy cautions against assuming that successful businesses will continue dominating their industries indefinitely.Technological advancements, regulatory changes, international competition and shifting market dynamics can weaken even established market leaders.Companies enjoying strong growth may also command expensive valuations, leaving their shares vulnerable to sharp corrections if business momentum slows or expectations are not met.Cassidy therefore advises investors to remain alert to changes in a company's competitive position rather than holding its shares indefinitely simply because it has performed well in the past.3. Always have a selling target before buying a stockCassidy believes investors should establish an exit strategy before entering an investment. Buying shares without a clear selling objective can lead to confusion and emotionally driven decisions when market conditions change.He suggests that an investment target should incorporate three elements: a specific price objective, the business or market scenario expected to drive the stock higher, and a defined time frame.If the share price reaches the predetermined objective, investors should consider booking profits. Similarly, if the expected developments fail to materialise within the specified period, they should reassess the investment rather than continually extending their holding period.Cassidy also cautions against buying shares simply because investors admire a company's management, like its industry or agree with its broader objectives. The investment decision should ultimately be supported by a credible opportunity to generate returns.4. Be willing to sell underperforming stocks, even if they are favouritesAnother common investment mistake is holding on to underperforming stocks because of familiarity or emotional attachment.Cassidy argues that investors should not become loyal to individual stocks when their underlying business prospects deteriorate. Negative developments affecting a company can often be followed by additional challenges, making it important to reassess the investment thesis.Investors should regularly examine whether a company's fundamentals, growth prospects and competitive position continue to justify holding its shares.With thousands of investment opportunities available in the market, capital need not remain locked in stocks that are consistently underperforming.Cassidy's broader message is that investors should be prepared to move on from unsuccessful investments and redirect capital towards opportunities with stronger prospects.5. Understand opportunities beyond rising stock pricesCassidy also encourages investors to understand that stock prices can move in both directions. Limiting investment strategies exclusively to buying shares in anticipation of price increases can restrict the range of opportunities available to market participants.He highlights short selling as a tool that can potentially help investors benefit when fundamentally overvalued or technically overbought stocks decline.However, short selling involves significant risks, including potentially unlimited losses if share prices rise sharply. It therefore requires careful risk management and is generally more appropriate for experienced investors.Cassidy's broader argument is that investors should avoid developing a one-sided view of the market and should understand how different market conditions can create opportunities as well as risks.Why selling discipline matters in investingCassidy believes successful investing requires investors to become as comfortable with selling as they are with buying. Fear of missing further gains, reluctance to acknowledge mistakes and excessive market chatter can all interfere with rational decision-making.His approach emphasises proactive selling, clearly defined investment objectives and regular reassessment of individual holdings.Ultimately, identifying a promising stock is only one part of the investment process. Knowing when the original investment thesis no longer holds, when valuations become excessive or when profit targets have been achieved is equally important.(Disclaimer: This article is based on investment principles discussed by Donald Cassidy in his book, "It's When You Sell That Counts". These are general investment insights and should not be treated as individual investment advice.)

items.title: How French protests went out of control
items.summary: PARIS: Smashed windows and ransacked shops. Bloodied teenage protesters. A city hall on fire.Such scenes shocked France as rioting erupted last month during nationwide protests over high living costs and strained ​public services.Government officials have repeatedly blamed far-left radicals and "opportunistic delinquents," who they say took advantage of mostly peaceful demonstrations to attack symbols of state authority and capitalism across France.Also read | A bitter African feud, a leadership battle and Macron's diplomatic tightrope in CambodiaBut the authorities' heavy-handed response - including thousands of arrests, police beatings and curbs on marches - has added to the volatile mix of grievances fueling an anti-government groundswell that shows no sign of abating before next year's presidential election, Reuters found.Reuters journalists reviewed dozens of videos of the violence, attended the court hearings of 26 people accused of taking part and interviewed over 50 government officials, police officers, attorneys, protesters and witnesses to understand how a movement that began in September with small protests over conditions in state schools spiraled into some of the worst civil unrest in years.Police tactics have faced scrutiny since the start due to the life-changing injuries suffered by some young people, including blown-off hands and lost eyes. United Nations and other human rights experts have also raised concerns about the arrest of nearly 7,000 minors during sometimes-violent school blockades, which they said was disproportionate.Images of riot police baton-charging teenagers fanned support for the students from a diverse array of protesters - including parents, teachers, left-wing politicians and trade unionists - who joined their marches."We have rights," said Emilie Berthier de Grandry, 42, who has attended four demonstrations in Paris with her 15-year-old son, Aaron, dressed in an inflatable shark costume. "We're not going to let ourselves be pushed around."Also read | Judo legend Teddy Riner's presidential bid faces a tough fight in FranceNationwide demonstrations on October 17 also brought a resurgence of so-called yellow-vest protesters, an anti-establishment movement that faced off against President Emmanuel Macron's government in 2018-2019 over high fuel prices.The violent outbursts were so intense that day that police lost control of entire neighborhoods to rioters and looters in France's three largest cities: Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Every week since then, people have taken to the streets across France to voice their anger at police and the government.While the protests after October 17 were calmer, clashes erupted when police sought to disperse demonstrators as marches wound down. Officers repeatedly fired tear gas and charged groups of protesters who pelted them with bottles, paving stones and mortar-style fireworks. On October 24, far-right gangs entered the fray saying they wanted to protect businesses and clashed with protesters in several cities, authorities said.The Interior Ministry, which oversees the police, said internal watchdogs have launched 161 investigations into allegations of officer violence against protesters since September.Responding to Reuters questions, the Interior Ministry said force is used in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.The minister, Laurent Nunez, has expressed regret for injuries caused by explosive weapons used in crowd control, including stun grenades. But he has resisted calls to ban them, saying security forces must be able to defend themselves.Nunez has acknowledged security lapses, telling lawmakers that authorities didn't anticipate the scale of the October 17 violence.He credits a massive security operation - including the deployment of 70,000 police officers and paramilitary gendarmes - for maintaining public order at subsequent protests. But he says security forces still face "a great deal of violence" at demonstrations, including a petrol-bomb attack that injured three gendarmes in Paris on Halloween.The unrest comes at a difficult time for Macron, who won't be standing for election again in April. Strained public finances leave him little room to meet protesters' demands, and his centrist party no longer has the majority needed to pass major legislation.Macron has promised to both "listen to the anger" and "impose respect of the Republican order."The government has sought to appease protesters with proposals to improve education and the decision to bring forward a planned minimum-wage increase. Student leaders and major trade unions say the moves don't go far enough and have vowed to keep up the pressure.AN ORCHESTRA HIT WITH TEAR GASOn October 17, protesters started gathering in Paris' Place de la Republique hours before a march was due to start at 2 p.m.Sousaphone in hand, Mael Roth arrived at about 11 a.m. for a warm-up session with the Orchestre du Nouveau Monde, a 400-piece classical orchestra that planned to perform in support of the marchers. The musicians were playing "The Avengers" theme song when the first clouds of tear gas wafted into the square about an hour later, the 20-year-old told Reuters.At first, he said, they assumed it wasn't aimed at them and kept playing. But within 30 minutes, tear gas canisters were landing at their feet.Reuters video shows riot police using tear gas around that time to drive back a group of protesters who tried to march down Rue du Faubourg du Temple, a street leading off the square.Elodie Aldila, who works at a patisserie on the street, welcomed the protection. Other businesses in the area were ransacked later that day.Roth, however, didn't see why the musicians couldn't remain in the square. Their aim was to "make people feel good," he said. "It was tough to feel ... like we're not legitimate."A huge crowd of mostly peaceful demonstrators soon filled the square again. But by then, the orchestra had packed up and left.POLICE OVERWHELMEDAs tensions built through the afternoon, bands of protesters spread into surrounding streets, smashing storefronts, erecting barricades and setting fire to cars and bicycles.Also read | JD Vance weighs 2028 presidential bid as Iran war and midterm losses cloud MAGA futureAround 4 p.m., police wielding batons beat a man to the ground after a heated exchange on the edge of the square, video verified by Reuters shows. Rumors of the man's death spread on social media, further inflaming tensions. The rumors later proved unfounded.An internal police watchdog is investigating the incident, the Interior Ministry said.As night fell, looting spread in Paris and other cities. Some 3,000 businesses were ransacked over 24 hours, from luxury boutiques to supermarkets.Addressing lawmakers last week, Nunez said an "unprecedented" mix of challenges unfolded simultaneously that day, overwhelming security forces.More than a half million people demonstrated around the country on October 17 - 110,000 in Paris alone, Nunez said. They included thousands of "ultra-left" activists, who he said confronted police from the start and tried to stage unauthorized marches toward seats of power.He didn't elaborate on the activists' suspected affiliations. French officials use the term ultra-left to describe a variety of groups, including anarchists and antifascists, who they say are willing to use violence.As word spread about the unrest on social media, people with no affiliation to such groups joined in the looting, Nunez said.In interviews with Reuters, three police officers and an intelligence official familiar with investigations into the violence said they couldn't confirm Nunez's assertions about the central role played by ultra-left groups. They said more investigation was needed to understand what happened."There is a body of circumstantial evidence but no certainty," said Eric Moulin, a regional representative of the UNSA Police union in Marseille.Asked about the assertion, the Interior Ministry referred Reuters to Nunez's previous remarks.Nunez and other officials have said rioters are using tactics promoted on ultra-left online platforms to provoke a police response. They include forming "black blocs," in which activists wear all-black clothing and conceal their faces, to attack businesses and public buildings, they said.HARDENED OFFICERS 'SCARED OUT OF THEIR MINDS'In Marseille, black-clad protesters broke into the city hall and toppled a bust of Marianne, a symbol of the French republic. Another group hurled rocks and steel bars at police at the Old Port, forcing around 45 officers to retreat to their vehicles and leave, verified videos show."Some of my colleagues who were inside the police vans said they felt so threatened they reached for their service weapons," Moulin said. "These are tough, hardened men, yet they confided in me that they were scared out of their minds."In Limoges, municipal police took cover inside the 19th-century city hall; rioters set it on fire. The officers escaped unharmed.The Lyon tourism office was also torched.Prosecutors are investigating charges of attempted murder against a 34-year-old carpenter suspected of helping start the Limoges fire. The city's mayor, Guillaume Guerin, told French TV the man is on a security watchlist for alleged ties to the ultra-left and was "most likely the mastermind of the operation."The suspect's lawyers said they had no such information. They urged the mayor to respect the presumption of innocence, saying the evidence against their client is weak.Prosecutors didn't answer Reuters questions about the case.4,900 SUSPECTS ARRESTED, MOSTLY YOUNG MENJustice Minister Gerald Darmanin has instructed prosecutors to deliver "an extremely firm judicial response" to the violence, including pre-trial detention and expedited trials for many accused.Over 4,900 suspects have been taken into custody since October 17, Darmanin told French TV on November 3. Some 2,290 were referred for prosecution and 404 handed prison sentences so far. Few details have been released about the suspects, though Darmanin said most are young men aged 18-25.The Tribunal de Paris, France's biggest courthouse, had to open two extra courtrooms for fast-track trials, which are reserved for people accused of low-level offenses. The schedule was so packed that some hearings Reuters observed had to be pushed back because the judge hadn't had time to review the case file.A union of French judges and prosecutors said it believes the justice system is being "instrumentalized" by the government. The Justice Ministry didn't respond to a request for comment.To avoid a repeat of the October 17 violence, the government reinforced police with troops at subsequent demonstrations, imposed curfews and banned numerous marches.Rights groups including Amnesty International have warned of a slide toward "authoritarianism." Officials said they were upholding the rule of law.Some researchers who study French social movements and policing have argued that the government's heavy-handed response is perpetuating the cycle of violence."Escalation happens when black blocs provoke with violence, and law enforcement are ordered to respond with violence," said Fabien Jobard, a sociologist at the French National Centre for Scientific Research.In this way, he said, groups are able to demonstrate that police are violent and attract support.Titouan Malin, an 18-year-old medical student, said he started volunteering as a medic at protests after seeing how police treated demonstrators on October 17."When you face this kind of violence - repression to such an extreme degree - you're forced to respond with violence," said Malin, who wore a white helmet and had a gas mask hanging around his neck as he watched for clashes during one of Paris' biggest marches on November 5."It's the only way to make ourselves heard."

items.summary:
Former vice president Jagdeep Dhankhar was discharged from AIIMS here on Saturday, three days after he was admitted following a collapse, family sources said.
The 75-year-old former vice president was admitted to the hospital on Wednesday after he collapsed during his morning walk and remained unconscious for a few minutes.
He was admitted to the hospital's Cardio-Neuro Centre and was under the care of the Department of Cardiology for medical evaluation and treatment.
Security personnel accompanying Dhankhar had initially taken him home in a PCR vehicle after he collapsed.
Later, he was admitted to AIIMS.
Dhankhar has experienced several episodes of fainting and loss of consciousness over the past two years. But this time, the duration of loss of consciousness was the longest.
In June 2025, he fainted during the golden jubilee celebrations of Kumaon University in Nainital. In January this year, he suffered two bouts of unconsciousness at home. He was also admitted to the AIIMS ..

TRAI received 15.29 lakh complaints of unsolicited commercial communications during the quarter, of which 7.23 lakh were classified as actionable. Out of the 59 air quality monitoring stations in the city, seven recorded AQI in the 'severe' category on Saturday morning.
According to forecasts by the Air Quality Early Warning System for Delhi, the AQI is expected to deteriorate further in the next few days.

items.title: Flights halted at airports across US due to ATC communications problems
items.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon because of communications problems at regional air traffic control centres.
The FAA notice said the ground stop was being imposed "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety."
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said there is a communications issue affecting the 22 regional air traffic control centres that direct planes en route between airports nationwide. He said FAA technicians are investigating. This is the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that, the last time had been after the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication yet that "this was a nefarious attack against us. It's just a telecommunications outage."
"Everybody's safe. There's no reason to be concerned about your loved ones if they're flying," Mullin said.
There is no timeline for restart

items.summary: Mumbai: Has Indian IT turned the corner?After surging more than 17% in October, the Nifty IT index appears to have lost momentum, declining nearly 2% so far in November, although the Sensex and Nifty harnessed new-found enthusiasm from foreign funds to climb more than 10% in the run-up to Diwali and its immediate aftermath.Legacy IT stocks have stagnated despite a precipitous plunge in AI-heavy bets across Asia, putting a question mark over whether earnings concerns at outsourcing firms would continue to keep prices - and valuation multiples - in restraint despite obvious opportunities arising from a sectoral churn.135820397Since the beginning of October, South Korea's Kospi and Taiwan's stock index have fallen around 20% and 13%, respectively. Japan's Nikkei has declined 10%, while the Nasdaq Composite has lost 6%. The Shanghai Composite and Hang Seng have fallen 4.4% and 2.4%, respectively, reflecting the correction in global AI-related stocks.The September-quarter earnings of Indian IT companies, meanwhile, point to an uneven recovery, with mid-tier players outperforming larger peers while underlying demand conditions remain largely unchanged. Choice Institutional Equities said companies under its coverage reported average sequential revenue growth of around 5.4% for tier-2 players, compared with nearly 1.1% for tier-1 companies.Read more: BSE launches 14 new sector indices, expands BSE 500-based suite to 20 benchmarksCoforge led the mid-tier pack with 10.9% growth, followed by Persistent Systems at 7.8%, while Tech Mahindra and HCLTech led among larger companies.However, healthy deal bookings have yet to translate into commensurate revenue growth. Phased transitions, staggered project ramp-ups and longer client decision-making cycles continue to delay revenue conversion.Shorter-cycle AI engagements, typically lasting one to two quarters, are also limiting the visibility traditionally associated with large, multi-year deals, Choice said.A key concern for the sector is the changing economics of technology services as clients increasingly use AI to improve productivity and reduce costs. While AI is creating new business opportunities, these gains are yet to fully offset pricing pressure in traditional services.Kotak Institutional Equities estimates gross deflation of around 7% and net deflation of 3.5% for companies as clients seek a greater share of productivity savings through contract renewals.Read more: 12 bluechip stocks within 5% of their 52-week highs; should you chase them now?Sandeep Gogia, MD and co-head, Investment Banking, Equirus Capital, said pressure on enterprise clients to improve returns on AI-related investments, alongside concerns around safety, security and token-cost optimisation, could create fresh opportunities for IT services providers. "Integration of systems of records and data systems with systems of intelligence and AI models is not plug and play," Gogia said, pointing to opportunities in data engineering, application modernisation, cloud migration and cybersecurity as enterprises move towards large-scale AI implementation.On profitability, Choice said operational efficiency and cost discipline had partly offset wage and delivery-related pressures, although margin performance remained mixed. Kotak expects margins at large IT companies to remain largely stable, with rupee depreciation providing some support. However, pricing pressure and AI-related investments could weigh on profitability.The earnings outlook also remains uneven. Kotak expects Infosys to lower its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1.5-2.5%.

items.title: Fed officials signal further rate hikes as inflation remains elevated
items.summary: Federal Reserve policymakers signalled that further interest-rate increases are likely as stubborn inflation and rising business costs threaten to keep price pressures elevated, Reuters reported.San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said her “bias” was that the central bank would need to raise its policy rate, particularly because services inflation was moving in the wrong direction and showing signs of persistence.“We’re going to need to, in all likelihood, raise rates; I will deliberate this with my colleagues in December at our meeting and in all future meetings and make the collective decision that we judge is most appropriate for the economy that is evolving,” Daly said at a University of Nevada, Las Vegas Center for Business and Economic Research forecast event.The core Consumer Price Index, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, has risen about 0.3% month over month in each of the past three months. That is well above the monthly increase of 0.2% or less that would be consistent with the Fed’s 2% annual inflation target.Daly said she was particularly concerned that services inflation excluding housing was “not moving in the correct direction,” as that category tends to be persistent.“That’s a place where you might think a retailer, or a professional business, if they have to buy more expensive IT goods, pay higher energy bills and have other inputs that are rising in price, might pass that along to customers,” she added.The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point in September before holding it at a range of 3.75% to 4% in October. Markets widely expect quarter-point increases at the Fed’s December 8-9 and January 26-27 meetings, although Governor Christopher Waller has raised the possibility of a half-point move in December.Daly did not comment specifically on the timing of future increases but said markets understood that the Fed adjusts rates in response to changing economic conditions.She is also monitoring consumer spending closely ahead of the December meeting.Collins sees tighter policy aheadBoston Fed President Susan Collins also said further tightening was needed because inflation remained high, suggesting that rates may have to rise more than she previously expected.“I think it’s clear the direction that monetary policy needs to go and I would think that soon some additional firming, tightening of policy is appropriate,” Collins said in an interview with Bloomberg Television.Recent inflation data have been unfavourable and indicate that price pressures are spreading across the economy, Collins said. “I think it may be that a bit of a tighter policy path than I had pencilled in a couple of months ago might be appropriate.”Collins declined to specify how quickly rates should rise or how high they should go.“I don’t want to get ahead in terms of how high we should go or how fast,” Collins said, adding that her “best-case scenario” is for “a careful adjustment of policy.” She acknowledged, however, that “there are scenarios where I might think about that somewhat differently.”Speaking while attending a housing conference hosted by the Boston Fed, Collins said restoring price stability was essential to a healthy housing sector, even if tighter policy caused some near-term pain. She also said financial markets appeared to be functioning well.Logan calls for stronger market-support toolsDallas Fed President Lorie Logan said inflation was too high and monetary policy needed to become more restrictive. Earlier in the week, she argued for at least two additional quarter-point rate increases, potentially in quick succession.Logan also said the US Treasury market was functioning “very well” despite bouts of interest-rate volatility and that banks had improved their access to emergency funding over the past three years.However, she called on the Fed to strengthen its tools for supporting Treasury-market functioning and providing liquidity to banks without working against monetary policy.“Especially in an economic environment where tighter policy appears necessary, I believe it is prudent for the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) to strengthen its tools for supporting market functioning without providing unnecessary economic stimulus,” Logan said at a Dallas Fed conference on bank funding.Logan, a former head of open-market operations at the New York Fed, said no intervention was currently needed. She warned, however, that intervening during a monetary-policy tightening cycle could complicate the Fed’s communications.“Historically, the Fed’s interventions to support market functioning have come at times when the FOMC also wanted to stimulate economic activity,” she said. “The same asset purchases could serve two purposes: providing monetary policy accommodation and supporting market liquidity.”“If Treasury market dysfunction emerged now, the FOMC would not have the luxury of using the same asset purchases to accomplish two goals,” Logan said.Logan further said that the banks had improved their access to contingent funding, which provides liquidity during periods of market stress, but should continue preparing to use facilities such as the Fed’s discount window.As services such as FedNow and private-sector payment systems expand, banks could face liquidity needs during weekends and holidays. With the Fed planning to extend its Fedwire Funds wholesale payment system to Sundays and weekday holidays, Logan said discount-window operations should also be expanded.“This is not a change any one Reserve Bank can make on its own,” she said. “I look forward to discussions with my colleagues about this possibility.”Logan also urged the Fed to develop the ability to centrally clear its repurchase, or repo, operations. “This would reduce the balance sheet costs of intermediation,” she said. “Funding from the Fed could then flow more efficiently to the broad market.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Why Indians behave better at sacred sites
items.summary: The tranquil and indescribably beautiful environs of Kamarpukur and Joyrambati, the birthplaces of Sri Ramkrishna Paramhansa and Maa Sarada Devi in the verdant plains of West Bengal, are truly balms for the soul. Green-gold vistas of ripening rice fields criss-crossed by a myriad of small rivers and dotted with distant sleepy hamlets greeted the eye as a friend and I headed there from Kolkata. And the early morning autumn sun cast a golden, almost divine glow.It was a world away from the pollution-spewing trucks and buses, factories and warehouses that crowd the suburbs of Kolkata beyond the graceful Vidyasagar Setu arching over the Hooghly. Once the cacophony of the Durgapur Expressway was left behind, there was a perceptible change in mood. Anyone who lives in a frenetic big city these days would vouch that stress is endemic and heading out, away from the madding crowds, leads to an instant lowering of tension.Also Read: Indians splurge Rs 72k cr on their favourite obsessionAnd peace is the overwhelming feeling upon entering the impeccably maintained compounds in both villages that contain not only the quaintly thatched huts where the two elevated souls came into this world, but also prayer halls, offices, bhog areas, dispensaries, guesthouses and flower-filled gardens. Given that thousands - exceeding 20,000 on important days - visit Kamarpukur and Joyrambati daily and stay on for bhog prasad, the compounds' serenity is hard to believe.And their cleanliness stuns. Forget jhalmuri packets, tissue papers or plastic water bottles, not even fallen leaves or dust mar the pathways and gardens. It is not as if there are armies of sweepers on hand to pick up detritus either; visitors are simply more mindful while on the premises. How come? After all Indians these days are notorious for being loud, littering gits, on par with British lager louts. It seems that it all depends on whether places inspire respect and restraint.Also Read: India says foreign goods can overstayIn the expansive hallowed campuses of Kamarpukur and Joyrambati, these same people - Indians - did not talk loudly; they did not try to scratch their initials on pillars; they did not drape themselves on walls or amid the flowers to take selfies; they did not throw trash into the ponds; and they did not let their children turn into screeching, high-speed, wrecking balls. Polite attendants firmly told the few infringers to abide by the rules. And they all willingly complied.I have seen a similar all-pervasive calm at the Belur Math of the Ramakrishna Mission near Kolkata, the Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry and the Golden Temple in Amritsar, thousands of miles apart. There are more such places around India where desi visitors are anything but the kind of Ugly Indian Tourist that locals complain about from Goa to Gangtok, Kashmir to Kanyakumari. That just begs the question why Indians are so badly behaved in many other places.An overwhelming majority of those who come to Kamarpukur and Joyrambati are devotees. They, therefore, know the sanctity of those places and behave accordingly. The same is true of the sacred precincts at Belur, Pondicherry and Amritsar. But why is the same courtesy not extended to all places they visit? Do only the divine merit courtesy, cleanliness and calm? The public's behaviour at these places show that Indians can be model visitors when we want to be.At Kamarpukur and Joyrambati it is hard to be anything but ideal visitors, though. There's something about the cumulative effect of their soothing tranquillity broken only by birdsong and trees rustling in the autumn breeze, the fresh flowers artfully arranged around the statues of Sri Ramkrishna and Maa Sarada Devi, and the smiling sanyasis telling stories of the divine couple's limitless humanity and humbleness... On the journey back to Kolkata, our hearts were full.

Jensen Huang controversy puts Southeast Asia’s AI chip trade under scrutiny
items.summary: Chip and data-centre operators in Southeast Asia are bracing for tighter scrutiny after reports linking former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to a Chinese businesswoman suspected of spying for Beijing put Singapore and Malaysia in the spotlight, industry executives and analysts told Reuters.The controversy has prompted US lawmakers from both parties to push for stronger restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s role in US national security.Washington already restricts exports of Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips to China to protect US leadership in the sector. Lawmakers are now seeking to close a loophole that allows Chinese companies to rent computing power from overseas data centres and remotely access systems equipped with restricted chips.Any tougher regulations could include new export controls and licensing requirements for shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, the Wall Street Journal reported.Also Read | Anthropic IPO share orders from China are said to be rebuffedAlice Huang, the businesswoman suspected of spying for China, previously worked as an executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed. The company has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US.Singapore authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since February last year over possible false declarations related to server purchases and other alleged offences.“After this case, every operator in the chain will be expected to know its end user. Southeast Asian operators will still get Nvidia chips, but proof of where every chip sits and who it serves is now part of the product,” Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based investment research firm Shenton Research, told Reuters.A ‘post-DeepSeek moment’Southeast Asia’s data-centre industry has grown rapidly as global technology companies expand their AI infrastructure.Malaysia has approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of data-centre-related investment since 2021, according to the country’s trade ministry. Thailand had 42 data centres representing 3,400 megawatts of IT capacity and about 750 billion baht ($22.58 billion) of investment as of February, while Indonesia’s market was valued at $2.81 billion in 2025.Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data-centre consultancy Sprint DC, described the prospect of tighter US rules as a “post-DeepSeek moment.”“Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia. There could be a short- to medium-term market shock to the Malaysian data centre market,” Goh said.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe AI boom has supported economic growth across the region. Singapore raised its annual growth forecast in August to between 4.5% and 5.5%, from 2% to 4%, citing the AI cycle. In Malaysia, an increase in data-centre projects helped the construction sector grow 6% in the third quarter of 2026.The trade ministries of Singapore and Malaysia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Malaysia said Thursday that it was considering legislation that would allow the government to monitor data-centre operations, including the use of high-performance chips. Authorities said they needed to ensure that chips subject to US restrictions were imported for domestic use rather than re-exported.An investor and CEO of an Asian neocloud company, who asked not to be identified, said he spent Friday morning consulting lawyers in the US.“Everyone is still figuring out... Maybe every time you export something, there will be additional process to go through. We are worried about more scrutiny which will make it longer for chips to come through,” the CEO said.Singapore said in February 2025 that entities operating in the country accounted for 22% of Nvidia’s chip sales, although only 1% of the chips physically entered Singapore. Authorities have also charged a fifth person in a case involving alleged AI-server fraud.Region expected to withstand tighter rulesSome analysts said tighter controls were unlikely to derail the data-centre expansion in Singapore and Malaysia.“Singapore itself will be more stringent; I think it’s a natural thing to happen. Singapore will tighten rules, and the US will tighten rules, but I don’t think this will harm Singapore’s and Malaysia’s prospects of buying chips,”  Jarick Seet, head of small- and mid-cap equities at Maybank, told Reuters.A senior executive at a Singapore chipmaker, who declined to be identified, said Huang’s departure could make it more difficult for Chinese companies to obtain US chips while potentially improving availability elsewhere.“With Jensen out, the Chinese will have a harder time getting chips from the US. Maybe it is not a bad thing for the non-US people who will have more access to chips.”The executive said companies could also redirect investment to Southeast Asia if Democratic electoral victories in data-centre-heavy US states such as Texas and Georgia slow the development of new facilities.“Those companies are going to look elsewhere and likely come to countries that can offer them land and deals and power,” the executive said. “Even if we lose a chunk of the China business, I think we will get other companies coming looking for compute.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: India says foreign goods can overstay
items.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)  introduced greater flexibility for foreign businesses and organisations on Friday, bringing goods into India temporarily by allowing senior customs officials to extend the existing four-month stay limit under the ATA Carnet system.The move will benefit foreign exhibitors, businesses, media organisations and other international participants who need to bring equipment, commercial samples or professional goods into India for a limited period. Until now, such goods were generally required to be re-exported within four months of their import.Under the revised provision, Principal Chief Commissioners of Customs and Chief Commissioners of Customs can approve an extension beyond the four months if they consider it necessary in the public interest.However, the extended period cannot go beyond the validity of the respective ATA Carnet."Provided also that where the Principal Chief Commissioner of Customs or the Chief Commissioner of Customs, as the case may be, is satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest so to do, may extend the aforesaid period of four months by such further period as it may deem fit, not exceeding the period of validity of the A.T.A. Carnet," said a memo from the Department of Revenue.What changes under the revised ATA Carnet rules?The amendment gives senior customs officials the authority to grant additional time for temporarily imported goods to remain in India.Previously, the four-month limit applied under the relevant customs notification, leaving limited room for businesses and organisations that needed more time before sending their goods back.With the latest change, the Principal Chief Commissioner or Chief Commissioner of Customs can assess individual cases and allow an extension where circumstances justify it.The additional time will depend on the official's assessment, but there is one important restriction: the extension must remain within the validity period of the ATA Carnet. This means the new provision does not allow goods to stay in India indefinitely.The amendment has been made to Notification No. 4/2018-Customs, dated January 18, 2018, by inserting an additional proviso under condition (vi).What is the ATA Carnet system and how does it work?An ATA Carnet is an international customs document that allows goods to enter a country temporarily without the importer having to pay customs duties at the time of import, subject to compliance with the applicable conditions.Often described as a passport for goods, the document simplifies customs procedures for businesses and individuals transporting professional equipment, commercial samples and exhibition materials across international borders.The system is particularly useful for companies participating in overseas trade fairs, exhibitions and business events. It also helps media organisations and professionals who need to carry specialised equipment across countries for temporary assignments.However, the duty-free facility comes with an important condition: the goods must be re-exported within the permitted period.

items.title: Outlook outage scam: Beware of fake refund emails
Outlook down? Don't reset your password yet
items.summary: Microsoft outage today: Outlook users not able to access emails during the Microsoft 365 outage should resist the urge to reset their passwords/ reinstall Office. These fixes may seem worth trying when an inbox suddenly stops working but they won't help as Microsoft's services are down.MQTec Managing Director Moneeb Qureshi has warned users against making unnecessary changes to their Outlook accounts and software while Microsoft works to address the disruption.Microsoft outage began on Thursday affecting "Exchange Online". Outlook users experienced problems accessing their mailboxes through desktop, web and mobile applications, while email delivery was delayed.Outlook Not Working: Experts Say Leave Your Account Settings AloneA sudden Outlook error doesn't mean something is wrong with your password or computer. During a wider Microsoft 365 outage, the problem is beyond a user's control.Qureshi advised against resetting passwords, rebuilding Outlook profiles or changing DNS, proxy and sign-in settings without a specific reason. Unnecessary changes could leave users with additional configuration problems even after Microsoft restores its services.Checking Microsoft's public service status page is a better first step. Administrators can also look at the Service health section of the Microsoft 365 admin centre for updates.135804339Microsoft 365 Problems Extend to Teams and SharePointThe outage has affected more than email. While Teams chats, calls & meetings remained available. But calendar functions, scheduling & invitations faced problems.SharePoint users could still access files, although external file sharing was affected. Copilot, To Do & Planner also experienced unreliable loading. Some Defender and Purview security features operated with limitations.Microsoft's initial investigation found that an unexpectedly large number of servers had become unavailable and increased pressure on the remaining infrastructure. Microsoft said there was no indication of an attack.Are Outlook Emails Being Lost During the Microsoft OutageDelayed emails are not necessarily lost. And email systems generally try to deliver messages again when the receiving server becomes available.As per MQTec, Microsoft extended Exchange Online's normal 24 hour delivery window to 48 hours during the disruption, allowing delayed messages more time to reach recipients.Qureshi advised users not to resend emails. But they should do so only after receiving a non-delivery report confirming that the original message failed.135802371How to Keep Business Communications Running As Microsoft Is DownMQTec recommends that businesses have backup communication arrangements rather than relying entirely on Outlook.Emergency email accounts with another provider can help essential employees stay in touch during an outage. Businesses can also consider email continuity services that retain incoming messages until Microsoft 365 becomes available again.Locally stored data is another option. Outlook cached mode allows users to access previously downloaded emails, calendars and contacts without a server connection. OneDrive files may also remain accessible when they have been synchronised and configured to stay on the device.135781761

Razorpay moves closer to public market debut as Sebi gives green signal to IPO
items.summary: Fintech major Razorpay Software Ltd has moved a step closer to its stock market debut after receiving approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its initial public offering (IPO), according to an update on the regulator's website.The market regulator issued its final observations on Razorpay's draft offer documents on November 3, clearing the way for the company to proceed with the next stages of its listing process. Renewable energy independent power producer Sembcorp Green Infra also received Sebi's approval, on November 13, the update showed.Razorpay had confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with Sebi in June. The confidential filing route allows companies to obtain regulatory feedback without immediately making their financial statements and other sensitive business information public.The Bengaluru-based company is working towards a listing in the first quarter of 2027, ET had reported earlier this month. However, the timeline could be pushed back depending on market conditions and investor appetite. The final IPO launch date and pricing will be determined by demand from institutional and retail investors, as well as broader equity market sentiment.ET had reported on April 20 that Razorpay was preparing a confidential IPO filing to raise Rs 5,500-6,500 crore at an expected valuation of around $5 billion, or Rs 49,000-50,000 crore. This would be below the $7.5 billion valuation the company commanded in its last major private funding round in 2021.Subsequently, the fintech has also attracted investor interest at a lower valuation of around $3 billion, or Rs 30,000 crore, reflecting the more cautious approach investors have adopted towards valuations of technology companies ahead of their public listings.Razorpay's shareholders have approved a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,700 crore, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) through which existing investors can partially pare their holdings. Axis Capital, JPMorgan, Citi and Kotak Mahindra Capital are advising the company on the proposed IPO.The Sebi approval comes at a time when public market investors are increasingly scrutinising the growth, profitability and valuations of India's new-age technology companies. Walmart-backed payments rival PhonePe had paused its IPO plans earlier this year amid market uncertainty, highlighting the importance of timing for fintech companies looking to tap public markets.ALSO READ: Razorpay gets Sebi nod for Rs 5,000-6,000 crore IPO: sourcesFounded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay provides businesses with online and offline payment acceptance solutions, cross-border payments and a range of financial services. Its investors include Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Y Combinator and GIC.The company reported a 65% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 3,783 crore in FY25, compared with Rs 2,296 crore in the previous financial year. However, it posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 1,209 crore, largely due to expenses related to employee stock options, restructuring and tax costs associated with shifting its domicile to India."FY25 was a pivotal year for Razorpay. We delivered top-line growth through strong execution, while simultaneously improving our gross margins," cofounder and chief executive Harshil Mathur had said while announcing the company's financial results.Ahead of its proposed listing, Razorpay has also recalibrated its offline payments business, shifting its focus towards merchants that require an integrated online and offline payments offering. The move is aimed at improving operating efficiency and profitability as the company prepares to face public market scrutiny.The company completed its reverse flip, moving its domicile from the US to India in May 2025, removing a key structural hurdle ahead of a domestic listing.More recently, it received a final payment service provider licence to operate from Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City). items.title: Supply shocks to weaken monetary policy effectiveness: CEA Nageswaran
items.summary:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran on Friday said monetary policy tools such as interest rate adjustments may become less effective in tackling inflation in a world increasingly vulnerable to supply-side disruptions.
"Fiscal and other public policy measures will be more important because raising interest rates will not solve the supply-induced problems. If anything, it may even be counter-productive," he said at the 9th Annual Food Systems Dialogue here.
Amid persistent supply induced issues, countries will have to use all kinds of flexibilities with regards to the inflation targeting framework, he said.
"Since 2022, very few countries have met their inflation target. So, it will be there as a framework, but I think countries will take creative liberties with it, as they have to," he added.

items.title: Manappuram Finance shares drop 3% even as Q2 net profit soars 3x to Rs 701 crore. Why did Jefferies cut target price?
items.summary: Shares of Manappuram Finance dropped around 3% on Friday after the company reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 701 crore for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027, surging over 3 times from Rs 220 crore reported in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.The gold loan provider’s revenue from operations jumped 48% year-on-year to Rs 3,362 crore during the quarter under review, from Rs 2,274 crore reported in the same period last year. The company’s total expenses jumped more than 23% YoY to Rs 2,434 crore, from Rs 1,973 crore reported in the year-ago period. Manappuram Finance’s gold loan and other segment recorded around 54% YoY rise in revenue to Rs 3,043 crore, while that for micro finance rose over 12% YoY to Rs 329 crore. The company’s standalone assets under management expanded 69% year-on-year to Rs 63733 crore at the end of September. The shares of the company dropped to Rs 311 apiece on NSE on Friday morning.Also read | Manappuram Finance Q2 results: Profit soars 77% YoY, but NPAs riseJefferies on Manappuram Finance share priceJefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Manappuram Finance shares but reduced its target price to Rs 400 apiece from Rs 430. The latest target price implies 25% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 320 apiece on NSE.The international brokerage noted that the company’s Q2 profit was 5% ahead of its estimates as higher net interest income offset higher provisions. It expects branch expansion and customer growth to drive 23% gold loan growth and 18% consolidated AUM growth in FY27. The company’s NIM rose 63 basis points sequentially to 11%, while gold loan yields rose 30 basis points QoQ to 18%, likely driven by customers slipping into higher-yielding (lower-rebate) slabs with longer repayment cycles, as per the rebate pricing structure, as well as penalty charges. Mannapuram Finance plans to price its loans competitively, but expects gold loan yields to sustain at 17.5-18%.However, the company saw some stress in shorter tenure schemes like peers. Its management indicated incremental trends are better as customers adapt, although the company is gradually shifting to longer tenure schemes.Also read | Manappuram Finance's Stage 2 gold loans jump tenfold to 5%Jefferies raised FY27-28 EPS estimates by 3-4%, factoring in lower AUM growth, better NIMs, lower opex & higher credit costs. It highlighted that the spot gold price is down 7% since September and may remain range-bound over the near term amid Fed rate hikes. “We expect profit to rise 3x (off weak FY26 base) with ROE improving to 14% (7% FY26) over FY26-28. items.title: Sensex, Nifty's explosive rally pushes market to pre-Middle East war levels. How long will they take to scale fresh peaks?
items.summary: The return of FIIs and easing oil prices sparked a skyrocketing rally in the Indian stock market this month, pushing the benchmark indices to levels not seen since the Middle East war ensued earlier this year, but analysts say it may take a few more months for them to hit fresh lifetime highs.Sensex this week touched 82,000, marking the first time since last February before US-Israel’s joint air strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, beginning a conflict that sparked a sharp surge in oil prices and spooked investors, continuing till date. Nifty traded above 25,350 before the infamous March selloff began. The index has now traced its way back above the level.Also read |Sensex erases all Middle East war losses but is it too soon to forget the Hormuz factor?How far are Sensex, Nifty from their lifetime highs?Despite the recent gains, the benchmark indices are sharply down from their respective lifetime lows. Sensex had hit a lifetime high of 86,159 on December 1 last year, and Nifty had hit an all-time high of 26,373 early in January this year. The benchmark indices are around 5% away from their respective record peaks despite the recent rally.Sensex has recovered over 11,000 from its recent low to hover near 81,900, which leaves 86,000 about 5% away. Vaqarjaved Khan, Senior Fundamental analyst at Angel One, feels that this rally has fundamental support. Earnings visibility is improving, banking, autos and consumption are showing healthier demand, and softer input costs are helping margins, he said, adding that steady SIP flows from domestic investors also give the market a cushion even when foreign money turns cautious. Sensex’s recovery of over 11,000 points from its October low reflects a sharp improvement in market sentiment, supported by renewed foreign institutional inflows, easing crude oil prices and encouraging corporate earnings, said Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura. Why caution is warranted after such sharp spikeHowever, after such a steep rally, some consolidation and profit booking cannot be ruled out, the analyst said. While the broader market outlook remains positive, geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures and fluctuations in foreign capital flows could create intermittent volatility, according to Bolinjkar. “We expect the next leg of the rally to be increasingly driven by earnings growth rather than liquidity alone.”“I would not call valuations comfortable after such a sharp run. Earnings need to catch up with prices, and that is what I will be watching in the coming quarters. Crude oil, global cues and foreign inflows will decide how quickly we move,” Khan from Angel One said.The current rally has been driven by falling crude levels, the return of foreign money and better-than-expected earnings. All three need to hold, and none of them is guaranteed while the US-Iran situation remains unresolved and the Fed stays hawkish, said Tanvi Kanchan, Associate Director at Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers. She noted that the market is already showing signs of fatigue near these levels as the Sensex has slipped back from its November 11 high and has been trading in a narrow range on Thursday.Also read | Rs 80,000 crore FII buying sparks explosive rally on Dalal Street. Will RBI rate hike worries kill the party?When could Sensex, Nifty soar back to lifetime highs?A fresh lifetime high, which is sustainable, is a realistic possibility over the next few months rather than the next few sessions, provided crude stays contained and foreign flows remain positive, one can expect short term consolidation before the breakout, according to Kanchan from Anand Rathi.Khan from Angel One has a base case that the Sensex can cross 86,000 and set a fresh lifetime high in roughly three to six months, provided Q3 FY27 earnings hold up and there is no external shock. “I would advise investors not to chase the rally and to accumulate quality large caps on dips.”Ventura analyst Vinit Bolinjkar believes that Sensex could test the 86,000–86,200 zone over the next two to three months, provided foreign inflows remain strong, crude prices stay contained and corporate earnings sustain their momentum. “A decisive breakout above the immediate resistance of 82,500 could pave the way towards 84,000 and eventually 86,000,” he said.Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said if the market succeeds in holding on to its bullish momentum, Sensex could potentially revisit its lifetime highs over the next 3-6 weeks. “However, investors should not expect the rally to be linear. After such a sharp recovery, intermittent profit-booking and consolidation would be healthy and could provide a stronger base for the next leg of the uptrend,” according to Shah.Ajit Mishra, SVP of Research at Religare Broking, meanwhile believe Sensex is well positioned to reclaim the 86,000 mark and potentially surpass its previous lifetime high over the next 3-6 months. However, the next leg of the rally will need earnings delivery rather than just valuation re-rating, he said, adding that investors should use intermittent corrections to accumulate fundamentally strong businesses with sustainable growth prospects.Also read |MSCI rejig: LIC, Meesho, Coforge set to gain from index inclusion. Standalone profit before tax climbed 50.5% to Rs 99.54 crore, while standalone profit after tax increased 51.8% to Rs 74.61 crore.The earnings growth was supported by a sharp increase in e-commerce activity. MSTC facilitated the sale of residential and multipurpose land parcels in Hyderabad, valued at Rs 2,863 crore, on behalf of the Telangana State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation and the Hyderabad Metropolitan Development Authority.The company also partnered with the Karnataka Excise Department for the e-auction of liquor shop licences. items.summary:
A preliminary probe into the derailment of the Kolkata-Sairang Express at Digaru Railway Station in Assam on November 11 has pointed to a malfunctioning main braking system on the train.
A six-member probe team, in its report, found that the system primarily responsible for applying brakes in the coaches, technically known as the BP angle cock, was in an isolated condition in the locomotive.
"This may be the reason for this accident, as the brakes may not have been applied when the FP/BP angle cock of the loco was in an isolated condition," a joint note prepared by the probe team on the day of the accident said.
It further stated that the train crew applied the brakes, "but the brakes may not have been applied as the angle cock was previously in the closed position".
The probe report does not identify who rendered the braking system dysfunctional or whether the train crew overlooked safety procedures to check its functionality before operating the train.

items.title: US returns over $12 bn in oil proceeds to Venezuela since Maduro's ouster
items.summary:
The Trump administration says it has returned more than USD 12 billion, or almost 99 per cent, of the revenue obtained from the sales of Venezuelan oil since it ousted then-President Nicolas Maduro in January.
In a report released Thursday by the State Department, the accounting firm KPMG said the sales of Venezuelan crude, along with minor amounts of gold, minerals and fertilizer, produced USD 12.26 billion. Almost all of the money has been returned to Venezuela under the terms of a broad energy deal reached with the country's interim authorities, according to the report.
As of Sept. 30, the end of the 2026 budget year, USD 168.6 million remained in an escrow account managed by the US Treasury Department, the report said.
Under the terms of the deal, Venezuelan crude is sold on the open market, with proceeds going into the US-managed account. Venezuelan officials then seek approval for those funds to be returned to the country to pay for infrastructure and humanitarian needs.

DIIs book profits in longest selling streak in 4 years
items.summary: Mumbai: Their roles have decidedly reversed.For years, domestic funds have provided the backstop against exiting foreigners, lifting the share of local stock ownership to a record and preventing a rout of Indian risk assetsOver the past fortnight, however, as foreign funds have come flooding in, domestic institutional investors (DII) have sought to book the profit of patience.Mutual funds, banks, insurers and retirement funds have turned net sellers over the past nine sessions, marking their longest selling streak in four years.135785472Their exits coincide with the sharpest rally in Indian benchmark indices in years - and the meltdown of AI-themed trades in eastern Asia.Data from the NSE showed that DIIs sold equities worth over ₹47,662 crore between October 30 and November 12, marking their longest selling streak since November 2022 when DIIs sold for 10 straight sessions.Read more: New SIP registrations fall 20%, stoppage ratio climbs to 116% in October after 5-month decline If the trend continues, November could become the first month of net selling by DIIs since July 2023, when they offloaded around ₹2,700 crore. It could also mark their steepest monthly selling since November 2020, when they sold equities worth around ₹48,000 crore.Read more: Meesho block deal: SoftBank-backed entity likely to sell 1% stake worth Rs 1,174 croreNilesh Shah, managing director, Kotak Mahindra AMC, said the bulk of the selling is likely coming from profit-booking and portfolio rebalancing by Multi-Asset Allocation Funds (MAFs), Balanced Advantage Funds (BAFs), insurance companies and pension funds. The market rally has pushed up their equity exposure, prompting them to book profits to maintain their targeted asset allocation. Arbitrage funds have also contributed to the selling, albeit to a smaller extent, by exploiting reverse arbitrage opportunities in mid-cap stocks, where futures are trading at a discount to the cash market, prompting funds to sell shares and buy futures, Shah added.The DII selling comes even as foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have returned to Indian equities. Since the beginning of November, the Sensex and Nifty have gained nearly 10% each, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices have advanced around 8% each. FPIs have invested around $8 billion in Indian equities since mid-October, amid a correction in AI-related stocks globally and a decline in crude oil prices.Despite the recent selling, DIIs have remained a key source of support for the market through the year. Akshat Garg, AVP - Research & Product at Choice Wealth, said DIIs had been net buyers of over ₹6.5 lakh crore in 2026, supported by steady SIP and insurance inflows through market corrections. Following the sharp recovery, they are now trimming exposure to richly valued pockets, raising cash and allowing returning foreign investors to take on the role of marginal buyers.
