items.title: US stocks: US market closes lower as Nvidia slide outweighs energy rally
items.summary: US stocks closed lower on Thursday, as a drop in Nvidia shares after CEO Jensen Huang's exit outweighed gains in energy shares.The chip company's shares fell but were well off the day's lowest level after earlier dropping nearly 12%. Retail investors bought Nvidia shares worth about $111 million in the first half hour of trading, the biggest opening bid on record for the stock, according to data from Vanda Analytics.The S&P 500 lost 25.99 points, or 0.34%, to end at 7,593.39 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 102.44 points, or 0.40%, to 25,363.75. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 190.29 points, or 0.36%, to 52,296.20. The S&P 500 energy index gained about 2%, making it the best performer among the benchmark’s 11 major sectors. Crude prices rose after President Donald Trump wrote on social media that the US did not need a deal with Iran.AI-linked stocks fell globally after Nvidia named Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. AI cloud company Nebius tumbled nearly 18% following its quarterly results and outlook.However, Nvidia rivals and other major technology companies, including Broadcom, Advanced Micro Devices, Alphabet and Amazon, advanced and provided the biggest support to the S&P 500.Stocks have been volatile in recent days as sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections fueled concerns about tighter AI regulation. Uncertainty surrounding Nvidia’s leadership has also pressured one of the main drivers of the current bull market.Also Read | US stocks: Nvidia shares plunge 13% after Jensen Huang quits as CEO; Colette Kress named interim chief“Right now, the market is selling AI stocks and tech stocks and buying safe stuff, just like it did in the first halo trade in January and February of this year, but it will flip back,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management in St. Louis.“That’s the tug of war the market is doing right now. It’s concerns about deceleration versus just pointing out that the absolute valuation and growth rates are still pretty compelling.”Nvidia’s financing ties face scrutinyHuang’s departure is expected to intensify scrutiny of AI companies with close financial ties to Nvidia.The chipmaker has backed several businesses, including some of its customers, through financing arrangements that investors are reassessing following the leadership change.Also Read | Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing“Nvidia is the circular-funder-in-chief; they’re the biggest by far at this point, and I assume that activity will moderate,” Ellerbroek said.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 0.5% after gaining 17.2% over the previous four sessions. CoreWeave dropped about 7%, while shares of data-center companies IREN and Applied Digital also declined.Investors await inflation dataInvestors are looking to Friday’s Producer Price Index for further indications about inflation after consumer prices rose more than expected earlier in the week.Markets are fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least 25 basis points in December, with a 15% probability of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Comments from several Fed officials this week suggested the central bank could consider a more aggressive path of rate increases as price pressures intensify.Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said Thursday that she did not believe the central bank needed to shift to larger rate increases to control inflation. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said rates would probably need to rise further to address elevated inflation but did not indicate any urgency.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday raised concerns not only about the future of the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker but also about its willingness and ability to continue financing the artificial intelligence boom, Reuters reported.Huang’s exit added another pressure point to one of the global market’s most crowded trades. It came after Nvidia’s board met late Wednesday to consider the longtime CEO’s future following reports of two extramarital affairs.Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, the company said in a statement.Investors initially sold Nvidia shares and stocks linked to the company, including data-centre operator CoreWeave and South Korea’s Naver. Shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced.Chinese graphics-processing-unit makers also rallied on expectations that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could help local suppliers gain market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each surged nearly 10%.Nvidia shares fell 13%, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.6%.The broader concern is that Nvidia could scale back its strategy of financing data centres under new leadership, potentially slowing investment across the AI industry.Also Read | Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, according to Reuters.Nvidia has been the flagship stock of the AI revolution. Its technological lead and surging sales have driven its share price up about 900% in the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT helped usher in the generative-AI era.The company has also emerged as a major financier of the industry, investing billions of dollars in customers through equity stakes and other financial commitments as it anticipates growing demand for increasingly powerful chips.“Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.”Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang after reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. A separate report involving another alleged affair emerged before Wednesday’s board meeting.Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters that Nvidia’s revenue was unlikely to fall suddenly following Huang’s departure. The greater concern, he said, was the company’s long-term direction because of Huang’s central role in shaping its computing strategy.“Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” Boloor said.Nvidia’s departure reverberates across AI stocksHuang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4 trillion company he co-founded and built over more than three decades. Nvidia has become the leading supplier of AI chips and a focal point of the technology rivalry between the United States and China.Asian chip stocks, which had rallied alongside Nvidia during the AI spending boom but recently came under pressure from concerns about financing costs and demand, also declined.Nvidia disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its latest earnings report. These included an obligation of up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and more than $50 billion in lease and capacity guarantees.In August, Nvidia said it had partnered with six major financial institutions, including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone, to establish computing-finance platforms seeking more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said the company could backstop as much as $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raise the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility,” Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot. Anthropic’s initial public offering this month is expected to test investor demand for AI-related assets.CoreWeave shares fell more than 7.5% in premarket trading after surging Wednesday on upbeat earnings. Naver, in which Nvidia invested $1 billion by financing a data-centre expansion, dropped 6%.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

President Xi Jinping on Thursday vowed to bring Taiwan under Chinese control, saying the "complete reunification" of the motherland is an "unwavering historical mission" for the ruling Communist Party of China (CPC) and will certainly be achieved.
Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks at a ceremony marking the 160th birth anniversary of Sun Yat-sen, one of China's nationalist leaders who is revered on both sides of the Taiwan Strait.
He pledged to accommodate the island's realities but took a hard line against separatism.
"Resolving the Taiwan question and realising the complete reunification of the motherland is an unwavering historical mission for the CPC, the shared aspiration of all Chinese people, and a natural requirement for the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation," Xi was quoted as saying by the state-run Xinhua news agency.
China views Taiwan as a rebel province that must be reunified

items.title: What Nvidia said after CEO’s shocking exit
items.summary: In a move that would certainly send shockwaves through the tech world, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company as president, chief executive officer (CEO) and a member of the company's board of directors, with immediate effect on Thursday.Meanwhile, Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has been appointed as interim chief executive officer as the chip giant begins a search for a permanent successor.Nvidia's board said it will consider both internal and external candidates for the position. Kress will continue to serve as the company's executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO until a permanent successor is appointed.Also Read | Jensen Huang quits as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandal; AI chip giant names Colette Kress interim chiefThe company did not disclose a reason for Huang's resignation in its announcement.Kress has served as Nvidia's executive vice president and CFO since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company's finance organisation and played a key role in Nvidia's growth and evolution.Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.What Nvidia's board saidHarvey C. Jones, who has been appointed Nvidia's first-ever chair of the board, said Kress has helped lead the company through a period of “extraordinary growth” and has a deep understanding of its business, customers, operations and financial position.The board said it has “full confidence” in Kress and the leadership team and expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.“NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” Kress said.She added that Nvidia would continue advancing its work in accelerated computing and AI while focusing on customers, partners, developers and shareholders.Also Read | Jensen Huang and the Chinese spy honeytrap: How does China allegedly use this strategy to gather sensitive US information?Jensen Huang's Nvidia legacyThe board said Huang's contributions to Nvidia were “profound” and described the company as one of the world's most consequential technology companies.“The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” Nvidia said.Huang founded Nvidia and has led the company for 33 years, overseeing its transformation into a dominant player in accelerated computing and AI.A private affair, a very public exitHuang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has been at the helm of the company for more than three decades. During that time, he transformed Nvidia from a graphics chipmaker into one of the biggest beneficiaries of the global artificial intelligence boom. His departure marks a major change for the company and the semiconductor industry.Huang's exit comes amid a controversy involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former senior executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, whom US intelligence agencies suspect of gathering information for Beijing. Huang admitted to having an extramarital relationship with her and apologised to his wife, children and Nvidia employees.The revelations prompted Nvidia's board to launch an independent investigation into reports that Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company, however, said its board had no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's confidential information had been compromised. The affair finally cost Huang to step down from his position from the company.

items.title: Kimberly Powell: Nvidia career in spotlight
items.summary: Kimberly Powell has spent 18 years at Nvidia, moving from medical imaging to some of the company's biggest healthcare AI projects, including genomics and drug discovery. But the 48-year-old vice president is now in the headlines for a different reason.The New York Times reported on November 11 that she had an intimate relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, 63, who is her direct boss. The report cited five people who worked at the company and said the two were seen being affectionate in a video recorded at a San Jose hotel during an Nvidia conference in March. Powell is married, the newspaper reported.When the Times asked Huang about his relationship with Powell, he reportedly replied, "I don't think you should be talking to me directly," before ending the call. Powell and Nvidia had not responded to Business Insider's requests for comment as of November 12. Neither has confirmed the reported relationship.The report comes as Nvidia is already dealing with another controversy involving Huang. The CEO recently told employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without naming anyone.Separately, the company's board has been examining whether a technology executive with alleged links to Chinese intelligence targeted Huang. That case involves Alice Huang, not Kimberly Powell. Together, the developments have put the company's leadership, internal policies and board oversight under fresh scrutiny.Who is Kimberly Powell and what is her role at Nvidia?Powell is one of Nvidia's senior executives responsible for taking its AI computing technology beyond conventional chip applications. Her current role covers healthcare and life sciences, two areas where Nvidia wants to expand the use of accelerated computing and artificial intelligence.        View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Yahoo Finance (@yahoofinance)She joined Nvidia in 2008 as a director. Her initial responsibility was to establish Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) as computing accelerators for medical imaging equipment.Before joining Nvidia, Powell worked in hardware engineering and product management at Planar Systems, where she focused on diagnostic imaging systems. She holds a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, with a concentration in computer engineering, from Northeastern University.Her entry into Nvidia was not the result of a conventional executive recruitment process. On an August 2026 episode of the Lifers podcast, she explained that she had contacted Nvidia to discuss its computing technology. The company subsequently recognised its potential applications in healthcare and approached her about joining.She described the opportunity as a "dream come true."Powell's responsibilities grew over the years. Her LinkedIn profile says she became a senior director in 2016, leading an AI-focused business development team. In 2017, she was promoted to vice president of healthcare.When she joined in 2008, one of the main opportunities was using GPUs to process medical images. Medical imaging systems generate large volumes of data, and GPUs can process many calculations simultaneously. This makes them useful for applications such as analysing CT scans, MRI images and other diagnostic images.Over time, Nvidia expanded this approach into other parts of healthcare.Its medical imaging platform, MONAI, provides tools for developing AI applications that analyse medical images. Its BioNeMo platform supports AI research in biology and drug discovery. Parabricks uses accelerated computing to process genomic data.Powell's role has therefore expanded from promoting GPUs for imaging equipment to developing a wider computing and software ecosystem for healthcare companies, hospitals and pharmaceutical researchers.According to her profile on the Milken Institute's website, she also oversees the global strategy and commercial expansion of these platforms.Kimberly Powell report and Alice Huang investigationThe Powell report is the second major development involving Huang's personal relationships to emerge during Nvidia's current leadership crisis. But the two cases concern different women and different allegations.The first involves Alice Huang, a technology executive associated with Megaspeed. The New York Times previously reported that US officials believed she might have been recruited by the Chinese government to gather information about Nvidia.The allegations have raised national security questions because Nvidia makes some of the world's most advanced AI chips, which are subject to US export restrictions on sales to China.Nvidia's board launched an investigation into whether Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The company has also faced scrutiny over its relationship with Alice Huang and the circumstances surrounding the alleged intelligence operation.The issue has also reached Congress. Republican lawmakers have sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on his relationship with Alice Huang and the national security concerns surrounding Nvidia's business in China.On November 11, Reuters reported that Nvidia's board had met to consider whether Huang should be removed as CEO. The Wall Street Journal separately reported that the board was preparing to oust him.Nvidia has 11 board members, including Huang. Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can remove him, with or without cause. All directors other than Huang are considered independent.As of November 12, no final removal decision had been publicly announced.Reuters also reported that there was no obvious successor if Huang were removed. Nvidia's CFO Colette Kress and senior data-centre executive Ian Buck have been mentioned in discussions about possible leadership arrangements, but no successor has been announced.Nvidia is scheduled to report its quarterly results on November 17.Nvidia shares closed at $173.73 on November 11, gaining 2.87% during the regular session. However, the stock fell more than 8% in extended trading after reports that the board was considering Huang's future.Reuters reported that Nvidia shares also fell around 7% in early Frankfurt trading on November 12. The company's market value had declined by roughly $600 billion since the board announced its investigation into the Alice Huang matter, according to the report.

items.summary: On Thursday, Andhra Pradesh called on American retail major Walmart to expand its local procurement by bringing the state's MSMEs, women-led self-help groups (SHGs), and artisans into its supply network.The request was made during discussions between Andhra Pradesh's IT and HRD Minister Nara Lokesh and Paul Dyck, Walmart's Senior Vice President for Global Government Affairs and Business Diplomacy, who met on the sidelines of the 31st CII Partnership Summit."Andhra Pradesh is asking Walmart and Flipkart to widen their sourcing from the State beyond seafood and pharmaceuticals, to include its MSMEs, women-led self-help groups and artisans," an official statement noted.To build on the momentum of the New Delhi Walmart Growth Summit—which linked Indian vendors with the retailer's international buying teams, Lokesh proposed that Walmart host a specialized MSME sourcing event in Andhra Pradesh centered on seafood and textiles. He further recommended establishing a dedicated pipeline within Walmart and Flipkart’s domestic and international supply chains for goods produced by local artisans and women-led SHGs, specifically those marketed under the state's Swayam AP and Lepakshi labels.According to the official release, Dyck acknowledged that Walmart ranks among the top purchasers of Andhra Pradesh shrimp, buying over 65 million pounds annually, while also procuring textiles, engineering goods, and pharmaceuticals from the region.Furthermore, Flipkart's regional footprint has generated over 28,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities. Its operational infrastructure includes over 100 logistics hubs covering roughly 12 lakh sq ft, alongside 0.33 million sq ft dedicated to wholesale operations. Through a memorandum of understanding with the AP MSME Corporation and the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (RTIH), over 3,200 MSMEs have received training, resulting in more than 900 businesses actively selling on the Walmart and Flipkart platforms.Dyck assured that Walmart would review the state's recommendations."Walmart is already one of the largest buyers of Andhra Pradesh shrimp. Now we want them to look at the rest of what our State makes. Our MSMEs, women's groups and artisans make products of global quality. What they need is a direct line to global buyers, and Walmart and Flipkart can provide it," said Lokesh.

items.title: India’s Russian fossil fuel imports hit record
items.summary: India was the second-largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels in October, purchasing hydrocarbons worth €6.4 billion, according to a monthly analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA). It was India’s highest monthly total in data going back to January 2022.Crude oil accounted for 91% of India’s purchases at €5.8 billion. Coal imports were worth €333 million, while oil products accounted for €232 million.Indian refineries raise Russian crude purchasesIndia’s imports of Russian crude oil rose 10% from September. Imports increased at all three of the country’s largest importing refineries—Vadinar, Jamnagar and Paradip.Imports at Vadinar rose 12% month-on-month, while Jamnagar and Paradip recorded increases of 22% and 28%, respectively. The rise made Jamnagar the biggest importer of seaborne Russian crude in October.Refineries in India, Turkiye and Brunei that use Russian crude exported oil products worth €1.6 billion to countries imposing sanctions in October. The destinations included the European Union, Australia, the US and New Zealand.Ten of the 12 shipments of oil products from refineries processing Russian crude that reached EU ports in October departed from India’s Jamnagar refinery. The remaining two shipments came from Turkiye’s STAR refinery.CREA estimated that €389 million worth of the oil products exported by these refineries were made from Russian crude. Exports from the refineries to sanctioning countries rose 21% in volume terms from September.Russia’s fossil fuel earnings reach four-year highChina remained the largest buyer of Russian fossil fuels, purchasing €10.7 billion worth of hydrocarbons in October. The European Union was the third-largest buyer at €2.2 billion, followed by Turkiye at €1.1 billion and South Korea at €488 million.Russia’s total fossil fuel export revenues rose 14% month-on-month to €754 million per day in October, the highest monthly level since December 2022. Export volumes remained broadly unchanged.Crude oil export revenues rose 19% to €449 million per day, with seaborne crude earnings increasing 23% to €352 million per day. CREA said this was the highest monthly level recorded since its data series began in January 2022.The report said higher global oil prices, linked to the energy crisis around the Strait of Hormuz, helped increase Russia’s fossil fuel earnings. Russia’s Urals crude averaged $101.70 a barrel in October, more than twice the EU and UK price cap of $44.10 a barrel.CREA also said that 60% of Russia’s seaborne oil was transported by sanctioned “shadow” tankers in October. Another 37% was carried by tankers owned or insured in G7 countries and their partners.A crude oil price cap of $30 a barrel, if fully enforced, would have reduced Russia’s seaborne crude oil export revenues by 21%, or €2.2 billion, in October, CREA said. A lower cap on crude and oil products together could have reduced Russia’s total seaborne oil export revenues by 25%, or €3.4 billion.

items.title: US stock market selloff: Four indicators suggest correction may not be over
items.summary: The recent selloff in US stocks has left investors searching for signs of a market bottom, but four key indicators suggest it may be too early to declare the correction over, according to a Reuters analysis.Technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks have fallen around 10% from their recent peaks after the Nasdaq-100 hit a record high in early October. While shares have stabilised somewhat, investor positioning, options activity and technical indicators continue to signal caution.Read more: Chinese yuan edges higher, but stronger dollar caps gains Technology positioning shows signs of easingAccording to Deutsche Bank data cited by Reuters, investors have reduced exposure to technology stocks since late September, shifting towards other sectors. The latest selloff pushed tech positioning below levels recorded during the April 2025 tariff-related market turmoil.Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte said the decline appeared to be driven by investors unwinding crowded positions. He added that positioning levels could create conditions for a technology sector rebound.Stock correlations offer some reliefAnother relatively positive signal is the limited increase in expected stock correlations. Barclays strategists noted that three-month realised correlation among the 50 largest S&P 500 companies fell to a record low in late September.Although expectations for correlations increased during last week's selloff, the rise remained modest. Rocky Fishman, founder of Asym Research, said this suggested investors viewed the decline as a sector-specific correction rather than a broader economic downturn, Reuters reported.Read more: South Korean shares rise as tech stocks rebound on Wall StreetOptions activity presents a mixed pictureRetail investors had purchased call options on individual stocks in record volumes this year, helping support the AI rally. However, that trend reversed sharply last week.According to Carrick Lane data, retail call buying in AI stocks dropped significantly, contributing to the post-election selloff.The shift has reduced excessive bullish positioning, but options indicators have not weakened enough to provide a strong buying signal.Technical indicators remain cautiousTechnical signals continue to suggest that the market may not have reached its bottom. Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors, said the rebound in the Invesco QQQ ETF, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, had stalled below its downward trend line.Weak short-term momentum and the absence of a DeMark exhaustion signal suggest US stocks could remain volatile for another couple of weeks, Newton said.Overall, while reduced technology exposure and relatively stable stock correlations offer some encouragement, options positioning and technical trends suggest investors should remain cautious before calling an end to the market correction.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times.)

items.title: Pacer Auqib Nabi banks on domestic experience to succeed in New Zealand
items.summary:
Extra pace has its benefits but Indian pacer Auqib Nabi says he is relying more on seam movement and skills acquired over the years in the domestic circuit to make a mark in the ongoing ODI series against New Zealand.
Nabi, who has played three ODIs after making a forgettable debut against the West Indies at home, relies on movement in the air and off the pitch to fox the batters. He bowls in the 130kmph range.
Speaking to reporters ahead of the fourth ODI against the Black Caps here, Nabi was asked if he plans to increase his pace. India lead 2-0 in the series after the third match was washed out.
"Obviously, if you have the pace, it's very good. But my skill, I back that. I have done well in domestic cricket. Here, I have come on skill. if there is pace, it is a plus factor. But I back my skill. What I did well in domestic will be useful here as well," said Nabi.

items.title: Ola Electric shares jump 7% ahead of Q2 results, extends EV-policy rally
items.summary: Shares of Ola Electric Mobility jumped more than 7% on Thursday ahead of the EV scooter-maker’s Q2 earnings announcement. The stock has now rallied around 9% in just two days following the Centre's decision to make electric vehicles the default choice for staff-car procurement by government ministries and departments.Ola Electric shares rose to Rs 37 apiece on NSE on Thursday morning. Notably, this is only the second time in a month the stock has crossed this level. The sharp 9% surge over the two days has added more than Rs 1,400 crore to the company’s market capitalisation, pushing it above Rs 17,150 crore.Also read | EV makers turn to family scooters to drive mass-market adoptionAll about the centre’s new EV procurement policyThe Finance Ministry has made electric vehicles (EVs) the "default and preferred choice" for the procurement of government staff cars in all ministries and departments of the Centre, with immediate effect. It also doubled the net dealer price ceiling for the procurement of EVs by central government ministries and departments to Rs 20 lakh, while that for ICE vehicles, including petrol, diesel and hybrid cars, has been fixed at Rs 10 lakh.The government also mandated preference to EVs in hiring cars for government use. The moves are aimed to promote electric mobility, reducing dependence on fossil fuels, and taking into account the prevailing market prices and lifecycle costs of vehicles."Going forward, Ministries and Departments shall ordinarily procure Electric Vehicles (EVs) at the time of condemnation or replacement of their existing ICE staff cars. EVs shall be the default and preferred choice for procurement," the official order reads.Also read | Centre's EV push puts electric mobility stocks in the fast laneOla Electric share priceAfter a flat market debut in August 2024, Ola shares rose to a lifetime high of Rs 157.40 apiece later that year. The stock subsequently lost momentum and fell to a lifetime low of Rs 22.25 in March 2026, nearly one-seventh of its peak value.The stock had fallen more than 62% from its 52-week high of Rs 59.20 apiece, hit in September last year, to a 52-week low of Rs 22.25 apiece in March this year. However, the stock subsequently staged a sharp recovery, doubling from that level in three months to hit a 52-week high of Rs 49.05 apiece in June this year. It has now pared some of the gains.Ola Electric shares gained over 4% in the past week and around 3% over the past month. However, the stock remains down more than 2% so far in 2026 and 15% over the past year.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Officials said there were no reports of property damage or casualties at the time of filing the copy.
The moderate earthquake occurred at 4.30 am, with its epicentre located around 40 km northwest of Yuksom in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).
The NCS said the earthquake was recorded at a depth of 73 km, at latitude 27.671 degrees north and longitude 87.987 degrees east.
Mild tremors were felt in several areas of West Sikkim, as well as parts of East Sikkim, including the state capital.

Specialised teams equipped with drones and sniffer dogs have been deployed across the forested stretches and difficult mountainous terrain, the officials said.
Babi Chand, 57, and Rashpal Kumar, 45, both posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at Kiyar village in Dachhan, went missing on Wednesday while travelling from their camp to an Army post at Dharna-Marwah.
Their mobile phones were initially reachable but were later switched off, raising concerns among security agencies and prompting to launch an extensive search operation.

items.title: Oil below $92 amid hopes of peace talks
items.summary: Oil prices edged lower by more than $1 on Thursday as investors increasingly hopes for peace talks to resolve the Middle East conflict as well as the much-longer lasting Russia-Ukraine war.Brent crude futures fell more than $1 to trade below $92 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures also lost over $1 to trade below $86 per barrel on Thursday morning. This comes after Brent crude rose over 1% on Wednesday after hitting two-month lows in the previous day.Russian and Ukrainian negotiators have agreed to a major prisoner exchange during their peace talks held over two days in Abu Dhabi, although US mediators said differences remained on other major issues, including territory. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country hoped to achieve concrete results on resolving the war this year.Also read | India's battered rupee finds an unlikely rescue party in cheaper oil and Wall Street's AI routBack in the Middle East, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the government will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave Iran and there will be consequences if the US launches new strikes. The US meanwhile has said that nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, while US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes.Meanwhile, OPEC+ crude oil production jumped in October, driven by a sharp increase in output from Saudi Arabia despite continued disruption to shipments through the Hormuz Strait. US crude stocks jumped by 9 million barrels in the latest week, Reuters quoted market sources as saying, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute.Where are oil prices heading for?While oil prices have dropped from their multi decade highs which they hit earlier this year, analysts remain cautious amid the seesaw political game in the Middle East. Goldman Sachs recently raised its oil price forecasts, citing increasing risks to global supplies. The investment bank warned that Brent crude could climb to $140 per barrel in 2027 if oil production across the Gulf region remains significantly below its 2025 average.Goldman Sachs recently raised its oil price forecasts, citing increasing risks to global supplies. The investment bank warned that Brent crude could climb to $140 per barrel in 2027 if oil production across the Gulf region remains significantly below its 2025 average.Also read | India in a 'sweet spot' amid oil volatility and currency dynamics: Kotak Neo's Anindya BanerjeeIn an upside scenario, Brent crude could reach $140 per barrel and average around $130 in 2027 if Gulf oil production remains 3.5 million barrels per day below its 2025 average, Reuters reported, citing Goldman Sachs' projections.Goldman Sachs expects oil markets to incorporate a higher geopolitical risk premium, given the possibility of disruptions to Middle Eastern supplies, the historical duration of major supply shocks and the challenges involved in securing a lasting diplomatic breakthrough.JPMorgan analysts also highlighted the uncertainty surrounding the conflict, saying it remained difficult to predict how the war would unfold. At the outset, the bank had expected the US administration to avoid crossing certain economic thresholds. Indians buy 30% more gold after recent price correction
items.summary: Kolkata: Indians stepped up purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period despite elevated prices, with gold buying rising 30% by volume and silver demand increasing 10% over the same period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said this signalled a revival of demand ahead of the crucial wedding season.As per the industry body, consumers bought 52 tonnes of gold worth ₹72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at ₹5,400 crore during this year's Dhanteras-Diwali. The surge came after gold prices corrected from a peak of around ₹1.8 lakh to ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams, encouraging buyers to return to the market. Advance purchases for the wedding season, which begins in mid-November and continues until March, also contributed to the increase.135751520"Jewellers have made good business in this year's Dhanteras and Diwali," said IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta.There was a pent-up demand in the market, after many consumers had earlier halted purchases following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's appeal not to buy gold, he said. "Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing ."The timing of the festivals also supported purchases, with Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8, both at the beginning of the month when most salaried people receive their salaries and festive bonus."This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment," said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council. This fiscal year till September, gold sales by volume fell by almost 50% due to price and import duty increase, and PM Modi's call to avoid purchase of gold.Read more: Smallcap mutual fund inflows drop 29% MoM to Rs 6,407 crore in October. Should investors be cautious or continue investing?Gold has delivered substantial returns over the past few years, with prices rising from around ₹60,000 per 10 gm in 2023 to ₹80,000 in 2024, ₹1.15-1.20 lakh in 2025 and about ₹1.42 lakh this year during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Silver too has witnessed significant appreciation. An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers shows that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third highest in a decade, despite prices being around 10% higher than a year ago."The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period," said C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers director C Vinod Hayagriv.Read more: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on ThursdayNatural diamond also demonstrated resilience, recording their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer reported a 250% rise in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras and a 47% rise during the Diwali season. This comes amid turbulence in the natural diamond industry due to global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and growing competition from lab-grown alternatives. Lab-grown diamonds are emerging as an additional category rather than replacing natural diamonds.

items.title: Debt Mutual Funds: What investors should know before investing
items.summary: Debt mutual funds saw a net outflow of Rs 1.8 lakh crore in September, the highest monthly withdrawal in the first half of FY27. Despite this, they remain an important investment avenue for investors looking to park surplus money, manage short-term goals and diversify their portfolios. A look at how debt funds work and what investors should know before investing.WHAT ARE DEBT MUTUAL FUNDS?Debt mutual funds invest in fixed-income instruments such as government securities, treasury bills, corporate bonds, commercial paper and certificates of deposit. They aim to provide relatively stable returns while taking lower risk than equity funds. Debt funds generate returns in two ways. The first is through the interest earned on the bonds and other securities held in the portfolio. The second comes from changes in bond prices. When bond prices rise, fund managers can book gains by selling these securities.HOW SHOULD INVESTORS CHOOSE A DEBT FUND? The choice depends on the investment horizon, liquidity needs and ability to tolerate fluctuations in returns. Investors looking to park money for a few days or months may consider overnight or liquid funds. Those with a horizon of six months to two years may look at ultra-short duration, low duration or money-market funds. For investment horizons of three years or more, categories such as short-duration funds, corporate bond funds and banking & PSU debt funds may be suitable. Gilt funds and long-duration funds are generally more appropriate for investors who understand interest-rate cycles.Read more: Smallcap mutual fund inflows drop 29% MoM to Rs 6,407 crore in October. Should investors be cautious or continue investing?WHY DID DEBT FUNDS WITNESS LARGE OUTFLOWS IN SEPTEMBER? The large outflows were largely driven by liquidity requirements rather than a change in investor appetite for debt funds. These schemes are widely used by companies and institutional investors to park surplus cash for short periods. September is also a quarter-end month when companies usually withdraw money to meet working capital requirements, advance tax payments and other financial obligations.Read more: Debt mutual funds see sharp recovery in October as quarter-end outflows reverseARE DEBT FUNDS RISK-FREE? While debt funds are generally less volatile than equity funds, they are not risk-free. One key risk is interest-rate risk. When interest rates rise, bond prices fall, which can affect the value of a fund’s portfolio. The second is credit risk, which arises when a company or other issuer fails to repay its debt or interest on time. Funds investing in lower-rated corporate bonds generally carry higher credit risk.HOW DO INTEREST RATES AFFECT DEBT FUND RETURNS? Interest rates and bond prices move in opposite directions. When interest rates fall, existing bonds offering higher interest become more attractive to investors. As demand for these bonds rises, their prices generally move up. This, in turn, tends to benefit debt funds. When interest rates rise, bond prices usually decline, which can weigh on returns. Long-duration funds are usually more affected by interest-rate changes, while liquid and overnight funds tend to see smaller fluctuations.

items.summary: The S&P 500 and the tech-heavy Nasdaq rose more than 1% on Wednesday after strong earnings from neocloud company CoreWeave eased concerns about excessive spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Nvidia also recovered some ground following a sharp two-session sell-off.The S&P 500 gained 96.91 points, or 1.29%, to end at 7,617.84 points, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 398.70 points, or 1.59%, to 25,464.57. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 245.03 points, or 0.47%, to 52,476.92.Battered CoreWeave shares surged more than 20% to the highest intraday level in nearly two weeks. The company said it would become profitable in the first half of 2028 on an adjusted basis, seeking to reassure investors that strong demand and customer commitments could support its debt-fueled expansion.The results lifted other AI infrastructure stocks, with Nebius Group climbing 17.4% and Applied Digital gaining 8.6%.Nvidia rose 3.8% after losing about $430 billion in market value over the previous two sessions. Its shares had come under pressure amid reports concerning CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a businesswoman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 7% to a one-week high. Marvell Technology surged 12.2%, while Micron Technology gained 13.3%.Equity markets have swung sharply this week as concerns about slower data-centre development, higher interest rates and uncertainty surrounding Nvidia compete with investors’ appetite to buy the dip.Investors purchased equities during last week’s sell-off, with all net inflows coming through exchange-traded funds and institutional clients leading the buying, Bank of America Global Research analysts said in a note.“We’ve seen some of the leverage getting washed out post the midterms, which could set us up for a constructive year-end rally,” said Ron Albahary, chief investment officer at Laird Norton Wetherby.Six of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors traded higher, led by technology and energy.The CBOE Volatility Index, widely known as Wall Street’s fear gauge, declined for a fourth consecutive session to 17.7.Investors also assessed the terms of Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering. The Claude chatbot developer is seeking a valuation of as much as $1.4 trillion.“There’s a lot of optimistic expectations related to Anthropic’s business ... any disappointment related to earnings growth, which has been outsized, could cause a selloff within the AI trade itself,” Albahary said.Rate concerns persistHotter-than-expected inflation data released on Tuesday strengthened expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates next month. Traders now fully price in a December increase, according to CME FedWatch.Before the CPI report, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers should consider raising rates by 50 basis points if October inflation accelerated. He warned that a smaller move could damage the central bank’s inflation-fighting credibility.Oil prices rose 2.8% after Iran’s security chief said Tehran would not allow enriched nuclear material to leave the country.The US bond market was closed on Wednesday for Veterans Day.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Tata Electronics in talks to raise $2 bn
items.summary: Mumbai: Tata Group's semiconductor business is in initial discussions with domestic and international banks to raise up to $2 billion through multiple loan tranches to fund its expansion plans, according to people familiar with the discussions.The first tranche is likely to be up to $800 million, with initial pricing discussions around SOFR plus 180 basis points. The talks are at an early stage, with the final size, pricing and lender participation yet to be firmed up. The loan could be priced at around 6%, assuming SOFR remains at around 3.9%.Also Read: Life insurers post 26 pc growth in new business premiums to Rs 42,914 crore in OctoberA Tata spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.135747359Tata Electronics, a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Sons, has signed a definitive agreement with Taiwan-based Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing Corporation (PSMC) for its proposed semiconductor fabrication plant in Dholera, Gujarat. The agreement will enable Tata Electronics to bring semiconductor manufacturing technology and expertise to India and cater to global customers, the company said.Also Read: When every bank has an app, what actually makes digital banking different?The plant is being developed with a planned capacity of 50,000 wafer starts per month, with PSMC serving as its technology partner, India Ratings said in a report.The project, estimated to cost ₹91,000 crore, will manufacture 12-inch wafers using technology nodes ranging from 28 nm to 110 nm for applications such as power management chips and microcontrollers. It will be funded through equity, long-term debt and capital subsidies from the central and Gujarat governments under their respective semiconductor incentive schemes, the rating agency said.Tata Electronics' liquidity is supported by unencumbered cash balances of ₹2,845 crore at the end of FY25, up from ₹1,485 crore a year earlier, timely equity infusions and its ability to raise working capital limits and long-term debt. The company had debt repayment obligations of ₹1,297 crore in FY27 towards term loans and external commercial borrowings as of September 30, 2025, the rating agency said.

items.title: CoreWeave shares surge over 26%, spark rally in battered AI cloud stocks
items.summary: CoreWeave shares surged more than 26% on Wednesday, fuelling a rally in battered AI cloud stocks after heavy infrastructure spending delivered strong revenue growth and the company signalled a retreat from the borrowing spree that had raised fears of an artificial intelligence bubble, Reuters reported.CoreWeave shares were trading at $61.61, up $12.88 or 26.43% over the previous close.The results also helped lift Nvidia, a major CoreWeave backer, by 2%. Nvidia had fallen sharply over the previous two sessions amid uncertainty surrounding CEO Jensen Huang following reports about his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to have ties to Beijing’s intelligence apparatus.Shares of other so-called neocloud companies, including Nebius and Iren, also rallied after weeks of pressure. Investors have worried that their debt-funded data-centre expansion could backfire if demand for AI computing weakens.For live updates on US Markets, click here“CoreWeave’s earnings directly addressed the fear that’s driven this whole selloff,” said Dan Sheehan, director of portfolio management at Telos Wealth Advisors, according to Reuters. “The neocloud that became the poster child for AI financing worries took real weight off the fear that had been the heart of the selloff.”Democrats’ sweep of last week’s US midterm elections had further unsettled the industry. Several victorious candidates campaigned for stricter regulation and moratoriums on new data-centre construction, including in Texas, a key market for the sector.CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told Reuters on Tuesday that increased regulatory scrutiny could slow data-centre development across the industry. However, he did not expect it to significantly affect the company’s expansion plans or raise costs.Intrator said CoreWeave’s planned capacity additions over the next year would remain unaffected.Also Read: Is AI wheel broken? Julius Baer flags 3 variables shaping AI investments ahead of Anthropic IPOThe company also said it would avoid unsecured debt markets following a recent surge in borrowing costs. Cash flow from existing contracts would cover repayments on both current and future debt, it added—a financing plan analysts described as credible.“CoreWeave delivered about the best quarter we could have asked for. Stats were good-to-great, funding concerns were addressed and the strategic moves make sense,” Bernstein analysts led by Madison Rezaei said in a client note.However, they warned that CoreWeave “will be among the first and hardest hit” once the shortage of AI computing capacity eases.The risks of mistiming AI investments were evident on Tuesday when SoftBank recorded a $3.7 billion write-down on non-refundable payments for equipment intended to power its US data centres. The charge contributed to a second-quarter net loss of $7 billion, the company’s first in nearly two years.Uncertainty surrounding Huang has also weighed on the AI sector. The controversy intensified on Tuesday after reports alleged that his relationship helped facilitate billions of dollars in Nvidia chip shipments to China.Republican US Senator Kevin Cramer, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, called on Huang to step down as Nvidia CEO.For now, CoreWeave’s results have given AI infrastructure investors some relief. Nebius, Iren, Oracle and Applied Digital climbed between 6% and 14%.With the exception of Nebius, the stocks had fallen between 32% and 48% this year through Tuesday. Nebius, by contrast, had gained 60%.Together, the companies—including CoreWeave—were on track to add about $36 billion in market value if the gains held. Nvidia alone was positioned to gain nearly $100 billion.Nebius is scheduled to report its results before Thursday’s opening bell.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

He pointed to the cryptocurrency breaking above its bear market trendline and 200-day moving average before returning to test that average, as per a Benzinga report.He said similar movements appeared during the 2014-2015 and 2018-2019 cycles. So Warren believes the current market is showing a comparable setup.Investor sentiment, meanwhile, has weakened. He described these as "fair value gap zones".A decline towards $68,400 would not necessarily change his constructive outlook. He stopped following the model around 18 months ago after the current cycle's low arrived in July rather than October, which was the timing the model had suggested.He believes institutional capital now has a greater influence on Bitcoin's price movements than halving-related supply changes.Bitcoin ETF outflows fall for a third consecutive dayThe latest ETF figures show that investors are still pulling money from Bitcoin funds, although the pace of withdrawals has eased.US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $95 million in net outflows on November 10, according to Farside data cited by Cryptopolitan. items.title: Nvidia rebounds after $480 billion wipeout
items.summary: Nvidia stock (NVDA) surged nearly 4% in premarket trading on Wednesday, November 11, as investors bought the dip after a two-day sell-off that wiped roughly $480 billion from the chipmaker's market value. Shares rose to $175.45 at 6:49 a.m. ET, up 3.88%, after closing Tuesday at $168.89, down $9.78, or 5.47%.The rebound came alongside gains in US stock futures, with Nasdaq 100 futures rising 1.67%, S&P 500 futures gaining 0.74% and Dow futures edging up 0.03%.Investors are returning to AI stocks even as Nvidia faces an investigation involving CEO Jensen Huang, just six days before its November 17 earnings report.Why is Nvidia stock rising today after a $480 billion market value crash?Nvidia's rebound comes after two difficult trading sessions. Shares fell 4.3% on Monday and another 5.47% on Tuesday as investors reacted to reports about Huang's relationship with a woman suspected by US intelligence of having links to Chinese intelligence.The stock closed Monday at $178.67 before falling to $168.89 on Tuesday. Wednesday's premarket recovery has helped Nvidia regain part of those losses, although shares remain below their level before the controversy intensified.The recovery is also part of a broader rally in AI stocks. CoreWeave shares gained more than 10% in premarket trading after its quarterly results helped ease concerns about AI infrastructure spending. Micron and Marvell also rose nearly 7%.Nvidia faces Jensen Huang investigation as board hires outside law firmNvidia confirmed on Tuesday that its independent directors had hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate whether company secrets or US national security had been compromised.The investigation will be led by former acting US Attorney Joon H. Kim.The company had already announced an independent review on Sunday. Nvidia's board said it had no reason to believe that company secrets or national security had been compromised. It also expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team.The allegations remain unproven, and China has denied claims of an espionage operation.Huang returned to Nvidia's office on Monday and continued holding meetings on Tuesday, according to CNBC. His return comes as investors assess whether the controversy could affect Nvidia's operations or leadership.Bank of America warns Nvidia could face three different outcomesBank of America outlined three possible scenarios for Nvidia in a research note on Tuesday.The first involves a contained investigation with no major disruption to leadership. Under this outcome, investor attention could return to Nvidia's earnings and AI chip demand.The second involves prolonged uncertainty that puts pressure on the company's valuation ahead of its quarterly results.The third carries greater financial risks. Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya warned that adverse findings, leadership changes or tighter restrictions could require investors to reassess Nvidia's earnings outlook.Morgan Stanley removes Nvidia stock from top picks after 25% declineMorgan Stanley removed Nvidia from its top stock picks on Wednesday after shares dropped more than 25% since the bank added the company to its list on October 2.The bank's analysts said Huang's leadership remains crucial to Nvidia's strategic direction.The decision adds to concerns about how much Nvidia's market valuation depends on its chief executive.Zacks Chief Equity Strategist John Blank also warned that investors were concerned about possible additional US restrictions and further developments in the investigation.Speaking to CNBC, Blank said the situation was negative for Nvidia, Huang and the broader AI trade.Nvidia earnings on November 17: Can NVDA stock sustain its recovery?Nvidia's next quarterly earnings report is scheduled for November 17, giving investors another major event to watch.The market will focus on revenue growth, AI chip demand, profit margins and the company's guidance for the coming quarter.

items.title: UK firm to invest 250 mln pounds in India
items.summary: New Delhi, UK-based business financial platform Tide plans to invest around 250 million pounds (about Rs 3,100 crore) in India by the end of 2030 to scale up operations and technology centres supporting its global business.The company plans to ramp up investment up to 500 million pounds in the longer term.India will remain an important part of its global operations, with investments focused on strengthening its operations and technology centres that support its businesses in the UK and Europe, Tide said in a statement.Tide employs around 800 people at its centre of excellence in Hyderabad across functions such as member support, product and engineering.The Hyderabad centre accounts for nearly one-third of the company's total workforce and drives its core operations, engineering and product innovation, it said, adding that the company also intends to advance its operations centre in Delhi, which supports its UK and European businesses.However, it said, following a detailed strategic review, Tide concluded that the economics of its India member-facing business did not offer a viable path to sustainable profitability, despite having grown to more than one million members in the country since December 2022.It will, therefore, focus its investments on the UK and European markets, where it sees greater potential for profitable growth at scale.The decision to wind down the India member-facing business will affect around 400 employees, it said.The company would support the affected employees during the transition, including offering transfers to its global operations and technology centres wherever possible, it said, adding that the company will also communicate directly with its members in India regarding the implications of the decision.Tide Chief Executive Officer Oliver Prill said India remained an integral part of the company's global business and long-term growth plans.The company has built a significant operations and technology presence in India and intends to continue expanding these capabilities, he said in the statement.Prill said the decision to exit the member-facing business followed a strategic review which found that the economics of the proposition did not provide a sustainable path to profitability, particularly compared with opportunities in the UK and Europe.Tide expects its annualised revenue run rate to exceed USD 500 million in the coming months.The UK remains its largest and most established market, where the company is profitable and approaching one million small and medium enterprise (SME) members, equivalent to around 16 per cent of the market.It also plans to leverage artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiency, enhance its products and provide better support to members.

Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) and Ola Electric Mobility emerged among the top gainers in the sector, with the former leading the rally with an intra-day gain of nearly 5%.M&M climbed 4.81% to touch an intra-day high of Rs 3,449, while Ola Electric Mobility advanced 3.53% to Rs 35.16.Hyundai Motor India was another major gainer, rising 3.08% to an intra-day high of Rs 2,175, while TVS Motor Company gained 2.89% to Rs 4,636.10. Ather Energy advanced 2.40% to Rs 1,904.50.Among other automobile companies, Maruti Suzuki India rose 2.10% to Rs 13,199, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles gained 2.03% to Rs 301. JBM Auto advanced 2% to Rs 511.95, while Bajaj Auto registered the lowest gain among the nine stocks, rising 1.28% to Rs 11,120.At the last check, M&M was trading 4.5% higher, followed by TVS Motor Company, which was up 2.53%. Ola Electric Mobility gained 2.20%, while Hyundai Motor India advanced 2.3%. Maruti Suzuki India was up 2%, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Ather Energy gained 1.5% each. Bajaj Auto and JBM Auto were trading 0.5% higher each, while Ashok Leyland was flat.ALSO READ: Earnings recovery, FII revival: 5 factors that will shape Dalal Street's next move after Q2What does the Centre's new EV procurement policy say?The Department of Expenditure (DEA), under the Ministry of Finance, has revised the Net Dealer Price (NDP) ceiling for the procurement of staff cars by government ministries and departments, doubling the limit for electric vehicles to Rs 20 lakh from Rs 10 lakh for internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles.Under the revised instructions, electric vehicles have been made the default choice for government staff-car procurement. Ministries and departments are directed to ordinarily procure EVs when purchasing or replacing their existing staff cars.However, the revised instructions do not completely prohibit the purchase of conventional vehicles. items.summary: Tehran: Iran's army said Wednesday that an oil tanker had struck a mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, where the country has been targeting ships that transit without its authorisation.Since the outbreak of the Middle East war in late February, Tehran has heavily restricted traffic through the strategic waterway, insisting vessels use routes authorised by the Islamic republic.The United States has in response imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports and helped tankers travel the strait, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil.The American military recently claimed all mines had been cleared from the strait."Early this morning, a violating oil tanker caught fire after striking a naval mine in an unsafe, prohibited area in the east of the Strait of Hormuz," the naval forces of Iran's army said in a statement carried by state TV.In recent weeks Tehran has made multiple announcements saying ships had caught fire in the strait, often claiming they struck mines.US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the region, has been escorting ships through the waterway and said last month that it had helped Gulf countries export 1.5 billion barrels of oil via Hormuz since the summer.On Tuesday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, the ideological arm of Iran's military, said three other oil tankers had caught fire in the strait.

items.title: Michael Burry calls Nvidia 'heck of a trade' after Huang’s scandal sparks $430 bn selloff. Why is Big Short fame dismissing fears?
items.summary: Michael Burry is known for his bearish take on artificial intelligence-linked stocks, but the ‘Big Short’ investor dismissed worries around Nvidia following the controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang’s extramarital affair, calling the chipmaker a “heck of a trade”.The popular American investor sees potential for a near-term trading opportunity in Nvidia but doubts the controversy surrounding CEO Jensen Huang will damage Nvidia's business much. "Still, I believe Nvidia's competitive advantage will shrink over the next five years," he said. While Burry struck a positive note for Nvidia, he is not exactly bullish on the chipmaker. He is not tempted to make a long-term trade on the stock, but he feels the entire market will soon think it is a “heck of a trade.”Also read | Nvidia Stock Sell-Off Deepens: Spy scandal, price target cuts put AI giant under pressureAll about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair controversy Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang openly admitted that he has been in an intimate relationship with a business executive whom US intelligence reportedly alleged was a Chinese spy, leading to the company launching an investigation into the reports. This has led to a sharp selloff in Nvidia shares, wiping out around $430 billion from its market value in just two sessions.Huang, in a message to company employees released on Sunday, acknowledged having an affair and apologised to both his family and company staff. "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” the 63-year-old Taiwanese-born executive said.Also read | Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces leadership questions as Republican senator calls for his resignationMichael Burry takes U-turn on Nvidia?Notably, Michael Burry had been shorting Nvidia shares until September, when he announced that he is exiting some of the put options. Put options typically reflect a trader’s conviction that the stock price is about to fall. Burry had long held put options on a variety of stocks which remained the face of the AI boom, spooking investors about a possible market crash when the artificial intelligence frenzy fizzles out. The American investor later exited some of the put options, triggering some optimism, but Burry clarified that it was not his intention.Burry said he sold his December 2026 puts on both Nvidia and Palantir entirely to avoid rapid time-based decay. He added that he did not replace or roll the positions, saying he is "pulling back on exposures across the portfolio." Michael Burry's AI warningsThe American investor who famously correctly predicted the 2008 US housing crisis has been sounding the alarm since the beginning of the year over a prospective big market crash when the AI frenzy fizzles out. Earlier this year, Burry said he continues to believe that the market is close to a major top, warning of a similar crash to that of 1987 when Dow Jones recorded a historic 23% plunge, which led to the introduction of regulatory circuit breakers. However, the market investor noted that the S&P 500 making new highs likely will bring new money into the market.He wrote in a Substack post that he sees many indicators, both technical and fundamental, lining up for the same conclusion as the Dotcom crash. "1999 went where no market had gone before, and I would say so can this one...It is already there on several indicators," he said, arguing that massive venture capital flows, rising AI debt issuance, and extreme market optimism are creating conditions where valuations may detach from economic reality.Also read | Anthropic retracts details of $69 billion IPO filing sent to bankers. Why analysts are raising worries over valuationsBurry’s popular bet against the housing market was depicted in the 2015 movie titled 'The Big Short', which starred Christian Bale, Ryan Gosling, Steve Carell and others.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Moody's Ratings on Wednesday said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience.
In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to "intensifying and broadening price pressures", with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6 per cent target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.
"India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7 per cent from 6.5 per cent," it said.

items.title: Hijack threat note found on Air India flight, plane taken to isolation bay
items.summary:
A hijack threat note found in the washroom of a Mumbai-bound Air India flight before take-off on Wednesday morning prompted security officials to park the aircraft in an isolation bay of the airport here, an official said.
The flight was scheduled to depart at 10.20 am.
The note threatening that the plane would be hijacked at 11.10 am was found in the washroom just before the departure of the flight, Kolkata airport director Vikram Singh said.
All the passengers who had boarded the aircraft were deboarded, and it was taken to the isolation bay, he said.
Security protocols were immediately activated, and the aircraft was moved to an isolation bay for a thorough inspection and necessary precautionary measures, he said.

items.title: China builds inside Europe's walls
items.summary: Sofia: China doesn't need to clear Europe's trade barriers. It can build inside them.Chinese companies are establishing production and supplier networks across Central and Eastern Europe, which could enable them to gain more control over the technologies and inputs that European manufacturing needs.China is increasingly challenging the European Union in the advanced manufacturing sectors that helped the EU weather the first China shock, which reshaped global manufacturing in the 2000s. Chinese firms are competing with the EU in chemicals, machinery, advanced equipment and autos - and increasingly coming out on top on both price and quality.The EU trade deficit with China has nearly quadrupled over the past decade, from around €100 billion in 2014 to over €370 billion in 2025, or roughly €1 billion a day, according to Eurostat data.France and Germany are seeking to push back with stronger trade defences, but import curbs will achieve little if Chinese investment, ownership and control of critical technologies recreates the same vulnerabilities inside the single market.LOOKING EASTCentral and Eastern Europe appear to be key to China's growth strategy in Europe.While the EU's trade deficit with China has hovered around 2% of EU gross domestic product (GDP) since 2014, it has risen sharply in parts of CEE. For example, Slovenia's goods deficit with China rose from 2.5% to 16% over that period. Meanwhile, Poland's goods deficit surged from €8.9 billion to €34.3 billion, equivalent to about 5.2% of GDP. The Czech Republic's deficit nearly quadrupled to €22 billion, or roughly 8% of GDP, and Hungary's tripled to €10.4 billion, or about 6% of GDP.Investment and corporate ties deepened that exposure. In 2025, Chinese foreign direct investment (FDI) flows into the EU approached €16.8 billion, and the cumulative value of Chinese investment in the bloc was about €95 billion, according to Eurostat and Rhodium Group data.While most legacy Chinese FDI in Europe centered on Germany, France and the Benelux countries, the focus has shifted east in recent years. CEE has attracted more than half of Chinese FDI into the EU and Britain since 2021, according to an analysis by the Rhodium Group, with an even larger regional share when the Western Balkans are included. Hungary has attracted the largest share of new investment since the COVID-19 pandemic, hitting 44% in 2023 and 23% in 2025.The investment surge in CEE has largely been driven by mega-projects in the electric vehicle (EV) supply chain. Chinese EV and battery manufacturers CATL, BYD and Sunwoda are all establishing major Hungarian operations. Slovakia has attracted investment from Chinese battery tech firm Gotion, and will be the site of a new Volvo plant owned by the Chinese automaker Geely.Meanwhile, Serbia, which has significant steel and copper assets, has signed contracts with Chinese auto firms Minth , Shanghai Automotive Chassis (SHAC), BMTS Technology and Xingyu Automotive, envisaging around €1 billion in investment and nearly 1,700 car-parts jobs, according to the government. The deals also include a new robotics factory in Sabac, billed as Europe's first humanoid robot mass production base.These investments can create jobs, spur growth, and accelerate the energy transition, but they may also erode EU competitiveness over time. Outsourcing key advanced manufacturing technologies to Chinese entities risks deepening Europe's dependence on external supply chains and weakening domestic innovation and R&D.DEFEND, THEN COMPETEEurope is seeking to limit China's access to its consumer markets and industries, but the current Franco-German push for faster defensive trade action and tougher investment screening across the bloc appears to be too little too late.Europe's flagship proposal, the Industrial Accelerator Act, leaves manufacturers' key competitiveness gaps unaddressed. Moreover, its screening mechanism would largely leave unexamined Chinese control via ultimate ownership, foreign subsidies and supply-chain concentration - some key issues when looking at CEE's growing dependence.There is also the problem of fragmentation across the bloc. Investment deals might be in one country's interest but could weaken the bloc's collective negotiating position with Beijing. To address this, the continent would likely need a permanent European economic security coordination mechanism to unite trade, competition and national screening authorities that could identify risks before investments become irreversible.Yet the chances of forming such a body at a time of growing political fragmentation within EU countries seem slim.And, ultimately, protectionism can only get Europe so far. It cannot compensate for the region's structural problems, including expensive energy, fragmented capital markets and slow industrial innovation. For that, the region would likely need to create a true energy union and invest in technological innovation. Building trade walls buys time, but not true change.(The views expressed here are those of Martin Vladimirov, director of the Geoeconomics Program of the Center for the Study of Democracy (CSD))

items.title: Dubai-bound tanker hit in Gulf; Indians injured
items.summary: A Dubai-bound oil tanker carrying six Indian seafarers was hit by a projectile while transiting the Persian Gulf on Tuesday, leaving four crew members injured, including one Indian national, the government said on Wednesday.Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal identified the vessel as the Liberian-flagged very large crude carrier (VLCC) MT Fujairah Energy, which was travelling from Al Ruwais to Dubai."The remaining 18 crew members, including five other Indian seafarers, are safe and accounted for," Sonowal said on X.— sarbanandsonwal (@sarbanandsonwal) He even added that the government was in contact with the ship management company to ensure medical assistance and the safety of the affected seafarers."We are continuously monitoring the situation and remain in close contact with the ship management company to ensure the ongoing security, medical care and wellbeing of our seafarers," he wrote on X.The incident adds to concerns over the safety of commercial shipping and Indian seafarers in the Persian Gulf and surrounding waters, where vessels have faced repeated attacks.Last month, a Panama-flagged tanker, MT Louise 1, carrying 27 Indian seafarers was hit by limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz, triggering a fire. The incident occurred 25 nautical miles (46 km) northeast of Oman's Khasab. The government subsequently confirmed that all Indian crew members were safe.Shipping routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, have faced disruptions and attacks since the Iran-US war began in February 2026.According to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the conflict began. US forces are also continuing to enforce a naval blockade of Iranian ports, adding to tensions in the region.
