items.title: Nvidia CEO's secret affair has a hidden angle
items.summary: The allegations on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang being targeted by a Chinese intelligence operation have brought a critical US national security concern into focus: whether access to one of America's most influential technology executives could have been used to gather sensitive information on its AI capabilities, semiconductor supply chains and strategy to maintain its lead over China.US intelligence agencies reportedly believe that Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman and former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed, was gathering information for Beijing after developing a close relationship with Jensen Huang. The Financial Times, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security.Also read: I was unfaithful to my wife: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admits secret affair with Chinese spy Alice HuangWhile the allegations have not been independently established publicly, the potential national security implications are significant. Nvidia is a leading supplier of the advanced processors used to train and run AI models, and its technology has become central to America's efforts to maintain an advantage over China in artificial intelligence.The company's board has initiated an independent investigation, saying it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. However, the episode has prompted lawmakers to seek answers about the company's safeguards against foreign intelligence operations.Why is Nvidia so important to America's AI and military ambitions?Nvidia's importance extends beyond its position as one of the world's largest semiconductor companies. Its graphics processing units (GPUs) are used to train and operate advanced AI models, making them a critical part of the computing infrastructure underpinning the AI industry.The technology also has potential military and intelligence applications, including in autonomous systems, surveillance, cyber operations and other advanced defence capabilities.This is why access to advanced AI processors has become a strategic issue in the US-China rivalry. Washington has maintained restrictions on exports of its most advanced AI chips to China since 2022, citing concerns that the technology could accelerate Beijing's military modernisation.The stakes were highlighted in January, when former White House national security adviser Matt Pottinger told a congressional hearing that allowing Nvidia's H200 processors to be sold to China could strengthen Beijing's capabilities in areas ranging from nuclear weapons and cyber warfare to autonomous drones and intelligence operations, according to Reuters.The controversy involving Huang therefore raises a broader question: could access to the leadership of a company at the centre of America's AI infrastructure provide a foreign intelligence agency with information valuable to its technological and strategic ambitions?Also read: China dismisses 'Chinese spy' narrative in Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang probe; calls it 'unsubstantiated'Could China have gained access to sensitive US technology or business information?One of the central concerns surrounding the reported intelligence operation is the possibility that proximity to Nvidia's CEO could have provided access to information about the company's technology, business strategy, customers and future product plans.The New York Times reported that US intelligence agencies believed Alice Huang's relationship with Jensen Huang could have provided her with insights into Trump's thinking on artificial intelligence.Nvidia has maintained that its cloud customers in Asia receive ordinary business information, not sensitive trade secrets or information related to US national security.Its board has also said it has no reason to believe that company secrets or national security were compromised.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?Could the alleged operation have implications for US semiconductor export policy?Another important dimension is the potential access to information about Washington's semiconductor export restrictions and the discussions surrounding them.The US has sought to limit China's access to advanced AI processors, arguing that the technology could strengthen its military and intelligence capabilities.Nvidia, meanwhile, has a commercial interest in maintaining access to the Chinese market and has sought permission to sell certain advanced processors there.The Financial Times reported that US national security officials had privately expressed frustration with Huang over his efforts to persuade Trump to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to Chinese customers.The New York Times also reported that the relationship between Huang and Alice Huang could have provided her with insights into Trump's thinking on AI.This has raised questions about whether an intelligence operation targeting a senior technology executive could potentially provide information about US policy discussions, export restrictions and the positions of influential decision-makers.Megaspeed's involvement may raise supply chain concernsThe connection to Megaspeed adds another layer to the national security concerns.The Singapore-based data centre company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology companies.According to The New York Times report, Megaspeed had bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years. The company has also come under US scrutiny over allegations that its network may have helped Chinese businesses access advanced AI processors restricted from export to China.The concern for Washington is that overseas data centres and intermediaries could potentially provide Chinese companies with access to computing resources powered by restricted American technology.The Financial Times also stated that a sister company in Malaysia bought at least $4.8 billion of advanced AI equipment containing Nvidia technology between June 2024 and February 2026.In a Reuters column, Robyn Mak on Monday noted that Chinese technology companies have legally accessed processors restricted in mainland China through overseas data centres operated by neocloud providers such as Megaspeed. Mak also pointed to US investigations into suspected illegal chip-smuggling operations through Southeast Asia.The allegations therefore bring two national security concerns into focus: the possibility of foreign intelligence gathering around a major US technology company and the challenge of preventing restricted semiconductor technology from reaching Chinese customers through overseas supply chains.Could the controversy prompt tighter US export controls?The allegations could increase pressure on Washington to strengthen oversight of Nvidia's sales channels and the movement of advanced AI processors through third countries. US authorities have already been examining whether overseas companies and data centres are being used to circumvent restrictions on semiconductor exports to China.The controversy could intensify scrutiny of customer verification, the end-use of advanced chips and the role of intermediaries in the global AI computing supply chain.The issue is particularly sensitive as the Trump administration has been weighing how to balance US chipmakers' commercial interests against concerns about China's access to advanced AI technology.In December, Trump announced that the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors to China under conditions that included a 25% fee for the US government. Regulations subsequently introduced requirements for third-party testing, customer security procedures and restrictions on the volume of chips that could be exported.The decision had already drawn criticism from China hawks in Washington, who argued that such sales could strengthen Beijing's military capabilities.Mak argued that the fallout could ultimately hurt China's AI ambitions more than it helps if Washington comes under pressure to tighten enforcement and close existing workarounds.Why are US lawmakers seeking answers from Huang?The national security implications have prompted congressional scrutiny.Three Republican committee chairmen — Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, John Moolenaar of the China Select Committee and Eric Crawford of the Intelligence Committee — have asked Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on November 18.In their November 4 letter, the lawmakers sought answers about his reported interactions with Alice Huang and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.They said the allegations raised significant national security concerns about China's access to sensitive US technology and information.Separately, Democratic Senator Chris Coons has pledged to investigate the reported links between the Trump administration, Chinese intelligence and major AI industry executives, according to the Financial Times.The congressional inquiry could examine not just the reported relationship but also the extent to which Nvidia's customer interactions, information-sharing practices and security procedures protect sensitive American technology.What is at stake for the US-China AI race?The controversy comes as Washington and Beijing compete for leadership in artificial intelligence, an area often viewed as strategically important for economic competitiveness, military capabilities and technological influence.The US has sought to retain its advantage through restrictions on advanced semiconductor exports, while China has been working to develop domestic alternatives and secure access to computing resources.Nvidia occupies a particularly important position in this competition because its processors power a substantial part of the global AI infrastructure.Reuters columnist Mak noted that heightened scrutiny could accelerate the shift among Chinese companies towards domestic alternatives, including chips developed by Huawei and smaller competitors. However, the columnist also argued that tighter US restrictions could make it harder for Chinese technology companies to access advanced computing resources through overseas data centres.The controversy thus has implications beyond Nvidia. Any tightening of export controls or greater restrictions on overseas access to American AI processors could affect the pace at which Chinese companies develop and deploy advanced AI systems.Nvidia's board has initiated an independent investigation, overseen by independent directors and external legal counsel, where Huang has agreed to cooperate with the inquiry. The board has said it has no reason to believe that US national security or Nvidia's trade secrets were compromised.The US intelligence assessment concerning Alice Huang has not been publicly substantiated through disclosed evidence. China has rejected the espionage allegations as groundless speculation.The investigation and the congressional scrutiny will therefore be important in establishing whether any sensitive information was accessed, what information may have been sought and whether Nvidia's security protocols need to be strengthened.For Washington, the larger issue is how to protect the technology, expertise and supply chains underpinning its AI advantage at a time when competition with China is increasingly becoming a national security priority.

Dissolved oxygen levels in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean (ISSO) have significantly risen over the past three decades, even as oceans elsewhere are showing the trend of declining oxygen levels, a study by scientists at a Goa-based institute has found.
The scientists attributed the oxygenation primarily to enhanced ocean ventilation - the process through which surface waters are mixed and transported into the ocean interior, replenishing oxygen at greater depths.
Oxygenation in the ISSO intensified between 1993 and 2025, particularly in the Polar and Antarctic zones, as per the study conducted by researchers from the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa.
The findings stand in contrast to the broader trend of declining oxygen levels in oceans worldwide, which scientists have linked to global warming, increased ocean stratification and weakening circulation.

items.title: All about Nvidia CEO Huang's affair controversy
items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship with a business executive suspected by US intelligence of gathering information for Beijing, as the chipmaker's board launched an independent investigation into reports that its founder was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. While Huang has apologised to his family and company employees saying he was ‘unfaithful’ to his wife, Nvidia said it has no reason to believe that US national security or the company's secrets were compromised.US President Donald Trump has defended Huang, describing him as an "honourable guy" who has done an "amazing job" for the country. Trump also expects Huang to remain at the helm of Nvidia, adding that the executive deserved to have his side of the story heard.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?The controversy follows reports by The New York Times and the Financial Times that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between the Nvidia leader and Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she was gathering information for Beijing.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang issues key statementIn a draft email to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.”In a separate message reported by The New York Times, he apologised to his family and company employees, taking responsibility for his actions. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it," he wrote.Addressing Nvidia employees, Huang also acknowledged that he had fallen short of his responsibilities towards them. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence," he said.He also requested privacy for his family, saying they bore no responsibility for his choices.Huang has not directly addressed the allegations that the business executive, aka, the Chinese spy was gathering information for the country. He has, however, supported Nvidia's investigation and committed to cooperate with it.Also read: Nvidia opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang over affair with woman suspected of spying for ChinaNvidia announces independent investigationNvidia's board of directors announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by external independent legal counsel.In its statement, Nvidia said, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." The company added that the board prioritised US national and economic security, which it said was paramount to Nvidia and its shareholders.The board also expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team and said it would provide further updates as appropriate.Huang, 63, will continue as Nvidia CEO during the investigation, it clarified.Speaking on Huang meeting thousands of customer executives every year, the company previously said that it regularly receives updates from the US government regarding parties and entities of concern and acts accordingly.Trump defends Nvidia CEOTrump has publicly defended Huang amid the controversy, describing him as an honourable person and praising his contribution to the US."I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on," Trump told reporters. "I think he's an honourable guy," he said, adding that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country".When asked whether Huang should remain Nvidia's CEO, Trump replied: "I think so. Sure."Trump also suggested that Huang should be given an opportunity to explain himself. Asked whether he would take Huang on his planned trip to Asia, Trump said, "I don't know, but I'd certainly take him."The remarks came amid reports that Trump had been briefed on intelligence findings concerning Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman roughly a year ago but had chosen not to act on the information, according to The New York Times.The Financial Times separately reported that a US government memo based on intelligence information about the alleged relationship had been shared with a small group of senior US officials shortly before Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The FT also reported that Trump had held multiple meetings with Huang since beginning his second presidential term in 2025. Huang had personally lobbied Trump earlier this year to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to customers in China.Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese spy?Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese national and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company.According to The New York Times, Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a senior executive at Megaspeed. The company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology company Alibaba.US intelligence agencies reportedly concluded that Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang and was passing information directly to Beijing.The Financial Times reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main intelligence agency.Jensen Huang had previously described their association as a normal business relationship.Megaspeed and its connection to the Nvidia caseMegaspeed has come under US scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia's advanced AI chips may have been diverted to China.The New York Times reported that Megaspeed had been examined for potentially steering Nvidia AI chips to China. According to the publication, the firm bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years.The Financial Times reported that Megaspeed was spun off from a Chinese gaming company in 2023. US authorities have been investigating companies, particularly in Southeast Asia, suspected of helping China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export restrictions.Nvidia had previously launched an internal investigation into allegations concerning the diversion of chips through Megaspeed but assessed that there was no evidence of wrongdoing, according to the Financial Times.US lawmakers step up actionSenior Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives earlier asked Huang to brief Congress about the allegations and Nvidia's security protocols.In a letter dated November 4, Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, who leads the China Select Committee; and Eric Crawford, chairman of the Intelligence Committee, sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on November 18.The lawmakers sought answers about the New York Times report and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage. The letter said the allegations raised significant national security concerns regarding China's access to sensitive US technology and information.The lawmakers added that Congress needed to determine the extent to which US national security had been placed at risk.Meanwhile, Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat who is due to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee from January, pledged to open an investigation."Congress will investigate and get answers," Coons wrote on X, referring to what he described as the relationship between the Trump administration, Chinese spies and AI billionaires.Political and corporate reactions to Jensen Huang affairUS Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on the allegations when asked about the report, describing it as an "internal corporate matter", according to AFP.Technology analyst Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives described the investigation as a "black eye moment" for Huang. Ives said the controversy could trigger multiple congressional inquiries and create an overhang on Nvidia's stock.He also warned that the development could increase scrutiny of the company's chip sales to China, which remains a key issue in Washington.Huang's position at Nvidia could also come under scrutiny depending on the outcome of the board's investigation, Ives said, adding that the CEO's importance to the company's global strategy made the controversy a risk for the stock.Separately, Elon Musk responded to a social media post about the controversy. The post suggested that while Huang had done something incredibly foolish, there might have been no malicious intention. Musk replied, "I agree."Nvidia stock downNvidia shares came under pressure in out-of-hours trading following the announcement of the board investigation.Perpetual futures trading on the Hyperliquid exchange and after-hours shares trading on the Blue Ocean system showed Nvidia shares at around $180.30 on Monday, down approximately 3.4% from Friday's Nasdaq closing price of $186.64.The development has raised concerns about the potential impact of the controversy on investor sentiment, particularly given Huang's importance to Nvidia's business and its global AI strategy.South Korean govt intervenes in Nvidia CEO caseSouth Korea stated that Nvidia's contracted GPU deliveries to the country are expected to proceed without disruption despite the controversy surrounding Huang.Vice Science Minister Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee on Monday that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use. GPUs planned for 2026 were under contract and expected to enter service this year."We expect production and the delivery schedule for contracted volumes to proceed without disruption," Ryu said, adding that the ministry was monitoring developments and discussing prices and schedules with Nvidia Korea.Meanwhile, a planned visit to South Korea by Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia senior director, was cancelled.South Korean AI startup Rebellions said her planned visit to its headquarters and a dinner with partners had been called off due to unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.Kakao Mobility also cancelled a photo session and question-and-answer event with her. However, the company said its business agreement with Nvidia would proceed, with senior director Gaurav Agarwal attending instead.Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to attract around 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, was proceeding as planned, according to South Korean media.The investigation's findings, the response from US lawmakers and any further developments concerning Megaspeed's business dealings with China will be key to determining the wider implications for Nvidia.

The company reported an 86.7% year-on-year (YoY) rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 73.25 crore for the September quarter on Friday, November 6, supported by strong demand across its beauty and personal care brands, wider distribution and improving profitability.Revenue from operations increased 35.9% to Rs 731.19 crore from Rs 538.06 crore a year earlier, marking the company's highest quarterly revenue growth since its stock market listing in November 2023.Red More: Samvat 2083 outlook: 8 triggers that could turn Sensex, Nifty correction into a rally by next DiwaliVarun Alagh, chairman, CEO and co-founder of Honasa Consumer, said the September quarter reflected the company's efforts to build a larger presence in the sector. "We delivered our highest growth since listing, with revenue growing 36% YoY and EBITDA nearly doubling to Rs 93 crore," Alagh said.Why is Jefferies bullish?Jefferies has raised its target price on Honasa Consumer to Rs 700 from its previous level, indicating an upside potential of 45%, while maintaining its 'Buy' rating.The brokerage said the company delivered its strongest growth since listing, supported by broad-based momentum across brands and sales channels. The strong performance also translated into a significant margin beat, with both EBITDA and net profit doubling year-on-year. Mamaearth recorded high-teen growth, while The Derma Co (TDC) and newer brands continued to scale up rapidly. Expanding distribution is also providing greater visibility into the growth potential of newer brands.Despite elevated input cost inflation, gross margin contracted by only around 55 basis points year-on-year. EBITDA margin expanded by more than 3.8 percentage points to 12.7%, comfortably exceeding expectations.Jefferies attributed the improvement to operating leverage, a better channel mix and greater advertising and promotion (A&P) efficiency in core brands. Overall A&P spending increased 36% year-on-year, broadly in line with revenue growth, with a significantly higher allocation towards newer brands. Lower sales commissions following the shift towards offline channels and quick commerce also supported operational efficiency.Read More: Finolex Cables shares fall 5% after rallying 20% during Muhurat Trading session. More upside ahead?Jefferies remains confident that Honasa can sustain its current margin trajectory of 12.5% in the second half of the financial year. items.title: Chandra and Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
items.summary: Mumbai: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.Also read: Plea seeking Tata Sons listing filed in Bombay High CourtPeople familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties.Mehli-Chandra meet focused onrebuilding trust, restoring equationMehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC).Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies. After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Also read: Noel Tata proposes splitting Tata Sons as alternative to RBI-mandated listingChandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts.Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.Among the relationships most affected was Mehli's equation with Chandrasekaran. Differences emerged over how developments within the trusts were characterised and communicated to external stakeholders, with Mehli maintaining that his interventions were driven by governance concerns. Communication between the two subsequently became infrequent.People said Chandrasekaran later made efforts, through intermediaries and directly, to reopen channels of communication with Mehli. Mehli remained a respected figure among trustees, a prominent voice within the Parsi community and an influential presence in discussions concerning the Tata legacy.Mehli has challenged the end of his trusteeship before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC), where the matter is pending. He, however, never withdrew his support for Chandrasekaran's stewardship of Tata Sons. In filings before the MCC, he said he had backed Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third five-year term and was a signatory to the resolution approving it.Chandrasekaran's second term as chairman ends in Feb 2027. His third term is linked to his continuation as a director of Tata Sons, which requires the trusts' approval at the company's annual general meeting (AGM). However, Tata Sons was unable to hold its AGM on Aug 18 after it failed to secure the requisite quorum. The impasse followed restrictions imposed by the MCC on SRTT, preventing it from joining SDTT in nominating a joint representative for quorum purposes.

Meanwhile, its Critical Injectables business accounted for the remaining 55% of revenue, registering growth of 18% during the quarter.The company continued to invest in research and development, with total R&D expenditure reaching Rs 107.7 crore in Q2 FY27, equivalent to 6% of consolidated revenue. This was higher than Rs 81.7 crore reported in the year-ago quarter. The expenditure was primarily directed towards complex product development and increasing the number of regulatory filings.During the September quarter, Gland Pharma launched four molecules in the US market: Sugammadex, Erythromycin, Fluorouracil and Atropine Sulfate.The company also filed 11 Abbreviated New Drug Applications (ANDAs) and received 10 approvals during Q2 FY27. With these additions, its cumulative US ANDA filings reached 399, of which 350 had been approved and 49 were awaiting approval.Management commentaryCommenting on the quarterly performance, Srinivas Sadu, Executive Chairman of Gland Pharma, said the company delivered another quarter of strong growth, supported by improved execution across its businesses. He highlighted the 31% growth in the CDMO segment, driven by expanding customer engagements, strategic partnerships and a strong opportunity pipeline.He also noted that continued investments in manufacturing capabilities, innovation and capacity expansion would help the company capitalise on increasing global outsourcing opportunities and create long-term shareholder value.Gland Pharma share price Gland Pharma shares have gained approximately 30% over the past three months. The 20-time English champion still goes into the international break 18th in the standings and in the relegation zone with just one win from 10 games. United's winless run in the league was extended to eight.

items.title: Sheikh Hasina about to return to Bangladesh?
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested on Monday a new passport and identity card so she can return from self-imposed exile in India, according to a letter seen by Reuters, her first such communication since fleeing in 2024.The request marks the clearest step by Hasina to act on her plan to return to Bangladesh in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising ended her long rule, raising the prospect of fresh political and legal tensions in a country where her party is now banned.Also read | G7 allies to assess impact of Trump's midterm setback at Paris talksShe has told Reuters she plans to return to surrender before a court, and her aides said on Monday the date would be announced once various formalities were completed. Bangladesh's war-crimes court sentenced her to death in November last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising, though she has denied the charges from exile."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers wrote to Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi.The letter asked for the applications to be processed "expeditiously" on the basis of her Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".Rahman in Delhi and spokespeople for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Dhaka did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Also read | Trump says his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' for votersHasina's Awami League party was the country's largest before it was banned following her fall. Many of her party colleagues have either been jailed or are in self-imposed exile in India or elsewhere.Having ruled Bangladesh for 20 years as prime minister across multiple terms, Hasina still enjoys support among sections of the population, and a return could sharpen political divisions as the government in Dhaka seeks to restore stability after more than two years of upheaval.On the other hand, it could improve Bangladesh's strained ties with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave her refuge.

FCNR(B) interest bill to keep dollar hedging costs high
items.summary: Mumbai: A multibillion-dollar FCNR(B) interest bill, coupled with the Reserve Bank of India's new reserve requirement on forex derivatives, is likely to keep dollar hedging costlier for Indian banks, treasury executives said.While the RBI provided a hedging facility for the $133 billion raised for three to five years under the special window opened for mobilising foreign currency deposits, banks must bear the currency risk on interest payments to non-resident depositors.135667176At an average interest rate of 6.5-7.0%, the annual interest outgo on these deposits is estimated at $8.6 billion to $9.3 billion. At least half of this amount remains unhedged, according to treasury heads at six banks ET spoke with, leaving lenders with more than $4 billion in dollar exposure to manage annually."The interest on FCNR(B) deposits is not covered by the window. Banks have to buy those dollars forward themselves, year after year, in the open market," said Anindya Banerjee, head of currency research at Kotak Securities.Read more: Bonus, stock splits & dividends: Dabur India, HUL, ONGC among 76 companies turning ex-record date this week"A forward premium is simply the extra price one pays today to lock in dollars for delivery later. When the entire banking system is buying dollars forward for the same reason, and there are not enough natural sellers, that extra price goes up," Banerjee said.Adding to the pressure is the RBI's new reserve requirement on banks' derivative positions. Introduced on October 10, the foreign exchange risk reserve (FERR) requires banks to maintain a cash reserve equivalent to 20% of the rupee value of eligible foreign-exchange derivative contracts.FERR makes it more expensive for banks to offer certain forward-dollar hedges because they must lock away cash against the contracts. Banks may pass on part of this additional cost to customers, putting further pressure on forward premia. The one-month and one-year forward premia were 2.50% and 2.78%, respectively, in early August. They surged to 8.50% and 4.85% by mid-October before easing to 3.83% and 3.91% by November 6, reflecting near-term dollar demand.A treasury head from a private bank said most banks had not put a hedging strategy in place as they were still assessing how best to manage this exposure. FERR in October added another layer of cost, making banks more cautious about locking in dollar liabilities over longer tenures. He explained that for now, the exposure was managed as it accrued, using short-term contracts that could be rolled over rather than hedging the entire interest obligation upfront. The reliance on short-term, rollover, contracts means banks will repeatedly return to the forward market as their interest liabilities accrue, sustaining demand for dollars instead of eliminating the exposure through an upfront hedge.Read more: Market may deliver bumper returns by next Diwali as valuations and earnings align, says Raamdeo AgrawalForeign banks, however, appear more comfortable carrying unhedged positions because they receive a steady stream of dollars from clients.A treasury executive from a foreign bank said some banks might hedge in the coming days as the rupee appreciated.The rupee staged a sharp recovery during the week, appreciating nearly 1.2% to close at 93.90 per dollar on Friday, its strongest level in more than six months.Some midsize banks, meanwhile, hedged the bulk of their dollar exposure after costs fell within their internal thresholds.

The party had received Rs 517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission.

items.title: UAE rescues 22 crew after ship catches fire
items.summary: Abu Dhabi: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) Coast Guard rescued 22 crew members of Arab nationality after a fire broke out aboard a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman, with all those rescued reported to be in stable condition.According to the UAE National Guard, the rescue operation was launched after the ship's crew alerted a Coast Guard unit about the fire onboard.In a post on X, the UAE National Guard said, "A National Guard Coast Guard unit rescued 22 people of Arab nationalities after a fire broke out aboard a cargo ship they were on in the Gulf of Oman."Following the distress report, specialised teams immediately initiated response procedures, located the vessel and reached the ship to evacuate all 22 crew members.The rescued individuals were provided with necessary first aid before being handed over to the relevant authorities. All 22 crew members were reported to be in stable condition.The National Guard said the operation demonstrated the preparedness and operational capabilities of its personnel, highlighting their continued commitment to responding swiftly to maritime emergencies.It further emphasised that the Coast Guard's efforts were aimed at protecting lives and strengthening maritime security and safety in the region."The operation underscores the high level of readiness and field competence of National Guard personnel, as well as their constant commitment to responding swiftly to maritime incidents and emergencies," the statement added.The latest rescue operation comes amid continued maritime security efforts by the UAE authorities to respond to emergencies involving commercial vessels operating in the region.Earlier, on October 10, the UAE National Guard's Coast Guard Division had rescued 22 Asian nationals after a fire broke out aboard an oil tanker in the Arabian Gulf.In that incident, the Coast Guard activated its emergency response procedures following a distress call from the vessel, located the tanker and rescued all 22 crew members.The rescued individuals were subsequently provided first aid and handed over to the relevant authorities, with all reported to be in stable health.

items.title: Strong earthquake with magnitude of 5.7 strikes central Japan, 22 injured
items.summary:
A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.
Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.
A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.
Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.

items.title: India, China stocks catch a second wind
items.summary: The unraveling of the AI trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asia playbook, reviving demand for out-of-favor Chinese and Indian stocks as well as companies poised to benefit from easing inflation and trade tensions.Aberdeen Investments favors markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms. Hedge fund Lotus Asset Management is long Hong Kong equity futures, while Allianz Global Investors is looking at healthcare and consumer companies.Also Read: Bloodbath in Nasdaq, Kospi and Nikkei but why Nifty is an oasis of peace amid global rout135649455“I expect investors to diversify more broadly and reduce their concentration in the AI trade,” said Rajeev De Mello, global macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management SA. “This should be supportive of China and other markets where valuations are less demanding.”India could also benefit, although its dependence on imported energy remains a headwind, he added.China and India as HedgesHao Hong, chief investment officer at Lotus, said he is betting against oil and petrochemical firms and going long precious metals and Hong Kong equity futures.A Hong Kong gauge tracking mainland companies gained 5.2% last week, its best performance since March 2025.Meanwhile, some global investors are interested in using China’s onshore market exposure as a diversifier to their AI-heavy portfolio, according to Jason Lui, head of Asia-Pacific equity and derivatives strategy at BNP Paribas SA.Also Read: $5 billion in 5 days! Why FIIs are suddenly shopping Indian stocks non-stop this DiwaliIndia’s appeal, meanwhile, has grown as oil prices declined on expectations of an earlier end to the Iran war, easing a key pressure point for the energy-importing economy. The market’s lack of AI exposure is also now seen as an advantage.135649462LOGOS Asset Management’s chief investment officer Charlie Hong said he sold his shares in SK Hynix Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., Intel Corp. and Lumentum Holdings Inc. last month and has since boosted his Indian holdings with shares of new-age tech companies, financial firms and contract drug manufacturers.India’s benchmark Nifty 50 gained 8.6% last week. registering its best week since 2021, as overseas investors returned in force. Foreign funds poured a net $1.9 billion into local shares last week through Wednesday.The sudden shift has kept market participants busy. Utkarsh Singh, a Mumbai-based senior manager at SBI-SG Global Securities Pvt., started taking calls from clients in Singapore as early as 6:30 a.m. Friday and continued fielding queries late into the day as Indian stocks rallied.“Foreign investors are suddenly pouring in,” Singh said. “I have taken more calls from foreign funds this week than I have all year,” he said. “I think we will see more inflows.”Before the latest gains, key benchmarks in India and China had ranked among the world’s worst-performing stock indexes this year through October.Going Beyond AIBeyond China and India, investors are also taking a fresh look at previously overlooked corners of Asian markets that offer value and less exposure to the AI boom.While defence and financial stocks could underperform, healthcare and consumer staples firms may get a boost, Allianz Global Investors’ chief investment officer for public markets Michael Krautzberger and strategist Liam Wash wrote in a recent note.In Korea, Fidelity’s long-only portfolio manager Dale Nicholls said he sees early signs of rotation beyond the semiconductor heavyweights, particularly among domestic pension funds.“Consumption-related areas stand out, spanning sectors from wellness through to some of the K-pop entertainment agencies” and Korea’s beauty and cosmetics industry, he said.At hedge fund ACG Management Pte., managing director Hui Ling Loh said Korea’s consumer stocks including retailers, cosmetics, food and beverage are benefiting from the perception that they are largely domestically oriented and face limited tariff and policy risks from the US.Phillip Wool, head of portfolio management at Rayliant Global Advisors, said he sees opportunity in Korea and Taiwan, “but it’s going to be beyond the highest-profile chip stocks that have run up so much and are now subject to so much unease.”One stock Wool likes is LG Electronics Inc., which he holds in his active emerging-markets exchange-traded fund. The company sells a lot of TVs, refrigerators and washing machines in the US, which “could be a catalyst for some upside as tariff pressure eases,” he said.The prospect of less isolationist US trade policies has also raised investor confidence in auto firms including Japan’s Toyota Motor Corp. and South Korea’s Hyundai Motor Co.Not everyone is ready to abandon AI. Some investors say the selloff may offer an opportunity to buy the dip, given the sector’s longer-term growth prospects.But for now, caution remains the prevalent mood.Foreigners will likely continue to sell Asia’s AI “picks and shovels” stocks, said Manishi Raychaudhuri, chief executive officer of Emmer Capital Partners Ltd. “India and China are the only two large liquid markets offering a considerable array of non-AI exposures.”

items.title: Emergency a mistake: Sonia Gandhi
items.summary: New Delhi: Weighing in on the Emergency, Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has called the decision to impose it a mistake and said that she believes that her mother-in-law and then prime minister Indira Gandhi also came to feel the same.The Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson in her upcoming book "Belonging: A Journey of Love" also writes that keeping Sanjay Gandhi "in check" could have prevented much of the damage that followed the imposition of the Emergency, according to The Guardian.Also Read: Sonia Gandhi says Penguin was 'uneasy' with criticism of govtIn an interview with the British daily ahead of the launch of her memoir, Sonia Gandhi said, "I always feel that Mrs (Indira) Gandhi was a democrat at heart.""I know that many would laugh at this, but I believe she was never comfortable in the course of the emergency. I think it was sitting heavy on her," she added.Sonia Gandhi, who also holds the distinction of being the longest serving president of the Congress, was quoted by the British daily as saying that it was a mistake for Indira Gandhi to call the Emergency, and that she believes her mother-in-law came to feel the same.Also Read: 'I will carry national flag across country, even if arrested': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at Kochi protestAccording to Gandhi, the family was split on the decision of Emergency.Sonia Gandhi's husband Rajiv was against the move, telling his mother to wait for the next election, but her younger son Sanjay pushed for it, arguing at one family dinner that the opposition would destroy his mother and telling her, "They must be stopped", the Guardian reported.Sonia Gandhi was quoted as saying that it inflamed tensions within the family, too, as Rajiv attempted to confront his mother, but she refused to listen."Keeping Sanjay in check could have prevented much of the damage that followed," Gandhi writes in her book, according to The Guardian.In another interview published in The Hindu on Saturday ahead of the launch of her book, Gandhi has also spoken about the turbulent times of the Emergency.She said that hindsight allows people to put things better in perspective and pointed out that Indira Gandhi herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency.Asked about Sanjay Gandhi's name becoming synonymous with the Emergency, and whether the excesses of that time could have been avoided had Indira Gandhi listened to her elder son Rajiv and to others, Sonia Gandhi said, "It was not only Sanjay, though in the public mind he is often seen as synonymous with the Emergency. There was a lot of pressure from some of her senior colleagues, and I think there were very few people around her like Rajiv who had a different point of view.""I think eventually my mother-in-law began to understand the situation through her own wisdom and took actions to remedy it," she said."It was only after the Emergency that I came to know the true gravity of what had been happening. Yes, democratic rights had been curtailed and there was a suspension of habeas corpus, but it was done constitutionally," the former Congress chief said."Yet, when I take myself back to that period and try and see it from Mrs Gandhi's point of view, I see her struggling to cope with the rapidly deteriorating prevailing circumstances: violent protests, government offices and public transport set on fire, widespread organised unrest and even a call for the bureaucracy and armed forces to disobey orders," Gandhi said.Hindsight allows us to put things better in perspective, she said.Sonia Gandhi pointed out that Indira herself came to recognise what was happening and called for the March 1977 election."And you know very well that she herself later publicly expressed regret and apologised for excesses during the Emergency," she said.According to The Guardian, Gandhi also recalled crying as she witnessed the demolition of the Babri mosque in 1992.Gandhi knew then that they faced "a long battle for the secular nation that Mahatma Gandhi, Nehru and their colleagues had strived to build", the British daily said.She accepted that failures of her own party in part contributed to the rise of the BJP and its hardline Hindutva politics."I think we have been too complacent in many ways. There was a laissez-faire kind of an attitude," she said.Emergency was imposed by Indira Gandhi just before midnight of June 25, 1975. President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed issued the proclamation at Gandhi's behest that was later ratified by the Union Cabinet.On January 18, 1977, Indira Gandhi called for fresh elections and released all political prisoners.On March 16, 1977, Indira Gandhi and son Sanjay were defeated in Lok Sabha elections and on March 21 that year, the Emergency officially came to an end.The BJP has been criticising the Congress over the Emergency, calling it a "murder of democracy".The Modi government has been observing 'Samvidhan Hatya Diwas' to mark the "dark phase" in Indian democracy.

items.title: Airstrike kills 22 near Yemen's capital
items.summary: Airstrikes hit homes in a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday, killing at least 22 people and wounding 30 others, mostly women and children, a spokesman for Yemen's Houthi-run Health Ministry said.Speaking to The Associated Press, Anees Alasbahi accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes on al-Shariya. The AP could not independently verify the claims, and Saudi Arabia's Information Ministry did not immediately reply to an AP request for comment.The toll reflected the rapid worsening of Yemen's civil war, where a yearslong truce fell apart over the summer. Fighting has escalated between the Iranian-backed Houthis - who control Sanaa, the north and the west of the country - and their Saudi-backed opponents based in the south and east.On Friday, an airstrike in a market in southern Yemen killed at least 30 people, according to Houthi officials. The Houthis and Yemen's Saudi-backed military each blamed the other for that strike.Footage from Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV of the aftermath of Saturday's strikes showed staff carrying limp bodies of young children out of ambulances bringing the casualties to a local hospital. One little girl's head had been cleaved open. Other children lay on stretchers, bloodied and bandaged as staff tended to them. Footage from the village showed the rubble of destroyed houses and dust filling the air as people hid in nearby agricultural fields.Alasbahi said in a posting earlier on X that Saturday's strikes hit several homes in al-Shariyah. Subsequent strikes targeted emergency responders, he told the AP.In September, the Houthis made a lightning advance capturing much of Yemen's Red Sea coast and strategic islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. They have also encircled the city of Taiz, a strategic gateway to southern Yemen. At the same time, they have stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, targeting oil and military infrastructure and shipping in the Red Sea.

items.title: Italy's foreign minister says his personal data was leaked on dark web
items.summary:
Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said Saturday that his personal data had been disseminated on the dark web, an encrypted part of the internet, and that he has been exposed to "threats and intimidation."
Tajani made the announcement in a social media post following a string of hoax bomb threats across Europe that caused flight diversions, security threats against broadcasters as well as recent attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems and drone incursions.
"For days, cybercriminals have been spreading my personal data on the dark web and seeking other information, in fact exposing me and my family to new threats and intimidation," Tajani said, adding that the criminals "are prepared to pay for other details on me and my loved ones."
Tajani, who is also a vice premier in Italy's government, did not specify what kind of information had been shared, but suggested that the cyberthreat was ongoing.

items.title: UP govt hikes DA by 5%, employees to get arrears retrospectively from Jul 1
items.summary:
The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 5 per cent for state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales.
Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63 per cent, up from 58 per cent. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the state government said in a statement on Saturday.
A government order was also issued in this regard on Saturday.
The enhanced dearness allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state.
The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the state's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees, the statement said.

items.title: Delhi to ban non-BS-VI vehicles from other states every year from Nov 1
items.summary:
The Delhi government on Saturday said it will implement the ban on vehicles below BS-VI emission standards registered in other states or Union territories every year between November 1 and January 31.
It earlier announced a ban on the plying of non-Delhi-registered motor vehicles that are below BS-VI emission norms for the same period this year -- which is usually marked by the worst of the city's air pollution and quality -- under its Winter Action Plan to limit vehicular emissions and curb dust on roads.
"Every year, from November 1 to January 31, other state-registered BS-IV and below vehicles will not be allowed to ply in Delhi," a Delhi transport department's public notification said on Saturday.

items.summary:
Divi's Laboratories Ltd on Saturday posted a sharp 63.57 per cent rise in net profit to Rs 1,127 crore in the September quarter due to higher revenues.
The company posted a net profit of Rs 689 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year, a regulatory filing said.
Revenue from operations rose 35.39 per cent to Rs 3,676 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,715 crore a year earlier, it said.
Its total expenses rose to Rs 2,265 crore in the period under review from Rs 1,948 crore a year ago, it added.
The company's net profit for the first half of the current fiscal year, however, declined 35.39 per cent to Rs 2,029 crore from Rs 2,568 crore in the year-ago period, the filing added.

items.title: Centre allows transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh, other states
items.summary:
The Centre has extended the Punjab Police and Correctional Services Act, 2006, to the Union Territory of Chandigarh, introducing provisions for the transfer of prisoners between states and Union territories and changes to the functioning of the prison administration.
The notification, issued under Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, extends the Punjab legislation to the Union Territory of Chandigarh with certain modifications, according to a notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Friday.
The amended provisions deal with the transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh and other states or Union territories.
Under the provisions, prisoners serving sentences in Chandigarh, including life imprisonment, may be transferred to prisons in another state or Union territory with the consent of the government concerned and an order issued by the Chandigarh administrator.
The amendments also provide for the transfer of undertrial prisoners in the interest of Chandigarh's .

items.title: Odisha CM Mohan Majhi cancels Diwali celebrations over Cyclone Arnab damage
items.summary:
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has cancelled Diwali celebrations at his residence this year in view of the damage and suffering caused by Cyclone Arnab and subsequent floods in several parts of the state.
In a statement, the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) said Diwali celebrations at Majhi's residence have been cancelled. The CM has also requested people not to bring gifts or bouquets on the occasion.
"The Hon'ble Chief Minister has appealed to people to remain sensitive to the public in the affected areas and extend a helping hand to those affected by the disaster," the CMO said in a post on X.
Earlier, Majhi had also skipped Durga Puja celebrations as a mark of solidarity with farmers who suffered crop losses due to heavy rainfall in October.
He had refrained from visiting puja pandals.

items.title: Sharad Pawar discharged from Mumbai hospital after treatment for infection

NCP-SP chief Sharad Pawar was on Saturday discharged from a Mumbai hospital after undergoing treatment for chest and respiratory infection.
Pawar (85) later proceeded to his residence near the Brech Candy Hospital, where he was under treatment for the last three days.
Congress leaders Sushilkumar Shinde, Balasaheb Thorat and NCP leader Dilip Walse-Patil visited the hospital Friday night to meet the former Union minister.
Industrialist Gautam Adani and NCP leader Praful Patel had also visited the hospital.
Pawar was initially admitted to Pune's Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 and discharged on November 4. The same day, he was admitted to the Mumbai hospital.

items.title: Illegal US migration: Indians remain in top 3
items.summary: Indian nationals continued to rank as the third-largest group encountered by US border authorities in the 2026 fiscal year, despite a steep decline in illegal migration attempts following President Donald Trump's crackdown on unauthorised immigration.US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) data show that 30,528 Indian nationals were encountered by border authorities in FY26, which ran from October 2025 to September 2026. Only Mexican and Canadian nationals recorded higher numbers, with 1,23,439 and 37,700 encounters, respectively.India ranked ahead of China, which recorded 29,818 encounters. The figures indicate that attempts by Indians to enter the US illegally continue despite tougher enforcement and the risks associated with the journey, commonly known as the 'donkey route'.According to sources familiar with illegal immigration networks, a sizeable number of those attempting the journey are from Gujarat, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh. Within Gujarat, people from North and Central Gujarat continue to figure prominently among those seeking to enter the US through unauthorised routes.Illegal migration encounters from India fall nearly 64%135630363The number of Indian nationals encountered at US borders has declined considerably over the past three fiscal years. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) recorded 90,415 encounters involving Indians in FY24. This fell to 34,146 in FY25 and further to 30,528 in FY26, marking a decline of nearly 64% from FY24.The reduction coincides with the Trump administration's tougher immigration enforcement measures. Trump returned to the White House on January 20, 2025, after winning the November 2024 presidential election, with a crackdown on illegal immigration among his administration's major priorities.The decline in Indian encounters is part of a wider fall in unauthorised migration to the US. CBP recorded 3,82,490 border encounters across nationalities in FY26, nearly 45% below the 6,91,906 recorded in FY25. The corresponding figures were considerably higher in FY24 and FY23, at around 29 lakh and 32 lakh, respectively.Among other nationalities, Guatemala accounted for 18,319 encounters, followed by the Philippines with 17,985 and Honduras with 13,005. Brazil recorded 6,285, Russia 5,327 and Venezuela 4,945. Nationals of other countries, grouped, accounted for 63,678 encounters.Gujarat continues to bear the human cost135630381The continuing attempts to reach the US illegally have also resulted in fatalities and disappearances. At least 11 people from Gujarat died and another 11 were injured or went missing between 2022 and 2025 while attempting the journey.One of the most devastating incidents occurred on January 19, 2022, when four members of a family from Dingucha village in Gujarat's Gandhinagar district froze to death near the US-Canada border. Jagdish Patel, 30, his wife Vaishali, 37, and their children Vihang, 13, and Dharmik, aged three, were found dead near Emerson in Manitoba, Canada, around 10 metres from the border. The family had been travelling on foot when they were caught in a blizzard.On March 28, 2023, four members of a family from Manekpura village in Mehsana district drowned after a boat capsized. Another tragedy occurred on May 5, 2025, when two children from Mehsana drowned off the California coast.Despite these incidents, illegal migration networks continue to attract people with the promise of better financial prospects in the US.A source familiar with the networks said, "Though people have been shunted out of the US through Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) crackdown, a large number of Gujaratis mainly from North and Central Gujarat are sneaking into America for better financial security."The source added that attempts to enter through the Mexican and Canadian borders were continuing, with individuals reportedly paying between Rs 80 lakh and Rs 1.25 crore for the journey.- Reference taken from TOI

items.title: Stocks vs Gold: Which asset could create more wealth in the Samvat 2083?
items.summary: Indian equities are looking increasingly attractive compared with gold, with their relative valuations falling to levels rarely seen over the past three decades. According to Samco Securities, the current market environment presents an opportunity for investors to increase their exposure to equities in Samvat 2083, while retaining existing gold investments as a portfolio hedge.In its Market Outlook for Samvat 2083, the brokerage highlighted that the Sensex-to-Gold ratio currently stands at 6.43, significantly below its long-term median of 9.8 since 1990. The ratio is also lower than approximately 86% of its monthly readings over the period.The ratio had touched 5.26 in March 2026, its lowest level since 1991, reflecting the extent of Indian equities' underperformance against gold during the recent market cycle.Historically, similar levels have marked attractive entry points for equity investors. The ratio previously entered comparable territory in 1993, 2001-03, 2009 and 2011-13. On each of these occasions, Indian equities subsequently outperformed gold by a significant margin over the following years.“Relative to gold, Indian stocks are as cheap as they have been in a generation. Gold has done its job as a hedge, and we recommend holding on to existing gold investments but not adding to them aggressively at these levels,” said the brokerage in its report.135629914The brokerage further believes the current valuation gap provides an opportunity to increase equity exposure. "This is the time to tilt your portfolio towards equities," it recommended, while advising investors to retain their existing gold investments rather than aggressively adding to them at current levels.Why Samco believes equities could outperform goldThe Sensex-to-Gold ratio provides a broader perspective on investor sentiment and relative asset performance. A rising ratio indicates that equities are outperforming gold and investors are increasingly willing to take risks. A declining ratio, on the other hand, suggests a preference for gold and safer assets.Samco noted that the decline in the ratio during the previous Samvat was initially driven largely by the rally in gold rather than a collapse in equities. However, Samvat 2082 brought the equity correction that the brokerage had considered necessary for a more durable bottom.During the period, the Sensex declined from its high of 85,762 to a low of 71,593, while gold continued to advance, pushing the ratio to its March 2026 trough of 5.26.With the ratio now recovering to 6.43, Samco believes the relative valuation equation favours equities.Cheap valuations, but global risks remainDespite its constructive outlook on equities, Samco has cautioned that the risks confronting Indian markets have not disappeared.Elevated crude oil prices, currency depreciation and global market volatility remain important considerations for investors entering Samvat 2083.Brent crude remained above $100 for much of the year amid the US-Iran conflict. Given India's dependence on crude oil imports, sustained high prices could put pressure on the rupee, inflation, government finances and corporate profit margins.Currency weakness is another concern. The rupee depreciated from 87.88 to 95.15 against the US dollar during the Samvat, a decline of approximately 8%, and touched record lows near 97. Persistent foreign investor outflows and a wide trade deficit continue to weigh on the domestic currency.Global market leadership has also shifted, with US healthcare, energy and financial stocks gaining prominence over technology and semiconductor stocks. Volatility across asset classes remains elevated."Cheap valuations tell us what to own; uncertainty tells us how to own it," Samco said, outlining diversification as its preferred strategy for the year ahead.Samco's stock picks for Samvat 2083Against this backdrop, Samco has identified a diversified basket of Indian stocks across sectors and investment horizons, combining long-term growth opportunities with shorter-term tactical ideas.Among the one-year recommendations, Adani Power represents the power-generation theme, while BSE offers exposure to the growing capital-market infrastructure segment. Tech Mahindra is positioned as a potential turnaround and rupee beneficiary.Azad Engineering and HFCL feature as high-growth opportunities linked to aerospace, defence, energy components, telecom and data-centre connectivity. Tips Music, meanwhile, represents an asset-light business model in the media and entertainment space.For the six-month investment horizon, Samco has selected L&T Technology Services, citing the potential for an earnings recovery and benefits from rupee depreciation, alongside TVS Motor Company as a consumption-oriented opportunity.The shorter-term basket includes MCX, which could benefit from increased market volatility, and Sansera Engineering, which features as a momentum-oriented play in the auto and aerospace components space.135629881Why US ETFs find a place in Samco's portfolioA notable feature of Samco's strategy for Samvat 2083 is its recommendation to diversify beyond Indian equities through dollar-denominated US-listed exchange-traded funds (ETFs).The brokerage has identified two ETFs: the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) and the Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLV).The XLE ETF provides exposure to the US energy sector and is positioned as a potential hedge against rising crude oil prices. This is particularly relevant for Indian investors because higher oil prices can hurt domestic equities through their impact on import costs, inflation and the rupee.The XLV ETF, which tracks the US healthcare sector, is recommended as a defensive, dollar-denominated holding that could help cushion portfolios against further weakness in the Indian currency.Indian investors should consider geographical diversificationSamco's overseas allocation strategy is built around three considerations: currency diversification, access to global businesses and the potential benefits of lower correlation between markets.For Indian investors with future expenses linked to foreign currencies, including overseas education and travel, holding dollar-denominated assets can help protect purchasing power when the rupee depreciates.US markets also provide access to global leaders in sectors such as technology, healthcare and energy, where comparable investment opportunities may not always be available in the domestic market.The brokerage also pointed out that Indian and US equities do not necessarily move in tandem. During Samvat 2082, the S&P 500 gained while the Nifty declined, illustrating the diversification benefits of holding assets across markets.Resident Indian individuals can invest overseas under the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS). However, returns from US investments depend on both the underlying security's performance in dollar terms and movements in the USD/INR exchange rate.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Compulsory retirement is not punitive, does not imply misconduct: SC
items.summary:
The Supreme Court has held that an order of compulsory retirement is neither punitive nor stigmatic in character and does not cast any aspersion on the conduct of an employee, nor does it imply any finding of misconduct.
A bench of Justices Manmohan and Shree Chandrashekhar, which upheld the Chhattisgarh government's order of compulsory retirement to five of its 14 employees, said it was based on subjective satisfaction of the competent authority that the employee's continued retention in service is no longer conducive to public interest.

items.summary: Jubilant FoodWorks, which operates Domino's Pizza and Popeyes in India, reported strong growth in its delivery business in the September quarter, while Popeyes continued to gain traction, emerging as a second growth engine for the quick-service restaurant (QSR) operator.Domino's India reported a 9.2% year-on-year increase in revenue in Q2 FY27, supported by 6.3% growth in orders. Revenue from its delivery channel grew 11.3% during the quarter, with delivery accounting for 75.8% of the brand's total revenue. The company's like-for-like (LFL) growth improved to 4.1% from 2.5% in the June quarter and 0.2% in the March quarter.Also read: Diwali shopping gets costlier this year: From milk, ghee, butter to dry fruits135628398The QSR giant reported sustained momentum in delivery, along with early signs of recovery in its dine-in and takeaway (DITA) business, supported the improvement in Domino's India performance. Late-night consumption also emerged as a strong-performing segment, with more than 90% of the network now offering services until 3 am.Over the past six to nine months, the company has expanded its late-night offerings to tap into additional consumption occasions and drive incremental orders. Product launches across the Maxxx range, Double Cheese Burst, cold coffee and mousse have also helped improve customer engagement and average ticket sizes.The company is also working to revive its dine-in and takeaway business, which recorded 2.4% revenue growth during the quarter. Infrastructure upgrades have been completed in around 20% of the identified stores, while its My Meal at Rs 119 proposition has been rolled out nationally to drive footfalls and improve ticket sizes.Meanwhile, Popeyes is gaining scale and emerging as a meaningful second growth engine for Jubilant FoodWorks. The fried chicken chain reported 122% year-on-year revenue growth in Q2 FY27, with like-for-like growth of 53%, marking its fourth consecutive quarter of growth above 40%.Also read: Quick commerce emerges beyond Diwali shopping panic to breathe on the necks of e-commerce giantsPopeyes added 11 stores during the quarter, taking its presence to 25 cities. Its system-level average daily sales are now broadly comparable with established competitors in most markets, according to the company.The brand's growth has also been accompanied by an improvement in profitability. Popeyes' gross margin expanded by 150 basis points year-on-year during the quarter. Jubilant FoodWorks is targeting the development of Popeyes into a Rs 1,000 crore brand over the next three to four years.However, the company is prioritising store-level returns and unit economics over an aggressive expansion strategy. While customer experience, gross margins and store productivity are approaching or matching competitive benchmarks, brand-level profitability is not yet fully established.Jubilant FoodWorks said it was following the expansion strategy adopted for Domino's, focusing on entering the right micro-markets, maintaining attractive store-level economics and ensuring new outlets meet return thresholds before accelerating expansion.At the consolidated level, Jubilant FoodWorks reported an 11.8% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 2,608 crore in Q2 FY27. EBITDA rose 7.3% to Rs 513 crore. Standalone revenue grew 11.5% to Rs 1,885 crore, while EBITDA increased 12.4% to Rs 372 crore.The company added 108 stores across its businesses during the quarter, taking its global network to 3,820 outlets.The Domino's India franchisee is managing elevated input costs through procurement efficiencies, calibrated pricing, menu-mix optimisation and tighter cost controls. Its standalone gross margin expanded 110 basis points year-on-year to 75.5%, while standalone EBITDA margin improved 16 basis points to 19.8%.The company is prioritising sustained growth at Domino's India, scaling Popeyes while improving unit economics, developing its international businesses and embedding technology across operations.
