items.title: China's giant pandas make debut at US zoo
items.summary: Atlanta: Giant pandas Ping Ping and Fu Shuang delighted visitors to Zoo Atlanta during their public debut Friday, chewing bamboo and lounging in their new US habitat while on loan from China.A male named Ping Ping and female Fu Shuang arrived from Chengdu in September via a FedEx flight dubbed the "Panda Express," and are to be hosted in the southern US facility for the next 10 years.Pandas are "animals that have got a unique ability to inspire curiosity, instill passion, evoke joy, and unite people around the globe," CEO Raymond King told onlookers at Zoo Atlanta."This extraordinary spirit of partnership helps create a future for a species that is truly beloved the world over."In preparation for their arrival, Zoo Atlanta has renovated its panda facilities and assembled a team of animal caretakers.It has also ensured a stable and long-term supply of bamboo, grown locally in Atlanta, which has a climate that is very similar to Chengdu."I think they inspire happiness," zoo visitor Rachel Totts told AFP on Friday. "They make people smile. I've never seen someone not say 'Oh, it's so cute!' when they're looking at a panda."Soft, furry power Native to temperate forest habitats in East Asia, the lumbering black-and-white mammals do not typically travel long distances in the wild.But many have been shipped to zoos around the world as apart of Beijing's decades-long "panda diplomacy" program to foster foreign ties.The furry show of "soft power" came as top US officials on Friday called on China to uphold the trade agreement made in an October 2025 meeting between US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping.The accord calmed tensions after a whirlwind of tariff hikes, and required China to buy US soybeans while suspending export controls on rare earths.Before 2016 pandas were considered endangered but are now listed as "vulnerable" by wildlife advocates, and an estimated 1,800 pandas live in the wild.The Chinese government has established more than 50 panda reserves for conservation, but in the wild the bears continue to face threats of habitat loss and poaching.Panda pairs Atlanta previously hosted pandas on loan from China starting in 1999, and seven panda cubs have been born at the zoo. All are now back in Chengdu, and Zoo Atlanta has not had any pandas since 2024.Atlanta native John Perez celebrated his 28th birthday at Zoo Atlanta on Friday, telling AFP the pandas drew him to visit for the first time because "it felt perfect, you know?"Both of the new arrivals were born in 2020, and it's hoped they will be suitable mates. Pandas in captivity typically live for around 30 years.In 1972, China gifted a pair of pandas to Washington, following US president Richard Nixon's historic visit to the Communist nation.Beijing recalled two of its pandas from Japan early this year, following a diplomatic spat that began when Japan's prime minister hinted that Tokyo could intervene militarily in the event of any attack on Taiwan.

EU's 2030 move puts single-use sachets in focus
items.summary: Now, over 70 years since they were invented, single-serve tomato ketchup sachets are slated to become contraband from 2030 under the European Union's Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation. Maybe in the future, secret stashes of them will find their way on to the dark web (or its future equivalent) to be picked up for a fortune by collectors and hoarded away in airtight vaults. Even further in the future, they will be unearthed as 20th century material culture.A newly rekindled romance with Europe has seen the current Labour-led British government there become willin', Barkis-like, to adopt rules that routinely used to make their Conservative predecessors see red. And that has now led to talk of an outrageous assault on a familiar and beloved table accessory in countless British pubs and eateries: sachets of not only single-serve ketchup but also mayonnaise, mustard and vinegar, usually reposing in a convenient bowl.Also Read: Why best leaders don't try to save the worldNo doubt back in 1955, Messrs Harold Ross and Yale Kaplan did yeoman service to the food trade by apportioning the right amount of condiment and ensconcing it in a sachet that required less energy to open and dispense than bottles or jars. Bigger receptacles were messy and wasteful it was believed, and sachets offered a clean and ordered - read, pre-measured - alternative that required no thought. Clearly, they had read the average convenience junkie's mind perfectly.Of course, the primary beneficiary of these prepackaged condiments were eateries themselves. Which business would not want to obviate the chance of wasteful or butter-fingered customers dispensing more from bottles than necessary? The extra packing cost per unit of ketchup is recouped by lower wastage even though the sachets are offered "free". Not many such sachets go waste anyway, even if a few brazen types grab handfuls of each to go with their fish and chips.Few humans can resist the allure of those sauce packets in our current stage of evolution. This writer included. When any of those come in my standard airline meal, I sagely tuck them into my bag rather than hand them back unopened along with my empty tray to the cabin crew. Ditto for wet tissue sachets, sugar packets, miniature jam and butter tubs and small water bottles. Is that wastage or thriftiness on my part? All my travel bags have a few tucked away from last time...Single-use sachets have become all pervasive in India, from pickles to shampoo, biscuits to spices, ointments to detergents. Speaking anecdotally, though, pan masala and gutka sachets appear to be the most pernicious. Those shiny, empty sachets find their way into every nook and cranny; most disturbingly they turn up even in the garden soil when I am repotting a plant. Millions of thoughtlessly chucked sachets now clog up our water bodies, forests and farmlands.Our planet would be better off without all sachets, but this EU regulation exempts takeaway food. So those ubiquitous oregano and chilli flakes sachets that arrive with pizza and burger orders will still be available for stockpiling by human packrats after 2030. Hospitals and nursing homes will also be exempt, on grounds of hygiene and safety. EU being EU, alternatives are also helpfully listed: refillable sauce dispensers, small bowls for jam and jugs for creamers.The EU regulation is aimed only at establishments that provide these to those who dine in. But there is a case to draw a line under this brilliant 20th century invention - for the sake of future centuries. Pre-portioned packaging really underestimates humans: we can go to the moon and deep space but cannot use a squeezy jar or a bottle at a fast-food restaurant or at home for ketchup or mustard? Single-use plastics are the most dispensable of inventions, pun intended.

items.title: Airtel calls for industry-wide data pricing reset
items.summary: New Delhi: Bharti Airtel Friday told analysts its prepaid tweaks are only a trial run, and that sustained growth in average revenue per user - a key growth metric - will need a sector-wide shift in how data is priced.Asked on the Q2 FY27 earnings call whether its August intervention was a step towards fixing the industry's pricing architecture, Shashwat Sharma, managing director of Bharti Airtel, said the problem was structural. The sector, he said, has "a very flat architecture and very low ARPUs.""You're giving away unlimited usage, and you're not monetising consumption in a way. Data in that sense is not charged properly." The withdrawal of the ₹299 plan move, he said, was "more of an experimentation on our own base to keep moving ARPUs up," while "the architecture correction is a much broader correction that is required in the industry."Airtel's India mobile ARPU rose to ₹271 from ₹264, helped by premiumisation and an extra day in the quarter. Sharma said the Q2 prepaid action had "already kind of paid out," with postpaid upgrades, international roaming and top-ups as the next levers.Data usage per user, an analyst noted, is closing the gap with peers to 20-odd percent. Sharma said heavy users must contribute more, "People who consume heavily must pay for data proportionately, and that is the shift the industry eventually will have to make." Doing so would give "organic growth of ARPU, which is consumption-led," and "a pivotal shift that we need to make."Sharma attributed higher churn to seasonality and tariff actions, which bring "a temporary impact on customer continuity." Interestingly, Airtel reintroduced the ₹299 plan that it had withdrawn in August, which had effectively increased the entry price for daily data plans to ₹349.

items.title: NY Fed's John Williams flags need to gather more information on inflation risks before rate decisions
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials are weighing the inflationary risks from strong economic activity and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure, even as they signal the need for more data before determining the next steps on interest rates, Bloomberg reported.For live updates on US Markets, click here New York Fed President John Williams said inflation remained too high, although other indicators were not yet pointing to broader concerns. Speaking at an event hosted by the European Central Bank in Frankfurt on Friday, he backed the Fed's position that policymakers should gather more information before deciding the appropriate course for monetary policy."Inflation is absolutely too high," Williams said, while noting that wage growth remained consistent with the central bank's 2% inflation target and inflation expectations were well anchored.Fed weighs inflation against economic resilienceWilliams said monetary policy had an important role in preventing temporary price shocks from spreading into broader or more persistent inflation.Also Read: Federal Reserve rate hike bets strengthen as US jobs growth beats estimates"Our FOMC statement last meeting, I think, captures correctly that this is an appropriate time to accumulate more information to help us determine what the appropriate stance of policy is to make make sure we achieve a timely return to our 2% target," he said, according to the Bloomberg report.The Fed held interest rates steady at its previous meeting after raising its benchmark rate by 25 basis points in September to a range of 3.75%-4%. Policymakers have since emphasised the need for additional information while keeping the possibility of further rate increases open, Bloomberg reported.The central bank's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures price index, rose 3.6% in September from a year earlier. Underlying inflation measures that exclude food and energy also increased. Meanwhile, the US economy expanded at its fastest pace in a year in the quarter ended September.AI infrastructure raises fresh inflation concernsSeparately, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem warned that the rapid build-out of AI infrastructure could add to near-term inflationary pressures, Bloomberg reported."When I look at inflation, excess inflation today, it’s coming both from negative supply shocks related to the Middle East and demand forces coming related to the AI build," Musalem said.While acknowledging AI's potential to improve productivity over time, he cautioned against shaping current monetary policy around benefits that may take years to materialise."We need to make monetary policy for the economy of the day," he said. "We cannot make monetary policy for the economy as it may be five years from now."(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: Federal Reserve rate hike bets strengthen as US jobs growth beats estimates
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's case for another interest rate hike in December has gained momentum after stronger than expected US employment data reinforced signs of economic resilience, shifting attention back to persistent inflation from concerns over a potential AI driven slowdown, Reuters reported.US employers added 165,000 jobs in October, more than double the 65,000 expected by economists, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The unemployment rate also edged down to 4.1%, suggesting the labour market remains firm despite concerns over the economic outlook.For live updates on US Markets, click here Following the report, markets priced in an 85% probability of a quarter point rate increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting, up from around 75% before the data release. Traders also brought forward expectations of another rate increase to April from June, Reuters reported.Strong jobs data reinforce Fed's hawkish outlookThe employment figures strengthen the argument for further monetary tightening as the Fed continues to battle inflation, which has remained above its 2% target for more than five years.Also Read: Nasdaq rebounds as chip stocks recover from steep losses, rate fears persist"This is a very strong labor market report on the heels of solid GDP and consumer spending data last week, reinforcing the economy’s positive momentum," Fitch Ratings analyst Olu Sonola wrote after the release.While acknowledging the risks posed by recent AI related concerns, Sonola said the economy remained on firm footing and that labour market resilience was pushing the policy debate towards a December rate hike, Reuters reported.Raymond James analysts also expect the central bank to raise rates next month."For the Federal Reserve, this should allow them to concentrate on the inflation side of their mandate," the analysts wrote. "We expect the Fed to increase the federal funds rate by 25 basis points in December."AI concerns had clouded rate outlookExpectations of another rate increase had weakened after Democrats' midterm election gains raised concerns about tighter regulation of AI and data centre construction.The prospect of slower AI investment had fuelled worries about weaker economic growth and easing inflationary pressures, reducing the urgency for further monetary tightening.However, Friday's employment report has renewed expectations that the Fed will prioritise inflation control as it assesses the strength of the US economy.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.summary: Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) stepped up their buying in Indian equities on Friday, November 6, pumping in a net Rs 13,750 crore and extending their buying streak to 14 trading sessions. With the latest purchase, cumulative FII investments since October 16 have reached Rs 53,154 crore, according to the exchange data.Friday's buying followed another massive investment of Rs 14,975 crore on Thursday, November 5, marking the biggest single-day FII purchase in Indian equities in more than a year.The pace of foreign buying has accelerated in recent sessions, with FIIs investing a net Rs 34,584 crore over the past five trading sessions alone. The latest inflows mark a sharp turnaround from the prolonged selling witnessed earlier this year, when overseas investors withdrew billions of dollars from Indian equities.The foreign buying came even as domestic institutional investors (DIIs) continued to sell. DIIs offloaded shares worth a net Rs 5,969 crore on Friday, following net sales of Rs 10,445 crore in the previous session. Their combined net selling over the two sessions stood at Rs 16,414 crore.The return of foreign buying follows months of sustained selling amid elevated crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, a weakening rupee and concerns over corporate earnings.Foreign selling intensified in September and October as oil prices climbed and global investors reduced their exposure to emerging markets. The outflows had pushed foreign ownership of Indian equities to historic lows.Global brokerage Nomura said Indian equities could become more attractive to foreign investors as earnings improve and valuations remain below their post-pandemic averages. It also noted that the correction in artificial intelligence-related stocks in international markets could encourage investors to redirect capital towards other markets, including India.Expectations of a possible reduction in long-term capital gains tax for foreign investors have also added to optimism, although any such change remains uncertain.ALSO READ: $5 billion in 5 days! Why FIIs are suddenly shopping Indian stocks non-stop this DiwaliSensex, Nifty climb higherIndian equities defied a global sell-off on Friday, extending their winning streak as investors turned to domestic markets as a relative safe haven amid turmoil across global markets. The Nifty 50 surged 494 points, or 2.01%, to settle at 25,030, while the BSE Sensex advanced 1,718 points, or 2.17%, to close at 81,028.The broader markets, however, came under pressure. The Nifty Smallcap 250 declined 0.85%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 ended marginally lower, signalling continued weakness beyond the benchmark indices.Among sectoral indices, the Nifty Private Bank index led the gains, rallying more than 3%, while the Nifty Financial Services index advanced over 2.5%. The Nifty Consumer Durables index also gained around 2%.Despite the sharp gains in benchmark indices, market volatility remained elevated. The India VIX, which gauges expected market volatility, surged more than 13% to trade near the 18 mark.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. Two-wheeler retail sales fell 28.35 per cent to 23.21 lakh units, while passenger vehicle sales dropped 4.23 per cent to 5.08 lakh units during the month.
"October is India's largest retail month of the year, and this year it must be read with the calendar firmly in mind," said FADA President Sai Giridhar, adding that the year-on-year decline is almost entirely optical.

items.title: Chawri Bazar building collapse: Rescue operation enters second day
items.summary:
Rescue operations at the site of a three-storey building collapse in Old Delhi's congested Chawri Bazar area are still underway 24 hours after the incident that left two people dead and several trapped, officials said.
The building located in Gali Sitara near the Chawri Bazar Metro station collapsed around 9.45 am on Thursday, triggering a massive rescue operation involving the Delhi Police, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Services and Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD).
Around 10 to 15 labourers were present at the construction site when the building came crashing down, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said.
Rescue teams have so far pulled out four people from the debris of the building that was under construction. Of them, two labourers, identified as Kishori (40) and Sanjeet (45), died, while Sahdev Chaudhary (25) and Firoz (37) are recovering from their injuries, police said.

AISTA seeks 35% hike in sugar MSP to ₹42/kg, backs Centre's cane price
items.summary:
Sugar trade body AISTA has asked the government to raise the minimum selling price of sugar to Rs 42 per kg from Rs 31, while backing the government's cane price as "fair and just", as a panel probes unrest among sugarcane farmers.
The All India Sugar Trade Association (AISTA) made the demands in a presentation to a four-member committee headed by former Niti Aayog member Ramesh Chand, set up on October 13 to address grievances of protesting growers, mainly in Karnataka and Maharashtra.
The panel met sugarcane growers in Bengaluru and later in Pune on November 4. An AISTA delegation attended the meeting in Pune.
AISTA Chairman Praful Vithalani said the minimum selling price of sugar had remained unchanged since February 2019 and should be raised to at least Rs 4,200 per quintal to ensure that mills do not sell sugar below their cost of production.

items.title: Rupee falls 9 paise to 94.50 against US dollar during early trade
items.summary:
The rupee depreciated 9 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar in early trade on Friday as the broad strength of the American currency in the overseas market dented investor sentiment.
Forex traders said overnight gains in crude oil prices and a recovery in the US dollar weighed on the domestic unit.
At the interbank foreign exchange market the rupee opened at 94.50 against the US dollar, registering a fall of 9 paise from its previous close.
However, during initial trade, it recovered slightly to touch a high of 94.36 against the US dollar.
On Thursday, the rupee had settled at 94.41 against the American currency.
The Bank of England kept policy rates unchanged while US weekly unemployment claims were better than forecasts, said Anuj Choudhary, Research Analyst, Mirae Asset Sharekhan.

items.title: D-St defies Asia rout! Sensex surges over 600 pts, Nifty above 24,650 as Diwali fireworks continue. What's ahead?
items.summary: The Indian stock market extended its ongoing rally this week, with Sensex and Nifty recording up to 0.5% gains even as global markets crashed as the AI frenzy fizzled out following US President Donald Trump’s defeat in the midterm elections.Sensex jumped over 600 points, while Nifty was above 24,650 during Friday's trading session. The benchmark indices have jumped up to 7% in the past five days.Mahindra & Mahindra shares jumped around 5% to lead gains on Sensex, while Titan, Infosys, HCL Tech, TCS and Bharti Airtel shares rose around 2% each to follow. Bucking the trend, Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance and Power Grid shares dropped more than 2% each to lead losses on the benchmark index.Also read | Infosys, Wipro, TCS and other IT stocks rise up to 3% amid US AI rout; is the bubble bursting?While benchmark indices extended gains, broader markets however, crashed. Nifty Smallcap 250 index plunged nearly 2% while Nifty Midcap 100 index dropped more than 1% on Friday morning. As a result, the overall market breadth turned negative, with NSE seeing 2,236 declines against 824 advances, while 94 stocks remained unchanged.Among the sectors, Nifty Metal plunged more than 2% to lead losses, while Nifty IT gained 1.5% to lead gains. India VIX, which measures volatility in the market, soared nearly 7% to near 17.What lies ahead for Dalal Street?The blood bath in the US markets will impact most other markets today, but India is likely to be the least impacted, said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. He noted that the big rout of 5.6% in Nasdaq was triggered on concerns of a big slowdown in data centre spending since the Democrats are opposed to massive data centre investment. This tech rout, particularly the sharp deceleration in AI trade will turn out to be beneficial for India, according to the analyst.“It is important to note that the FIIs have bought equities for Rs 35781 crores in the last five trading days. Despite selling and profit booking by DIIs the market is likely to remain resilient since FII buying will continue in the changed global market construct,” he added.Also read | Bulls roar! Market value of BSE-listed companies crosses Rs 500 lakh cr for first time. More upside ahead?It is important to recognise the fact that this ongoing rally has fundamental support from impressive earnings growth which has come better-than-expected. “A significant factor which investors should understand is that this rally is driven by large-caps which had become attractively valued. Note that yesterday while the Sensex rallied 2.6%, the Smallcap 100 index crawled by a measly 0.67%. It is evident where money is going. For financials, tech and auto stocks there is more upside,” Vijayakumar said.Technical view on NiftyNifty’s staying below 24,800 keeps the undertone subdued, said  Hemang Gor, Senior Research Analyst of Derivatives and Technical Research at Axis Direct. He said the support lies at 24,300 (a break risks 24,000).If the index manages to reclaim 24,700, then it can target 25,000, the analyst added.Disclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. The order follows an administrative meeting chaired by Chief Secretary Rajeev Verma on Thursday.

items.title: Infosys, Wipro, TCS and other IT stocks rise up to 3% amid US AI rout; is the bubble bursting?
items.summary: The shares of Indian IT companies, including Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro and others, rose up to 3% on Friday even as the global AI selloff intensified sharply, with Wall Street seeing its worst crash since 2020, boosting sentiment for the Indian IT stocks, which are seen to have the so-called ‘anti-AI’ advantage.In today's session, Infosys gained over 2%, while India's biggest IT company, TCS, rose 3% to Rs 2,565 per share. Wipro, HCL Tech, Coforge, and Persistent Systems gained up to 2% after the opening bell.Artificial intelligence-linked stocks plunged on fears of tougher AI regulation after Democrats won ‌control of the US Congress, defeating President Donald Trump’s Republican Party in the midterm elections. Democrats’ victory sparked concerns that tighter regulation could slow the AI infrastructure buildout that has helped lift stocks to record highs this year.Nasdaq fell 6%, marking its worst drop since the infamous Covid-19 crash in March 2020. The tech-heavy index also entered a technical ‘correction’ territory, a 10% drop from ⁠its October 6 record-high close.Nvidia shares plunged more than 9%, while the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index crashed over 12%. The selloff wiped off $3 trillion in stock market value from S&P 500 companies. South Korea’s Kospi, which was seen as the face of the sharp volatility around the AI frenzy, also felt the pain, crashing more than 9% to trigger a circuit breaker.Also read | US stocks suffer worst rout since 2020: Dow plunges 1,800 points, Nasdaq crashes 5.5% as AI fears wipe out $3 trillion"Investors appear to be recognizing that some newly elected members of Congress and governors are looking to slow the pace of AI infrastructure development," Reuters quoted Melissa Brown, global head of investment decision research at SimCorp."While it seems unlikely that they will be able to stop it altogether, any slowdown would raise concerns because the AI growth story has largely depended on the rapid buildout of supporting infrastructure,” she said.Why Indian IT stocks stand to benefitEarlier this year, when Anthropic’s launch of new plugins for Claude triggered sharp hopes for artificial intelligence, India’s much-touted IT services companies saw a massive rout in their share prices as analysts worried that innovations could lead to displacement in the sector. "We call it the ‘SaaSpocalypse,’ an apocalypse for software-as-a-service stocks," Bloomberg quoted Jeffrey Favuzza from the equity trading desk at Jefferies as saying.However, as the AI frenzy began to fizzle out, analysts were quick to point out India’s so-called ‘anti-AI’ advantage. This has been boosting a recovery in these stocks while experts scream about a bubble-burst crisis ahead amid the massive spending behind AI infrastructure. Michael Burry, popular for correctly predicting the 2008 housing crisis, has been ramping up his warnings over the excessive optimism regarding AI. Recently, he said that the market is currently in a 'denial' mood, a phase that could last six to nine months as seen during the previous 2000 and 2008 crises.Also read | AI bubble is coming, and there is no way out! Aswath Damodaran explains what investors should do before the crash beginsAmid the growing concerns over the excessive frenzy around artificial intelligence, valuation expert Ashwath Damodaran said in a recent podcast that the AI bubble is coming and there is no way one can avoid it completely.These rising worries around the AI bubble will likely be a positive for Indian IT companies. Veteran banker Uday Kotak expects India to benefit from the reverse flows as the AI frenzy fizzles out, while working down the path of building its own AI capabilities. This comes as worries around excessive spending by hyperscalers on artificial intelligence grow louder, with several analysts warning of a bubble-burst situation ahead.Also read | Uday Kotak says $700 bn outstanding FII payments will boost market, sees AI worries driving flows to IndiaDisclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. items.title: Turkish lawmakers approve defence pact with Pakistan, Saudi Arabia
items.summary:
Turkish legislators on Thursday ratified a defense cooperation agreement among Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia as Riyadh seeks increased regional support in its conflict with Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen.
The vote also came as countries in the region remain anxious about the prospects of a new escalation in the US-Iran war, which would likely spill over into neighboring countries. During previous rounds of fighting, Iran has lashed out at US-allied Gulf Arab countries, including Saudi Arabia.
The 16-article Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, signed in August, commits the three countries to regard an attack against one as an attack on all three, to work together to deter threats and deepen military cooperation, share intelligence and strengthen defense industry ties.
It was approved by 279 votes to 119 in the 600-seat parliament, despite objections from opposition parties who argued that the agreement could embroil Turkey in regional wars and put Turkish soldiers in .

items.summary: DUBAI, - Iran has sent the United States a nuclear proposal via Qatar, to be discussed only after Washington meets Tehran's seven demands, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Thursday.The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the US was reviewing the proposal but declined to provide further details.Mediators have intensified efforts to end the war between Iran and the United States amid fears it could reignite after the US midterm elections, with Trump on Tuesday declining to rule out a resumption of combat operations after the vote and Iran planning wider retaliation if war resumes.Iran's top security official Mohsen Rezaei had said earlier on Thursday, during a visit to Russia: "On the issue of diplomacy, we have announced seven conditions to the Americans. As long as they do not execute our seven conditions, we will neither open the Strait of Hormuz nor have negotiations".Iran has demanded the lifting of US sanctions, the release of frozen Iranian assets and war reparations, among other conditions, while Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations.The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, and Iran responded with strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. Conflict also erupted in Lebanon between Iran-backed Hezbollah and Israel, and more recently spread to Yemen, from where the Iran-aligned Houthis have struck energy facilities, airports and other targets in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Nithya Raman elected Mayor of Los Angeles
items.summary: New York: Indian-born democratic socialist Nithya Raman has been elected Mayor of Los Angeles, scripting history as she becomes the first South Asian mayor of the nation's second-largest city.Raman, 45, who was a Los Angeles City Council member, defeated incumbent 73-year-old Karen Bass in the November 3 mid-term elections.Also read: Democrats' US midterm sweep may give India more room to negotiate a balanced trade deal with TrumpWith this victory, America's two largest cities - New York and Los Angeles - are now run by Indian-descent mayors who are Democratic Socialists."Los Angeles, I am deeply honoured to be your next Mayor. Thank you to the thousands of people who knocked on doors, sent texts, made phone calls, convinced their neighbours to believe in the promise of this big, beautiful, joyful city that we get to call home," Raman said in a video posted on X Thursday.Raman paid tribute to her predecessor Bass, the first woman mayor of Los Angeles, for her decades-long public service."I am going to City Hall to work every single day to earn your trust and to earn your trust in this city again. And that work starts now, so that we can build housing that people can afford, parks for our children to play in, a transit system that can get people where they need to go, a city that is safe for its working people and its families, and a city government that is actually capable of delivering on its promises," Raman said.LA City Councilmember for District 4, Kerala-born Raman is an urban planner by training, and she received her bachelor's degree from Harvard and a graduate degree from MIT.Raman is among the several Indian-American candidates who have emerged victorious across the country in the US midterm elections that concluded Tuesday and delivered a significant rebuke to President Donald Trump and the Republicans as the Democrats gained control of the House and Senate, flipping seats and traditional party strongholds in a massive blue wave across America.Also read: Marco Rubio weighs leaving administration after GOP’s midterm lossIndian American Impact, an organisation that empowers South Asian and Indian-American communities through community engagement, civic partnerships, and candidate support, congratulated Raman on her victory in the general election for Mayor of Los Angeles.Noting that Raman will become the first South Asian American mayor of the nation's second-largest city, the Indian American Impact said her victory reflects the growing political power of South Asian Americans in California, a state with more than one million South Asian residents, the largest such population in the country.Executive Director of Indian American Impact Chintan Patel said in a statement that Raman ran on lowering rents, building housing faster, and making city services work for Angelenos, and voters chose her to deliver it."With her win, South Asian Americans will lead the two largest cities in the United States," Patel said, referring to New York and its Mayor Mamdani.The 5.5 million-strong Indian-American community registered significant political gains in the midterms, with several candidates from the community winning historic elections to various positions across the country.Pia Dandiya of Florida and Dr Amish Shah of Arizona will be the newest Indian-American members of the US Congress, with their victories speaking to the "growing political power of our communities."They will join Representative Ami Bera, Representative Pramila Jayapal, Representative Ro Khanna and Representative Suhas Subramanyam at Capitol Hill."At a time of rising hate against our communities, representation matters, and they will fight to keep our communities safe," Indian American Impact said. "All six are committed to lowering costs for working families, expanding access to health care, and protecting immigrants, and they will serve as a powerful check on the Trump administration in the next Congress," the organisation said.Among the other notable election victories are that of Manoj Chourasia, who has been reelected to the New Hampshire State House, Darshana Patel who won her reelection to the California State Assembly, Ranjeev Puri whose won reelection to the Michigan House of Representatives.With Democrats retaking the chamber, Puri is expected to become Michigan's next Speaker of the House, which would make him the first Indian American Speaker of a state House in the country.Dr Krish Subrahmanian won his election for the Minnesota State Senate; Aruna Miller has been reelected as Lieutenant Governor of Maryland; Lisa Kaul won her election for the New York State Senate, defeating a Republican incumbent and flipping a seat in New York; and Nabeela Syed won her election for Illinois State Senate District 26.Amar Mukunda won his election to the Maryland State Senate; Saba Haider has been elected to the Illinois State House; Josh Kaul has been re-elected as Wisconsin's Attorney General; Pooja Sethi won her election to the Texas House, District 47, becoming the first Indian American to serve in the Texas legislature; and Jyot Singh has been elected to the Georgia State House, District 97, the first Indian American and first Sikh American elected to the Georgia State Legislature.

M-cap of BSE-listed companies tops Rs 500 lakh crore mark
items.summary: Mumbai: The combined market capitalisation of all companies listed on the BSE crossed ₹500 lakh crore for the first time Thursday, reaching around ₹502 lakh crore ($5.31 trillion) amid a broad-based rally in equities and a steady addition of newly listed companies.It took 622 trading sessions for the total mcap to rise from ₹400 lakh crore, first crossed on April 8, 2024, to the latest milestone. The mcap first crossed ₹100 lakh crore on March 12, 2014, and took 1,494 sessions to reach ₹200 lakh crore on February 4, 2021. The ₹300 lakh crore milestone was reached on July 6, 2023, after another 586 sessions, while the subsequent rise to ₹400 lakh crore took 181 sessions.135589318The latest milestone is significant because it comes even as the benchmark Sensex and several broader market indices remain below their record highs. The Sensex is still 7.6% below its peak of 85,836, recorded on September 26, 2024.The BSE MidCap 150 is 5.3% below its record of 17,373, reached on August 26, 2026, while the BSE SmallCap 250 is 8.4% below its peak of 7,514, recorded on September 23, 2024. The BSE MicroCap 250 is 7% below its record of 19,988, reached on September 8, 2026.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than everA steady stream of initial public offerings (IPOs) has also contributed to the expansion of the overall mcap, even as several benchmark indices remain below their peaks. In 2024, 94 companies made their mainboard debut, adding around ₹12 lakh crore to mcap on their listing days. In 2025, 115 companies listed, adding nearly ₹14 lakh crore, while 107 companies have listed so far in 2026, adding above ₹25 lakh crore."The large number of IPOs has added to the overall mcap. At the same time, several companies outside the main indices have participated in the rally, helping total mcap reach a record even as major indices remain below their peaks," said Ankur Punj, MD, Equirus Wealth.The latest milestone has also coincided with a sharp recovery in equities. The Sensex and Nifty have gained more than 8.1% each in six consecutive sessions. The BSE MidCap 150 has advanced over 8.4% in eight of the past nine sessions, while the BSE SmallCap 250 has risen around 7% in seven of past eight sessions.Read more: Titan Q2 Results: Profit jumps 54% YoY to Rs 1,722 crore; total income up 25%The rally has been supported by a decline of more than 19% in crude oil prices over the past three sessions, easing concerns over inflation, India's import bill and the rupee. Strong foreign portfolio investor (FPI) buying, with net inflows of over $3.4 billion in the past 12 sessions, positive global cues, reduced uncertainty following the US midterm elections and better-than-expected second-quarter earnings have also lifted investor sentiment."The momentum could continue in the near term if crude prices remain stable at lower levels and foreign inflows sustain. However, investors should remain cautious as geopolitical developments, crude price volatility and profit booking after the sharp rally could limit further upside," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services.

items.title: Demat account additions hit 9-month high in October as IPO boom draws investors
items.summary: Mumbai: New demat account additions rose to a nine-month high in October, marking the fourth monthly increase in five months after a prolonged period of moderation between January 2025 and May 2026, as robust IPO activity drew more investors to the stock market.NSDL and CDSL together added nearly 3.36 million demat accounts in October, the highest monthly addition since January 2026. The total number of demat accounts stood at around 244 million at the end of the month. The number of demat accounts does not represent unique investors, as individuals can hold multiple accounts. The number of unique investors is estimated at around 136.6 million as of September, according to NSE data.Robust primary market activity was a key driver of the increase, with several large and smaller public issues attracting retail participation. October was the busiest month for IPO activity in 2026, with 13 issues raising a record ₹44,507 crore, including the Jio Platforms IPO - India's biggest ever.Read more: Why Nithin Kamath believes NRI investing in India has become easier than ever"Demat account openings typically rise when there is a surge in IPO activity, as investors open accounts to participate in public issues. The recent listing activity, including the large Jio Platform IPO and several smaller issues, has contributed to the increase," said Sunny Agrawal, head of fundamental equity research at SBICAPS Securities.Growing interest in gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) has also encouraged retail investors to open demat accounts, Agrawal said. Investors can purchase these products through the secondary market using a demat account.Read more: Equity mutual fund inflows may drop 18% in October as midcap and hybrid funds lose momentum: NomuraThe pickup in demat account additions came with gains in benchmark indices, with the Sensex rising 2% and the Nifty gaining 1.9% in October. However, broader market segments, which see greater retail participation, underperformed.

items.title: Fed's Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin favour gradual rate hikes as inflation stays high
items.summary: Federal Reserve officials Beth Hammack and Thomas Barkin are making the case for a gradual approach to interest rate increases, signalling that policymakers remain focused on bringing inflation under control even as uncertainty over the economic outlook grows, Reuters reported.Their comments on Thursday come as the US central bank faces competing pressures from persistent price increases, geopolitical tensions and heavy investment in artificial intelligence (AI). The remarks also mark the first round of comments from Fed officials after Democrats won control of Congress and made gains in state level elections. For live updates on US Markets, click here "I expect that monetary policy will need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2% in a timely manner," Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said in a speech ahead of an event in Zurich.According to Reuters, Hammack, a consistent supporter of higher borrowing costs, favours smaller and more frequent adjustments rather than sharp increases. She said this approach would be less disruptive to households, businesses and financial markets. Gradual increases could also prevent an “inflationary mindset” from taking hold, she added.Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin echoed that view, saying inflation remained “too high” and was holding firm rather than easing. "When it comes to the pace of future rate hikes, gradual makes sense," he said.Inflation keeps pressure on the FedThe comments follow the Fed's decision last week to keep its benchmark interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Hammack, along with Fed Governor Lisa Cook, voted in favour of a rate increase, highlighting the divide among policymakers over how aggressively to tackle inflation.Also Read: Emerging markets lose $33.8 billion in October as investors flee Asian stocksFinancial markets broadly expect another increase in December, although expectations beyond that remain less certain. Reuters reported that futures traders have lowered the probability of a December hike to around 70% from more than 80% on Wednesday.AI investment and elections add to uncertaintyThe political shift could also influence the inflation outlook. Local voter opposition to data centres and permitting challenges could slow AI infrastructure spending, potentially easing demand for equipment and related resources.Evercore ISI analysts told clients on Wednesday that AI capital expenditure could slow in the next year or two, helping keep demand and supply in balance without requiring many more rate increases.TD Securities said it expects the Fed to raise rates by another 50 basis points by early next year. However, the brokerage said a resolution to the Iran war or a slowdown in AI investment could reduce the need for further tightening after March.Meanwhile, Friday's US jobs report is expected to provide another test for policymakers, with economists forecasting 65,000 additional jobs in October after September's 29,000 gain, Reuters reported.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.title: LTCG cut may come with a separate tax tweak
items.summary: New Delhi/Mumbai: Key stakeholders are offering divergent prescriptions on how to address concerns over long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) tax and securities transaction tax (STT).These include scrapping LTCG altogether, removing it just for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), or lowering the rate. As for STT, suggestions include reducing it for some products and increasing it for others, people familiar with the discussions said."A well thought-out call would be taken," said an official. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said she will consider investors' concerns regarding LTCG. These measures are being considered as a way of stemming the exodus of overseas investors that has led to a slump in Indian stock markets.While the LTCG collections amounted to ₹1.29 lakh crore in FY25, those for STT stood at ₹57,522 crore. Any call on the levies would have to take into account the revenue impact and funding for social sector schemes and subsidies.Finance ministry officials have met senior market participants to seek their views on capital market taxation. ET had reported on October 28 that the finance ministry officials had reached out to stakeholders on the issue.Financial sector regulators including the Reserve Bank of India and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) are understood to have backed the idea of doing away with LTCG to make India an attractive destination for foreign investors.Most participants favoured abolishing LTCG on equities while suggesting that the government could consider a marginal increase in STT on options trading alone, leaving cash and futures transactions untouched. They argued that options account for the bulk of daily trading activity and have been the focus of regulatory efforts to curb excessive speculation, people said.Some participants have cautioned against extending preferential tax treatment to FPIs alone, saying such a move could draw criticism from domestic investors. Short-term capital gains on listed equities, held for up to one year, are currently taxed at 20%, while long-term gains on holdings exceeding one year attract a 12.5% levy.Foreign portfolio investors have argued that several competing markets in the region do not levy LTCG, putting India at a disadvantage.Market participants said the combination of rupee depreciation and capital gains taxation has weighed on foreign investors' dollar-denominated post-tax returns, making other markets more attractive. One of the suggestions that has been put forth is calculating an FPI's taxable capital gains in dollar terms rather than rupees, said one of the persons.Separately, some FPI representatives also sought simplification of procedures governing the inflow and repatriation of foreign capital, calling for easier processes to bring funds into India and take money out of the country. Market participants said senior finance ministry officials have patiently heard out their suggestions.Another official said the implications of all suggestions would be examined before a final decision is reached.

items.title: Mehli Mistry challenges Tata Trust exit
items.summary: Mumbai: Former Tata trustee Mehli Mistry has challenged his removal as a trustee of Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Bai Hirabai Charitable Institution (BHJTNCI), arguing that the decision was invalid and that some trustees who voted against his reappointment were themselves ineligible.In a series of rejoinders filed with the deputy charity commissioner for Greater Mumbai Region, Mistry has argued that the trust deed does not prescribe a fixed tenure for trustees or specify citizenship or tax residency as a qualification for trusteeship.He also accused Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) of attempting to prevent scrutiny of alleged governance lapses, including commissions and financial benefits received by trustees. The matter has been adjourned to December 3. Challenging the recording of his cessation as a BHJTNCI trustee with effect from October 28, 2025, Mistry argued that neither the trust's 1913 will nor its 1923 trust deed prescribes a fixed tenure for trustees.The trust's position that his three-year term had expired relied on a 2022 circular and appointment letter, but neither of them can override the governing instruments, he argued.Citing Clause 23 of the deed, Mistry said vacancies arise on grounds including death, permanent residence outside the Bombay Presidency, insolvency, renunciation of faith and unfitness, but not on expiry of a fixed term. The codicil also says trustees "shall always be trustees," he added.Mistry argued that he is not a "tenure trustee" under Section 2(17A) introduced through an 2025 amendment and that Section 30A(1), therefore, does not apply to him. He also cited the trust's annexures, which allegedly show different renewal periods for other trustees, including about two years for Vijay Singh and less than two years for Venu Srinivasan."The trust cannot use Section 30A(1) as a sword to oust the objector on October 28, 2025, and, in the same breath, ignore that very provision when its own vice chairman (Singh) acted in breach of it on that very day. A party cannot approbate and reprobate," Mistry said in his submission.He also cited a resolution passed on October 17, 2024, at a joint meeting of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust trustees, shortly after Ratan Tata's death. The resolution provided for trustees to be reappointed on expiry of their terms without any limit on tenure, he said.The trust deliberately omitted it from its reply to his complaint, Mistry claimed.He urged the authority to reject BHJTNCI's change report against him as "illegal, non-est and contrary to the trust deed."According to Mistry, Circular Resolution No 671 of October 23, 2025, proposing his reappointment, was approved by Jehangir H C Jehangir and Darius Khambata but was not approved by Noel Tata, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. Jimmy Tata did not respond.He said the trust failed to follow the 2024 resolution's requirement of unanimous approval.In a 24-page rejoinder filed under Section 22 of the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950, Mistry also contested the trust's objections to his citizenship and tax residency, saying the will, codicil or trust deed does not prescribe these as criteria for trusteeship."If foreign citizenship and overseas residence are to be treated as relevant considerations, they must be examined in relation to the reporting trustee with equal rigour," he further said and alleged that Noel Tata, the current reporting trustee, is an Irish citizen, a UAE tax resident and a UAE Golden Visa holder.He sought an affidavit from Tata detailing his citizenship and tax residency history, including whether he has held a Swiss passport.

items.summary:
Bakery food company Britannia Industries Ltd on Thursday reported an increase of 10.82 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 725.99 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis, led by volume growth.
The company had posted a net profit of Rs 655.06 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Britannia Industries.
Britannia Industries' revenue from the sale of products was up 16.6 per cent to Rs 5,541.57 crore in the September quarter.
The sales growth was "led by volume growth of 13 per cent", said Britannia Industries in its earnings statement.
Its revenue from operations was up 15.64 per cent to Rs 5,597.79 crore in the second quarter of FY27. It was at Rs 4,840.63 crore in the corresponding quarter.
Britannia's total expenses were at Rs 4,690.47 crore, up 17 per cent in Q2, FY27.
Its total income, which includes other income, was up 15.9 per cent to Rs 5,671.30 crore in the September quarter.

items.title: Rubio to quit Trump team for 2028 run?
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio may be looking to quit the Trump administration and run for presidency in 2028, a report by The Independent said. US midterm elections were disastrous for Republicans as they lost control of both the House and the Senate. Rubio needs to distance himself from controversial policies of Trump administration like US Iran war, the report said citing insiders. The move may help to improve his prospects in the 2028 Republican presidential nomination against main rival US Vice President J. D. Vance.Marco Rubio ResignationUS secretary of state and White House national security adviser seems to be looking for an early exit from President Donald Trump's cabinet to lay the groundwork for a 2028 Republican presidential run, The Independent report said citing unnamed party insiders and sources. Rubio may need to distance himself from the Trump administration to avoid the fallout of foreign policy issues like US Iran war, the sources said.Who will exit Trump administration?Around five cabinet members are looking to exit the administration to avoid congressional investigations or impeachment efforts under a newly elected Democratic majority, the report said citing insiders. The White House and the State Department have strongly denied the report. The speculation of the departures has been dismissed and called baseless.The speculation comes after devastating US midterm results for Republicans as they lost control of both the House and the Senate. White House spokesperson Davis Ingle dismissed the claims as "baseless, false conspiracy theories," an Anadolu Agency report said. State Department Assistant Secretary Dylan Johnson characterized the reports as "completely baseless fake news from made-up anonymous 'sources'".J. D. Vance may be his main rivalVice President J. D. Vance may be currently his main rival in the race to be the Republican nominee in November 2028, the report said citing senior party sources in the US and senior figures in the UK government.Vice president JD Vance has already blamed the war in Iran for the disastrous results to distance himself from it. Trump may also pin the blame for the policy and US midterm election loss on Rubio, defense secretary Pete Hegseth and White House chief of staff Susie Wiles. These all the officials may be the potential scapegoats, the report said.

Nvidia stock falls below $200: What's next?
items.summary: Nvidia stock (NVDA) has fallen below a level investors have been watching closely, as concerns over the future of AI spending weigh on the chipmaker. Shares dropped below $200 during Thursday's trading after Democratic victories in the US midterm elections raised questions about whether new data center projects could face greater restrictions. Wall Street, however, still sees considerable upside in the stock.NVDA Stock Price Falls TodayNvidia shares fell more than 6% to around $186 in early trading Thursday. If the decline holds, it would be the first time the stock has closed below $200 since July 30, according to Barron's.The concern is that fewer data center projects could eventually mean fewer orders for Nvidia's processors and networking equipment. Companies such as SpaceX and CoreWeave are already facing investor concerns over possible construction delays, putting pressure on shares of businesses closely tied to the AI infrastructure expansion.However, delayed projects do not necessarily mean that spending will disappear. Technology companies could shift construction to other states or overseas. Gavekal US chief economist Will Denyer told Barron's that some states and counties would remain willing to welcome data centers because of the tax revenue they bring.135579574135576908Nvidia Stock Price Today Faces Pressure Despite Strong Revenue GrowthThe latest decline comes at a time when Nvidia's business continues to grow rapidly. The company has forecast 70% revenue growth for fiscal 2028, largely corresponding to calendar 2027, and has indicated that supply constraints, rather than a lack of demand, are limiting its growth.Nvidia generated $96.22 billion in revenue in its latest quarter, up 105.8% from a year earlier. It also recorded its fifth consecutive earnings beat. Its third quarter revenue guidance stands at $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, assuming no data center compute revenue from China.The chipmaker closed Wednesday at $200.13, down 3.17%, after touching an intraday low of $199.68. The decline came even as S&P 500 gained 1.58% and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 1.44%.The stock is now about 16.3% below its October 6 record closing price of $239.24 and trades below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, according to 24/7 Wall St report.135575113NVDA Stock Could Rebound as Analysts Maintain Bullish TargetsDespite the recent selling, Wall Street analysts remain optimistic about Nvidia. FactSet data cited by Barron's puts the average price target at approximately $333. Meanwhile, 24/7 Wall St. reported a consensus target of $327.14, suggesting roughly 63.5% upside from Wednesday's closing price.Nvidia's next quarterly earnings report, scheduled for November 17, could offer investors a better understanding of whether demand is holding up despite concerns about data center construction.CEO Jensen Huang said during the August earnings call that demand growth was much higher than 70%, but available supply allowed the company to confidently deliver that level of growth.There are still risks. Nvidia has $279 billion in supply commitments and expects fourth-quarter gross margins to bottom between 71% and 72%. If data center construction slows and major technology companies cut their budgets, those commitments could become a burden.135572618135551377

items.title: US jobless claims hit 57-year low
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment slipped to a 57-year last week as layoffs remained low against the backdrop of a resilient labor market.Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 189,000 for the week ended October 31, the Labor Department said on Thursday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 196,000 claims for the latest week.Claims matched the 189,000 level touched in mid-July, which was the lowest reading since 1969.They have stayed mostly below 200,000 since mid-September.Low layoffs, thanks to strong domestic demand and profit growth, are anchoring the labor market, with hiring still constrained by uncertainty over the dragging US-Israeli war with Iran.The government reported this week that there were 1.06 open jobs for every unemployed person in September, up from 1.02 in August, which some economists argued was a sign of the labor market starting to tighten. Others, however, viewed the low level of jobless claims as a function of a smaller labor force amid an immigration crackdown, rather than fewer job cuts.A separate report from global outplacement firm Challenger, Gray and Christmas on Thursday showed US-based employers announced 43,994 job cuts in October, up 2% from September. Planned layoffs dropped 71% compared to October 2025.Despite the rise over the month, layoffs were the lowest for any October since 2023. Employers announced plans to hire 444,692 workers last month, a 57% jump from October 2025. Hiring plans were the highest for any October since 2009, and likely mostly seasonal jobs."Employers are holding on to the workers they have heading into the holidays, and the hiring they are announcing is largely short-term, seasonal work," said Andy Challenger, chief revenue officer at Challenger, Gray & Christmas. "Companies want the flexibility to meet holiday demand without adding permanent headcount."The reluctance to increase permanent hiring means some unemployed people are experiencing long periods of joblessness.The claims report showed the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 23,000 to a still-low seasonally adjusted 1.718 million during the week ended October 24. The so-called continuing claims, however, do not include some unemployed people, including recent college graduates and others who have little or no work history.Some people might also have exhausted their eligibility for benefits, limited to 26 weeks in most states, keeping continuing claims at relatively low levels.The claims report has no bearing on the government's closely watched employment report for October due on Friday as it falls outside the survey period. Nonfarm payrolls likely increased by 65,000 jobs last month after rising 29,000 in September, a Reuters survey of economists showed. The unemployment rate is forecast unchanged at 4.2

items.title: Mahindra realty arm buys 100 acres in Bom
items.summary: Mahindra Lifespace Developers, the real estate and infrastructure development arm of the Mahindra Group, has acquired 100 acres of land along the Karjat-Murbad road in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) for a plotted development project, marking its entry into the segment in the region.The company is likely to start the project around the middle of the next financial year. It is also looking to acquire additional land in the area, according to people familiar with the development.The land acquisition is part of Mahindra Lifespace Developers’ efforts to expand its residential development pipeline across key markets. The company has been pursuing projects through outright land acquisitions, joint development agreements and partnerships with landowners.“In line with our strategy, we look to expand into plotted development in future in MMR, Pune and Bengaluru. Homebuyers today are increasingly seeking greater flexibility and personalization in their residential requirements. Plotted developments offer a compelling proposition through land ownership, customization, and long-term appreciation potential,” said Vimalendra Singh, Chief Business Officer - Residential, Mahindra Lifespace Developers.The proposed development will be the company’s first plotted project outside Mahindra World City in Chennai. In Chennai, Mahindra Lifespace Developers has established a presence in the segment through two projects.The Mumbai-region project marks the company’s entry into a segment that has attracted interest from homebuyers seeking land ownership and the option of building independent homes.Plotted developments have emerged as an alternative to conventional residential projects, with homebuyers showing interest in owning land and having the flexibility to construct homes according to their requirements.Developers are also looking at plotted projects as a way to enter markets where large land parcels are available, without undertaking construction of apartment buildings. The format allows developers to sell individual plots in phases, while buyers can decide the timing and design of construction, subject to applicable regulations.Several developers have been exploring plotted development opportunities as part of their residential portfolios, particularly in locations on the outskirts of major cities, attracting institutional capital and investments from real estate funds into land acquisition and development projects.

items.title: LIC Q2 Results: Profit jumps 20% YoY to Rs 12,115 crore, NPI grows 16%
items.summary: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), the country's largest insurer, reported a nearly 20% rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 12,114.78 crore for the September quarter on Thursday, supported by strong growth in premium income and higher investment earnings. The state-owned insurer had reported a net profit of Rs 10,098 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. However, profit declined 11% sequentially from Rs 13,584 crore in the June quarter.Net premium income increased 16.2% year-on-year to Rs 1.47 lakh crore from Rs 1.26 lakh crore in the September quarter of FY26. It rose 15% sequentially from Rs 1.27 lakh crore.The growth in premium income was largely driven by a sharp increase in single-premium collections, reflecting higher contributions from policies where customers pay the entire premium upfront.Single-premium income surged 34% to Rs 68,425 crore from Rs 50,882 crore a year earlier. Renewal premium income increased 5% to Rs 68,718 crore from Rs 65,320 crore in the same quarter last year. However, first-year premium income declined 4% to Rs 10,484 crore from Rs 10,884 crore.LIC also reported an increase in investment income during the quarter, providing additional support to profitability.Net investment income in the shareholders' account increased to Rs 2,855 crore from Rs 2,066 crore a year earlier, representing a rise of about 38%.Total income in the shareholders' account increased 11% to Rs 10,527 crore from Rs 9,454 crore. Meanwhile, the insurer's income from investments in the policyholders' account stood at Rs 1.15 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.12 lakh crore in the year-ago quarter, an increase of around 2.2%.The company reported a surplus of Rs 10,379 crore in the policyholders' account, compared with Rs 9,503 crore a year earlier. The increase in investment income and policyholder surplus contributed to the company's overall financial performance during the quarter.LIC's benefits paid, including claims and other policyholder payouts, increased to Rs 1.34 lakh crore from Rs 1.06 lakh crore in the corresponding quarter last year.Expenses of management rose to Rs 15,143.38 crore from Rs 13,908 crore, an increase of 9%. Net commission expenses increased to Rs 6,089 crore from Rs 5,807 crore a year earlier.LIC's solvency ratio improved to 2.35 as of September 2026, from 2.13 a year earlier. However, the ratio declined sequentially from 2.42 in the June quarter. The insurer's expense of management ratio improved to 10.26% from 12.05% a year earlier, reflecting better cost efficiency.The 13th-month persistency ratio declined to 67.67% from 68.19% a year earlier, while the 25th-month ratio improved marginally to 63.01% from 62.63%.The insurer's investment yield, excluding unrealised gains, declined to 9.04% in the September quarter from 9.33% a year earlier. However, including unrealised gains, the yield increased to 4.10% from 2.07%.

Mistry challenges removal as SDTT trustee
items.summary: New Delhi: Mehli Mistry has challenged his removal as a trustee of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, alleging procedural irregularities and violations of trust governance rules.In three rejoinders and applications filed before the Deputy Charity Commissioner, Mistry has questioned the legality of the decisions leading to his removal, the eligibility of certain trustees and their participation in decisions concerning his reappointment.He has also sought an independent inquiry into SDTT's administration, alleging conflicts of interest, improper retention of financial benefits by trustees and irregularities in decisions involving Tata Group companies and the trust's investments in Tata Sons.A key issue raised by Mistry concerns Venu Srinivasan's participation in the decision on his reappointment. Mistry has argued that Srinivasan's tenure as a trustee ended on October 23, 2025, while he communicated his vote against Mistry's reappointment on October 28.Read more: Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran meets Italian PM Meloni after Iveco acquisitionAccording to Mistry, the trust's own records acknowledged that Srinivasan was no longer a trustee when he cast his vote. He has pointed out that a footnote in the records stated that Srinivasan's vote should be disregarded for this reason.However, Mistry contends that removing the vote from the final count does not address the larger issue, as Srinivasan was still included in the decision-making process. He has argued that the entire resolution was invalid because the body considering his reappointment was not properly constituted.Mistry has also disputed the trust's position that his three-year tenure ended on October 28, 2025, requiring a fresh resolution for reappointment. He has cited the SDTT Trust Deed of March 11, 1932, arguing that it does not prescribe a fixed tenure for trustees.He has further relied on an October 17, 2024, joint resolution of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust, which provided for the reappointment of trustees after the expiry of their tenure without any limitation on the renewed term, subject to applicable law.Read more: Finance Minister Sitharaman urges Tata to resolve feud amicably, rules out govt interventionIn a separate challenge concerning the Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution, Mistry has questioned the eligibility of trustees under the trust deed. He has cited provisions requiring trustees to profess the Parsi Zoroastrian faith and meet specified residency conditions.On this basis, he has questioned the eligibility of Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. He has also raised questions about Noel Tata's alleged Irish citizenship and UAE residency, arguing that eligibility requirements should be applied uniformly to all trustees.Mistry has sought affidavits from trustees confirming that they meet the qualifications prescribed under the trust deed. He has also disputed the trust's position that the relevant eligibility provisions are invalid or unenforceable.Separately, Mistry has sought an inquiry into the financial affairs of SDTT, particularly commissions and other benefits allegedly received by trustees serving as nominee directors in Tata Group companies.His application refers to an annual commission of approximately Rs 1.42 crore received by Noel Tata from Tata Sons Private Limited during FY 2024-25, as reflected in corporate filings.He has also raised questions concerning the engagement of Gerry McGovern for Norton Motorcycles, equity infusion into Tata International Limited and alleged deviations from unanimous resolutions on voting the trust's shareholding in Tata Sons.Mistry has argued that such matters could involve conflicts of interest and breaches of fiduciary duties. He has urged the Charity Commissioner to examine corporate filings, declarations of interest, board records and relevant approvals.He has sought rejection of SDTT's preliminary objections and an inquiry or inspection under the Maharashtra Public Trusts Act, 1950.Importantly, Mistry has clarified that he is not seeking reinstatement as an SDTT trustee. Instead, he has sought an examination of the trust's administration and the appointment of an independent administrator, if required, to ensure its proper functioning.Mistry's trusteeship of SDTT and Sir Ratan Tata Trust ended in October 2025 after three trustees opposed his reappointment. On November 4, 2025, he had written to Tata Trusts trustees, including chairman Noel Tata, describing his departure as a harmonious exit and saying he did not wish to drag the charitable institutions into controversy.In the letter, he stressed the need to protect the reputation of the institutions and uphold transparency, good governance and public interest. He also cited a quote attributed to the late Ratan Tata: "Nobody is bigger than the institution it serves."Mistry had earlier filed a caveat before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, seeking an opportunity to be heard before any changes were made to the register of trustees.

items.title: Bharti Airtel Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 31% YoY to Rs 8,887 crore; revenue up 17%; ARPU rises to Rs 271
items.summary: Bharti Airtel reported a 31% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit to Rs 8,887.5 crore for the September quarter (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 6,791.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.The telecom major's consolidated revenue for the quarter rose 16.7% YoY to Rs 60,878 crore, up from Rs 52,145 crore reported in Q2FY26.India mobile revenue grew 10.1% YoY, while ARPU increased to Rs 271 in Q2FY27 from Rs 256 in the year-ago quarter, reflecting improved customer realisations.Operating performance remained strong, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) growing 17.8% YoY to Rs 35,240 crore in Q2FY27, compared with Rs 29,919 crore in the year-ago period.India revenue increased 9.4% YoY to Rs 42,308 crore, with the company's mobile business continuing to benefit from premiumisation of its customer portfolio, higher average revenue per user (ARPU) and strong additions in smartphone data customers.The company's Homes business remained another key growth driver, with revenue increasing 25.3% YoY. The segment added 676,000 customers during the quarter, taking its total customer base to 15.4 million.Airtel Business reported an 11.4% YoY increase in revenue, driven by broad-based growth across its core connectivity business and digital services portfolio. Digital TV revenue rose 2.4% YoY to Rs 771 crore, supported by growing adoption of IPTV services.Africa continued to deliver strong growth, with revenue increasing 25.7% YoY in reported currency and 20.6% in constant currency. The business had a customer base of 193.9 million.Airtel's balance sheet also strengthened during the quarter. Its consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA ratio, on an annualised basis, improved to 1.18 from 1.63 as of September 30, 2025. The net debt-to-EBITDAaL ratio, excluding lease obligations, stood at 0.70.The company reported consolidated capital expenditure of Rs 12,467 crore during the quarter, including Rs 9,908 crore in India. It also invested Rs 2,826 crore in a strategic land parcel for its data centre expansion plans in the country.Postpaid additions hit record; smartphone data base expandsOn the operational front, Airtel added 2.9 million smartphone data customers sequentially, taking the number of such users to 81% of its overall mobile customer base. Smartphone data customer additions stood at 18.8 million over the past year.The postpaid segment recorded net additions of 1.2 million customers during the quarter, its strongest-ever performance in a single quarter, taking the overall postpaid base to 31.2 million.Mobile data consumption increased 36.5% YoY to 36.5 GB per customer per month.The company added 497 towers and 11,684 mobile broadband base stations during the quarter. Its network expansion over the past year included 5,649 additional towers and 44,718 kilometres of fibre.Across its operations in 15 countries, Airtel's total customer base expanded to 693 million, supported by quarterly net additions of 12 million customers across India and Africa.Management commentaryCommenting on the performance, Gopal Vittal, Executive Vice Chairman of Bharti Airtel, said the company delivered another quarter of consistent growth, supported by its diversified business portfolio.He highlighted Africa's strong performance, with revenue growing 6.7% sequentially in constant currency, attributing the improvement partly to the deployment of Airtel's homegrown technology stack across markets. India business revenue also recorded healthy sequential growth of 2.7%.Vittal said the India mobile business continued to benefit from the company's portfolio premiumisation strategy and focus on acquiring quality customers. The segment recorded 3.4% sequential revenue growth, while postpaid additions touched a record 1.2 million during the quarter.He also pointed to sustained momentum in the Homes business, which added 676,000 customers, and Airtel Business, which reported 3.8% sequential revenue growth.The company's newer growth initiatives, including financial services and data centres, are also gaining traction, Vittal said. Airtel's investment in a strategic land parcel during the quarter is part of its ambition to build 1 GW of data centre capacity.He added that the company remained focused on maintaining a strong balance sheet, supported by robust cash generation and disciplined capital allocation.Bharti Airtel shares end lowerShares of Bharti Airtel ended Thursday's trading session 0.52% lower at Rs 2,056.90, compared with the previous close of Rs 2,067.60 on the NSE.During the session, the stock traded in a range of Rs 2,048-2,084.The telecom major's shares have declined nearly 3% so far this year. At the prevailing market price, Bharti Airtel had a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 12.84 lakh crore.
